sec06-card-sec06-F01.front: At least how many seconds ahead should you look in town, and how far is that at thirty miles per hour?
sec06-card-sec06-F01.expected_back: Look ahead at least twelve seconds, to the spot your vehicle will reach twelve seconds from now; at thirty miles per hour that is a little more than one block.

sec06-card-sec06-R01.front: How do you count-check your twelve-second look-ahead, and how far ahead should you scan at freeway speed?
sec06-card-sec06-R01.expected_back: To test your look-ahead, pick a fixed object in front, count one-thousand-one upward until your front bumper reaches it, and if you have not got to one-thousand-twelve, look farther; at freeway speeds look at least twenty to thirty seconds ahead.

sec06-card-sec06-F02.front: At forty miles per hour or less, what is the minimum following gap, and what do most instructors recommend?
sec06-card-sec06-F02.expected_back: If you drive forty miles per hour or less, keep at least two seconds behind the vehicle ahead; that is only the minimum, and most driving instructors recommend up to four seconds.

sec06-card-sec06-R02.front: How do you use a roadside object to test whether you are following at least two seconds back?
sec06-card-sec06-R02.expected_back: To test following distance, start counting when the rear of the car ahead passes a fixed point such as a sign; reaching that point before one-thousand-two means you are too close.

sec06-card-sec06-F03.front: Almost how many seconds does stopping from fifty-five miles per hour take even under ideal conditions?
sec06-card-sec06-F03.expected_back: Stopping from fifty-five miles per hour takes almost seven seconds even with perfect brakes and ideal roads, so leave more room at highway speeds and whenever roads are slippery or visibility is poor.

sec06-card-sec06-R03.front: How should you position yourself relative to traffic packs to keep room to maneuver?
sec06-card-sec06-R03.expected_back: Keep room to maneuver by adjusting speed and lane position so you sit between the clusters of vehicles ahead and behind, in the lane that leaves you the most escape options.

sec06-card-sec06-F04.front: In what exact left-right order should you look right before entering an intersection?
sec06-card-sec06-F04.expected_back: Just before entering an intersection, look left, then right, then left again.

sec06-card-sec06-F05.front: When is making a cell-phone voice call legal while driving in Nevada?
sec06-card-sec06-F05.expected_back: Holding a cell phone or other handheld wireless device for a voice call while driving is prohibited unless you use a hands-free accessory.

sec06-card-sec06-F06.front: Which non-voice handheld device actions are prohibited while driving in Nevada?
sec06-card-sec06-F06.expected_back: Using a handheld device by hand to text, send or read messages, search the Internet or otherwise communicate without voice is prohibited while driving.

sec06-card-sec06-F07.front: Under what exact condition may a Nevada driver use a handheld wireless device while moving?
sec06-card-sec06-F07.expected_back: You may use a handheld device to report an emergency when stopping the vehicle would be inadvisable, impractical or dangerous.

sec06-card-sec06-F08.front: What three steps should you take as soon as police lights flash behind you, especially at night?
sec06-card-sec06-F08.memory_hook: Pull clear, stay in, dome light
sec06-card-sec06-F08.expected_back: If police lights flash behind you, pull over as far out of the traffic lane as you can, stay inside the vehicle, and at night switch on the interior light.

sec06-card-sec06-F09.front: Where should your hands stay during a police stop, and when should you reach for your documents?
sec06-card-sec06-F09.expected_back: During a police stop, keep your hands where the officer can see them, ideally on the steering wheel, avoid sudden movements, and wait to be asked for your license, registration and proof of insurance.

sec06-card-sec06-R04.front: What category of violations causes most police traffic stops?
sec06-card-sec06-R04.expected_back: Moving violations such as speeding, running a light or sign, not signalling or leaving your marked lane are the most common reason police stop a vehicle, and drivers can break a law without knowing it.

sec06-card-sec06-R05.front: In what order do officers usually conduct a stop, and where is the proper place to contest a ticket?
sec06-card-sec06-R05.memory_hook: Give papers calmly, contest in court
sec06-card-sec06-R05.expected_back: Officers usually ask for identification first and explain the stop second; hand over the papers promptly and without argument, and contest a citation later by requesting a court hearing rather than arguing at the roadside.

sec06-card-sec06-F10.front: To whom must you yield when entering a roundabout, and which direction does all traffic circulate?
sec06-card-sec06-F10.expected_back: Drivers entering a roundabout must yield to the traffic already circulating in it, and all traffic travels around it counterclockwise.

sec06-card-sec06-F11.front: In a two-lane roundabout, which movements use the left lane and which use the right lane?
sec06-card-sec06-F11.expected_back: In a two-lane roundabout, use the left lane to turn left, make a U-turn or go straight, and the right lane to turn right or go straight.

sec06-card-sec06-F12.front: How fast should you drive inside a roundabout, and which signal do you switch on to exit?
sec06-card-sec06-F12.expected_back: Inside a roundabout, slow to the speed of the traffic already circulating, and switch on your right turn signal as you exit.

sec06-card-sec06-R06.front: Who is the raised concrete truck apron around a roundabout's center island built for, and what should cars do?
sec06-card-sec06-R06.memory_hook: Big trailers use apron, cars off
sec06-card-sec06-R06.expected_back: Large trucks and trailers may run their rear wheels over the raised truck apron around a roundabout's center island to manage the tight turn, but cars should stay off the apron.

sec06-card-sec06-R07.front: What two safe options do bicyclists have for navigating a roundabout?
sec06-card-sec06-R07.memory_hook: Take full lane or walk crosswalks
sec06-card-sec06-R07.expected_back: Cyclists comfortable in traffic may take the lane in a roundabout, yield when entering, keep to traffic speed and hand-signal when leaving, or else walk the bike through the crosswalks.

sec06-card-sec06-R08.front: Where must pedestrians cross at a roundabout, and where must they never step?
sec06-card-sec06-R08.expected_back: Pedestrians at a roundabout must stay in the marked crosswalks and never cross to the central island; they have the right-of-way but should still watch for cars.

sec06-card-sec06-F13.front: For which five everyday vehicle actions does Nevada law—not mere courtesy—require signaling?
sec06-card-sec06-F13.expected_back: Signalling before you turn, change lanes, slow down, stop or park is required by law, not just a courtesy.

sec06-card-sec06-F14.front: Using your left arm, how do you hand-signal a left turn, a right turn, and slowing or stopping?
sec06-card-sec06-F14.memory_hook: Straight left, up right, down stop
sec06-card-sec06-F14.expected_back: Hand signals: a left arm held straight out means a left turn, a left arm bent upward at about a right angle means a right turn, and a left arm pointed down with the palm facing back means slowing or stopping.

sec06-card-sec06-F15.front: How many feet ahead must you signal a turn on city streets versus on open Nevada highways?
sec06-card-sec06-F15.memory_hook: One hundred city, three hundred highway
sec06-card-sec06-F15.expected_back: On city streets, turn your signal on no less than one hundred feet (roughly ten car lengths) before the turn; on open highways make it three hundred feet (roughly thirty car lengths).

sec06-card-sec06-F16.front: Which lane do you use to turn right, and what is forbidden once inside a reserved right-turn lane?
sec06-card-sec06-F16.expected_back: For a right turn, be in the far right travel lane or a lane marked for right turns; a lane reserved for right turns may be entered only to turn right, never to drive straight through.

sec06-card-sec06-F17.front: How must your front wheels point while waiting to turn left, and which lanes connect on a two-way road?
sec06-card-sec06-F17.expected_back: For a left turn, keep the wheels pointed straight until you actually start turning, and on a two-way road turn from the lane just right of the center line into the nearest lane going your way.

sec06-card-sec06-R09.front: Which lane must you enter immediately after turning right, and when may you move to another lane?
sec06-card-sec06-R09.expected_back: After a right turn, enter the right-hand lane of the new road or the lane marked for the turn, and change lanes only after signalling once you are well clear of the intersection.

sec06-card-sec06-R10.front: What final checks belong right before turning, and what should you do once settled in the new lane?
sec06-card-sec06-R10.expected_back: Many crashes come from drivers making turns, so watch for pedestrians and bicyclists, look once more in each direction before turning, and cancel the signal after joining traffic.

sec06-card-sec06-F18.front: What are the mirror, signal, and blind-spot rules for changing lanes, and where must you never change lanes?
sec06-card-sec06-F18.expected_back: To change lanes, check the rear and side mirrors, signal at least one hundred feet ahead in the city or three hundred feet on highways and freeways, look over your shoulder at the blind spot, and never change lanes inside an intersection.

sec06-card-sec06-F19.front: Where are U-turns generally legal in Nevada, and from which lanes do you start them?
sec06-card-sec06-F19.expected_back: U-turns are generally legal on any Nevada road where they can be made safely; signal and make them from the far left lane or the center left-turn lane.

sec06-card-sec06-F20.front: When are U-turns legal across double yellow lines, at green signals, and on divided highways?
sec06-card-sec06-F20.expected_back: A U-turn is legal across a double yellow line when safe and legal, at an intersection on a green light or green arrow unless a No U-turn sign is posted, and on a divided highway only through an opening in the divider.

sec06-card-sec06-R12.front: What three center barriers on a divided highway may you never drive across for a U-turn?
sec06-card-sec06-R12.expected_back: On a divided highway a U-turn is allowed only through an opening in the center divider, never by crossing a dividing curb, strip of land or two sets of double yellow lines.

sec06-card-sec06-F21.front: At which four roadway locations or traffic conditions are U-turns flatly illegal?
sec06-card-sec06-F21.expected_back: U-turns are illegal on or at railroad tracks, on a one-way street, where a No U-turn sign is posted, or where other vehicles could hit you.

sec06-card-sec06-F22.front: How many feet of clear visibility in both directions are required when curves, hills, rain, or fog limit sight?
sec06-card-sec06-F22.memory_hook: Two hundred clear feet both ways
sec06-card-sec06-F22.expected_back: Never make a U-turn where a curve, hill, rain, fog or anything else keeps you from seeing two hundred feet clearly in each direction.

sec06-card-sec06-R13.front: Near a roadway grade, what visibility minimum applies to U-turns, and who else can ban them?
sec06-card-sec06-R13.expected_back: A U-turn is forbidden near a grade where visibility is under five hundred feet in both directions, and local authorities and the state transportation department may ban U-turns at any location they control.

sec06-card-sec06-F23.front: What buildings count inside a Nevada business district for U-turn rules, and where may you turn around there?
sec06-card-sec06-F23.expected_back: Never make a U-turn in a business district, which also covers areas with churches, apartments, multifamily housing and public buildings; there, turn only at an intersection or a provided opening.

sec06-card-sec06-R11.front: How does U-turn legality in a residential district compare with a business district?
sec06-card-sec06-R11.expected_back: U-turns are legal in a residential district when a traffic sign or signal protects you from approaching vehicles, but never in a business district except at an intersection or a provided opening.

sec06-card-sec06-F24.front: May you make a U-turn in front of a fire station or pull into its driveway to turn around?
sec06-card-sec06-F24.expected_back: Never make a U-turn in front of a fire station or use a fire station driveway to turn around.

sec06-card-sec06-F25.front: What two shortcuts are always illegal when passing another vehicle in Nevada?
sec06-card-sec06-F25.expected_back: Never go over the speed limit to pass, and never use the road shoulder to pass.

sec06-card-sec06-F26.front: Which three conditions must line up before passing on the left on a two-lane, two-way road?
sec06-card-sec06-F26.expected_back: On a two-lane road with opposing traffic, pass on the left only when you can see clearly ahead with no oncoming traffic close by, the broken yellow line is on your side, and it is safe.

sec06-card-sec06-F27.front: Within how many feet of a street intersection or railroad crossing—plus which other zones—is two-lane passing banned?
sec06-card-sec06-F27.memory_hook: Within one hundred feet, curves, hills
sec06-card-sec06-F27.expected_back: On a two-lane road, do not pass when nearing a curve or hilltop that hides the road ahead, at or within one hundred feet of a street or railroad crossing, where a double solid yellow line is painted, or where signs forbid it.

sec06-card-sec06-R14.front: How far ahead must you signal left before passing in business or residential areas versus elsewhere?
sec06-card-sec06-R14.memory_hook: One hundred town, three hundred open
sec06-card-sec06-R14.expected_back: When passing on a two-lane road, turn on the left signal one hundred feet ahead in business or residential areas and three hundred feet ahead elsewhere.

sec06-card-sec06-F28.front: When is it safe to pull back into your right-hand lane after overtaking a vehicle?
sec06-card-sec06-F28.expected_back: After passing, return to your lane once you can see the passed vehicle in your rear-view mirror.

sec06-card-sec06-F29.front: What two actions must you take when a driver behind you signals to pass?
sec06-card-sec06-F29.expected_back: When a vehicle behind you signals to pass, move right within your lane and let it go by, and never speed up while it is passing.

sec06-card-sec06-F30.front: Why must you never pass on the left of a vehicle making or signaling a left turn?
sec06-card-sec06-F30.expected_back: Never pass on the left of a driver who is making or signalling a left turn.

sec06-card-sec06-F31.front: On a highway with two lanes in your direction, when is driving below the speed limit in the far-left lane illegal?
sec06-card-sec06-F31.expected_back: On a highway with two lanes in your direction, it is illegal to drive the far left lane below the posted limit while a faster vehicle is coming up behind you in that lane.

sec06-card-sec06-R16.front: In which six situations does Nevada's slow-left-lane prohibition NOT apply?
sec06-card-sec06-R16.memory_hook: Cities, left turns, police, hazards, passing
sec06-card-sec06-R16.expected_back: The slow-left-lane rule does not apply inside a city or town, when preparing for a left turn, when police direct you there, for an emergency vehicle on duty, when conditions or hazards require it, or while overtaking.

sec06-card-sec06-F32.front: When is passing on the right allowed in Nevada, and what surface boundary may you never cross?
sec06-card-sec06-F32.expected_back: You may pass on the right only where the road is clearly marked for two or more lanes going your way and it is safe, and never if it would take you off the paved road.

sec06-card-sec06-R15.front: Why is passing on the right riskier even where marked multi-lane roads allow it?
sec06-card-sec06-R15.expected_back: On a multi-lane road you normally pass on the left where nothing forbids it, while passing on the right is allowed only on roads marked for two or more lanes your way and is risky because the other driver may not see you.

sec06-card-sec06-F33.front: What is Nevada's preferred lane rule when passing a cyclist, and what minimum clearance applies on a single lane?
sec06-card-sec06-F33.expected_back: To pass a cyclist, move into the next lane to the left if there is one going your way and it is reasonably safe; otherwise pass at a safe distance of at least three feet and do not move back right until clear.

sec06-card-sec06-F34.front: May motor vehicles drive along a marked bicycle lane in Nevada?
sec06-card-sec06-F34.expected_back: Driving in a marked bicycle lane is prohibited.

sec06-card-sec06-F35.front: What three steps belong every time you park and step out of your vehicle?
sec06-card-sec06-F35.memory_hook: Engine off, brake set, check door
sec06-card-sec06-F35.expected_back: When you park and leave the vehicle, turn off the engine and set the parking brake, and look for bicycles and other vehicles before opening your door.

sec06-card-sec06-F36.front: Which direction must a parked vehicle face, and within how many inches of the curb must both wheels sit?
sec06-card-sec06-F36.expected_back: Park facing the direction normal traffic flows, with the front and rear wheels within eighteen inches of the curb.

sec06-card-sec06-F37.front: From how many feet away in both directions must other drivers be able to see your parked vehicle?
sec06-card-sec06-F37.memory_hook: Visible two hundred feet both ways
sec06-card-sec06-F37.expected_back: Park where other drivers can see your vehicle from two hundred feet away (roughly twenty car lengths) in both directions.

sec06-card-sec06-F38.front: Why must you never twist the ignition key to the lock position while your vehicle is rolling?
sec06-card-sec06-F38.expected_back: Never turn the ignition to the lock position while the vehicle is moving, because the steering will lock when you turn the wheel and you will lose control.

sec06-card-sec06-F39.front: What parking rule does each painted curb color set—white, green, yellow, red, and blue?
sec06-card-sec06-F39.expected_back: Curb colors: white usually allows only a very short stop to load or unload passengers or drop mail, green allows parking for a limited time, yellow marks a loading zone, red means no stopping, standing or parking, and blue marks handicapped parking.

sec06-card-sec06-R17.front: Which visual clues warn that a curbside parked vehicle is about to pull out or open into your lane?
sec06-card-sec06-R17.expected_back: Signs that a parked car may pull out include a lit turn signal, white backup lights, red brake lights and exhaust from the tailpipe; also watch for opening doors and people stepping out between cars.

sec06-card-sec06-R18.front: If forced to stop along a highway, where should your wheels sit and when must warning lights shine?
sec06-card-sec06-R18.expected_back: If you must stop on a highway, get all four wheels well off the pavement if you can, leave room for others to pass, and use parking lights or four-way flashers in poor visibility or between sunset and sunrise.

sec06-card-sec06-R19.front: How should you align your car where no curb or markings exist, and what lights apply in emergency bays?
sec06-card-sec06-R19.expected_back: With no curb, barrier, sign or marking to guide you, park parallel to the road, and in highway or freeway emergency parking areas always use four-way flashers or parking lights.

sec06-card-sec06-R20.front: How long a space, side gap, bumper alignment, and initial wheel turn start right-side parallel parking?
sec06-card-sec06-R20.expected_back: For parallel parking on the right, choose a space about five feet longer than your car, pull up beside the car ahead of it about two or three feet away with rear bumpers lined up, then back slowly with the wheel turned fully right.

sec06-card-sec06-R21.front: What landmark cue tells you to straighten your wheels while parallel parking, and what goes wrong too late or overdone?
sec06-card-sec06-R21.expected_back: Once the back of your front seat lines up with the other car's rear bumper, steer smoothly left to straighten; not straightening makes the right rear wheel hit the curb, and over-steering left can bring the right front fender into that car.

sec06-card-sec06-R22.front: At what curb distance, gear setting, and brake step do you finish parallel parking?
sec06-card-sec06-R22.expected_back: Finish parallel parking about eighteen inches from the curb, then shift to park in an automatic or to first gear or reverse in a manual, and set the parking brake.

sec06-card-sec06-F40.front: What core goal governs aiming your front tires when parking on any hill?
sec06-card-sec06-F40.expected_back: When parking on a hill, aim the front tires so a rolling car moves into the curb or away from traffic: downhill toward the curb or shoulder, uphill with a curb away from it, uphill without a curb toward the shoulder, and always set the parking brake.

sec06-card-sec06-R23.front: Across downhill, uphill without a curb, and uphill with a curb, which is the only case where tires turn away?
sec06-card-sec06-R23.memory_hook: Only uphill with curb turns left
sec06-card-sec06-R23.expected_back: Downhill tires turn toward the curb or shoulder, and uphill without a curb they also turn toward the shoulder; only uphill with a curb do the tires turn away from it.

sec06-card-sec06-F41.front: How far from a fire hydrant must you stay where parallel parking is allowed versus angle parking?
sec06-card-sec06-F41.expected_back: Do not park within fifteen feet of a fire hydrant where parallel parking is allowed, or within twenty feet of one where angle parking is allowed.

sec06-card-sec06-F42.front: Within how many feet of a crosswalk or of a highway roadside traffic signal is parking prohibited?
sec06-card-sec06-F42.expected_back: Do not park on a crosswalk or within twenty feet of one, or within thirty feet of a roadside traffic signal on a highway.

sec06-card-sec06-F43.front: How far must you park from a fire-station driveway on the same side versus the opposite side?
sec06-card-sec06-F43.expected_back: Do not park within twenty feet of a fire station driveway entrance, or within seventy-five feet of that entrance on the opposite side of the highway.

sec06-card-sec06-R25.front: How do Nevada's fifteen-, twenty-, and thirty-foot parking buffers line up across hydrants, crosswalks, and signals?
sec06-card-sec06-R25.memory_hook: Fifteen parallel, twenty angle-crosswalk, thirty signal
sec06-card-sec06-R25.expected_back: Fire hydrant clearance is fifteen feet for parallel parking but twenty feet for angle parking, and a crosswalk needs twenty feet while a roadside traffic signal needs thirty feet.

sec06-card-sec06-R24.front: At which seven street, structure, or lane locations is non-emergency parking never allowed?
sec06-card-sec06-R24.expected_back: No parking is allowed on a sidewalk, in front of a driveway, inside an intersection, next to or opposite a highway construction zone, beside an already parked vehicle, on a bridge or in a tunnel, or in a bicycle lane unless your vehicle is disabled.

sec06-card-sec06-F44.front: Who must be in the vehicle to use an accessible parking space, and what is Nevada's minimum fine for violators?
sec06-card-sec06-F44.expected_back: Parking in a space marked with the international symbol of access is allowed only when the person issued the valid disabled placard or plate is driving or riding in the vehicle, and the minimum fine for anyone else is two hundred fifty dollars.

sec06-card-sec06-R27.front: Why are placard holders asked to spare accessible stalls that have striped loading zones when possible?
sec06-card-sec06-R27.expected_back: Placard holders are asked to be mindful of accessible spaces with loading zones, which people needing lifts may require, and to use those spaces as little as possible.

sec06-card-sec06-R26.front: What should you do if your car breaks down on a freeway, and why shouldn't you walk down the highway?
sec06-card-sec06-R26.expected_back: If your car breaks down, move to the shoulder or emergency area as soon as it is safe, turn on four-way flashers, and stay in or near the car on the side away from traffic, since walking on a freeway is dangerous and a trooper will stop to help.

sec12-card-sec12-F01.front: How does alcohol impair your brain and coordination, and how much does crash risk jump past point zero eight?
sec12-card-sec12-F01.expected_back: Alcohol slows brain function, affects how you process information and delays hand-eye coordination, and driving above the point zero eight legal limit raises crash risk from five times to as much as thirty times.

sec12-card-sec12-F02.front: Do impaired-driving dangers come only from street drugs, or from legal prescriptions and over-the-counter medicine too?
sec12-card-sec12-F02.expected_back: Both medical drugs and illegal or prescription-controlled drugs can seriously harm motor skills and the ability to think and react, so do not drive under their influence.

sec12-card-sec12-F03.front: Even though recreational cannabis is legal in Nevada, what blood nanogram cutoffs make driving or physical control unlawful?
sec12-card-sec12-F03.expected_back: Although marijuana is legal in Nevada, it is unlawful to drive or be in actual physical control of a vehicle with more than two nanograms of marijuana per milliliter of blood, or five nanograms of marijuana metabolite.

sec12-card-sec12-R03.front: What roadway-death share in two thousand sixteen and injury-crash total from twenty-twelve to twenty-fifteen does the handbook cite?
sec12-card-sec12-R03.expected_back: The handbook reports that in two thousand sixteen alcohol-related crashes were a factor in over thirty-one percent of Nevada roadway deaths, and that from two thousand twelve to two thousand fifteen alcohol and drugs contributed to four thousand six hundred fifty-one injury crashes in the state.

sec12-card-sec12-R12.front: How many people died—and what percentage of all Nevada traffic deaths did alcohol cause—in two thousand nineteen?
sec12-card-sec12-R12.expected_back: The handbook notes that in two thousand nineteen, one hundred twenty-nine people died in alcohol-related crashes in Nevada, forty-two percent of all traffic deaths.

sec12-card-sec12-F04.front: Which two separate penalty tracks hit a driver under Nevada impaired-driving law?
sec12-card-sec12-F04.expected_back: Nevada DUI law has two kinds of penalties: administrative action by the DMV, taken regardless of what the court finds, and criminal action by the courts.

sec12-card-sec12-R04.front: How does an administrative impaired-driving penalty differ from a criminal penalty?
sec12-card-sec12-R04.expected_back: An administrative penalty is the DMV's action and stands regardless of the court's findings, while a criminal penalty is imposed by the court.

sec12-card-sec12-F05.front: What tests can an officer require under Implied Consent, and what if you refuse on a first offense?
sec12-card-sec12-F05.expected_back: Under the Implied Consent Law, a driver an officer suspects of DUI will be asked to take a blood, breath or urine test, and an officer may order a blood draw even on a first offense.

sec12-card-sec12-F06.front: How long is your driving privilege revoked for a first test refusal versus a second refusal inside seven years?
sec12-card-sec12-F06.expected_back: Refusing the officer-directed tests revokes your driving privilege, with no eligibility for one year on a first refusal or three years if your privilege was revoked for refusal in the prior seven years (NRS 484C point two two zero).

sec12-card-sec12-F07.front: Which chemical test findings automatically revoke your privilege under Nevada's Illegal Per Se Law?
sec12-card-sec12-F07.expected_back: Under the Illegal Per Se Law, a chemical test showing point zero eight percent alcohol concentration or more, or any detectable amount of a controlled substance, revokes your driving privilege.

sec12-card-sec12-R01.front: How does Implied Consent differ from Illegal Per Se in what triggers revocation?
sec12-card-sec12-R01.expected_back: Implied consent is about refusing a test, which brings revocation for refusal, while illegal per se is about the test result itself, which brings revocation at point zero eight percent or with any detectable controlled substance.

sec12-card-sec12-F08.front: What alcohol concentration triggers administrative license loss for a driver under twenty-one?
sec12-card-sec12-F08.expected_back: A driver under twenty-one whose test shows an alcohol concentration of point zero two percent or more but under point zero eight percent loses the driving privilege administratively, and the officer can take the license on the spot.

sec12-card-sec12-R02.front: How does the per se alcohol cutoff for adults twenty-one and up compare with drivers under twenty-one?
sec12-card-sec12-R02.expected_back: The adult per se level is point zero eight percent alcohol concentration, while drivers under twenty-one face action starting at point zero two percent.

sec12-card-sec12-F09.front: Does blowing below point zero eight percent guarantee you cannot be arrested and convicted of impaired driving?
sec12-card-sec12-F09.expected_back: The point zero eight percent level is only a guide, and you can be arrested and convicted of DUI at a lower alcohol concentration.

sec12-card-sec12-F10.front: What procedural right can you request through the state licensing agency whenever you lose your license?
sec12-card-sec12-F10.expected_back: Whenever you lose your license, you can request an administrative hearing through the DMV.

sec12-card-sec12-F12.front: At what alcohol concentration does administrative per se action kick in for a commercial license holder?
sec12-card-sec12-F12.expected_back: For a commercial driver license holder, the administrative per se level starts at point zero four percent alcohol concentration.

sec12-card-sec12-R08.front: How strictly does alcohol affect commercial license holders, and how severe can repeat penalties get?
sec12-card-sec12-R08.expected_back: For commercial driver license holders, any detectable alcohol can affect the driving privilege, and DUI penalties are harsher, including lifetime disqualification from commercial driving.

sec12-card-sec12-F11.front: How many days does an administrative illegal per se revocation last, and what else can follow?
sec12-card-sec12-F11.expected_back: An administrative illegal per se action for point zero eight percent or a detectable controlled substance revokes the driver license for one hundred eighty-five days, may require an SR-twenty-two, and may be followed by criminal penalties.

sec12-card-sec12-F13.front: How long is a driver under twenty-one revoked on the penalty chart at point zero two percent alcohol?
sec12-card-sec12-F13.expected_back: On the penalty page, drivers under twenty-one at point zero two percent alcohol concentration also have the license revoked for one hundred eighty-five days, may need an SR-twenty-two, and may face criminal penalties.

sec12-card-sec12-F14.front: What revocation, jail-or-service, and fine ranges hit on a first impaired-driving conviction?
sec12-card-sec12-F14.expected_back: A first DUI conviction brings license revocation for at least one hundred eighty-five days, two days to six months in jail or forty-eight to ninety-six hours of community service, and a fine of four hundred dollars to one thousand dollars.

sec12-card-sec12-F15.front: What class fee and possible treatment order apply to a first impaired-driving offender?
sec12-card-sec12-F15.expected_back: A first DUI offender also pays DUI school tuition, averaging about one hundred fifty dollars, and may be ordered into treatment when the blood or breath alcohol was point zero eight percent or more.

sec12-card-sec12-R09.front: Can days already served under administrative revocation count toward a first criminal revocation?
sec12-card-sec12-R09.expected_back: With a first DUI conviction, the judge may count time already served under the administrative revocation toward the minimum one hundred eighty-five-day criminal revocation.

sec12-card-sec12-F16.front: What revocation, jail, fine, and service penalties hit for a second conviction within seven years?
sec12-card-sec12-F16.expected_back: A second DUI within seven years brings a one-year revocation, ten days to six months in jail or residential confinement, a seven hundred fifty dollars to one thousand dollars fine and one hundred to two hundred hours of community service.

sec12-card-sec12-R05.front: How do custody and community-service minimums compare between a first offense and a second within seven years?
sec12-card-sec12-R05.expected_back: A first DUI carries jail of two days up to six months, with forty-eight to ninety-six hours of community service as the alternative, while a second DUI within seven years brings ten days to six months plus one hundred to two hundred hours of community service.

sec12-card-sec12-R07.front: Beyond jail and fines, what plate and supervision consequences can accompany a second conviction inside seven years?
sec12-card-sec12-R07.expected_back: A second DUI within seven years can bring possible registration suspension and an order for treatment or clinical supervision by a treatment facility for up to one year.

sec12-card-sec12-F17.front: What revocation, state prison term, fine, and treatment minimum apply to a third offense within seven years?
sec12-card-sec12-F17.expected_back: A third or later DUI within seven years brings a three-year revocation, one to six years in prison and a two thousand dollars to five thousand dollars fine, plus possible registration suspension and at least three years of treatment if ordered.

sec12-card-sec12-F18.front: What revocation, prison sentence, and fine hit when impaired driving causes death or serious bodily harm?
sec12-card-sec12-F18.expected_back: A DUI that causes death or serious injury brings a three-year revocation, two to twenty years in prison and a fine of two thousand dollars to five thousand dollars.

sec12-card-sec12-R06.front: How do minimum and maximum impaired-driving fines climb across first, second, and third or injury offenses?
sec12-card-sec12-R06.expected_back: Fines rise with each DUI: four hundred dollars to one thousand dollars for a first, seven hundred fifty dollars to one thousand dollars for a second within seven years, and two thousand dollars to five thousand dollars for a later offense or one causing death or serious injury.

sec12-card-sec12-F19.front: How can an impaired-driving offender regain restricted driving privileges right away, and who pays?
sec12-card-sec12-F19.expected_back: A DUI offender's driving privilege can be reinstated immediately if issued a license with an ignition interlock restriction and an interlock device is installed, at the driver's own expense, in every vehicle they drive.

sec12-card-sec12-F20.front: How long does a licensed driver under eighteen lose their license if juvenile court finds impaired driving?
sec12-card-sec12-F20.expected_back: A licensed driver under eighteen whom juvenile court finds drove under the influence of alcohol or a controlled substance loses the license for one hundred eighty-five days.

sec12-card-sec12-R10.front: How do revocation length and ignition-interlock reinstatement options for minors compare with adults?
sec12-card-sec12-R10.expected_back: Young drivers face the same one hundred eighty-five-day revocation period and the same reinstatement options, including ignition interlock, as drivers over the age of eighteen.

sec12-card-sec12-F21.front: Which underage impaired drivers must complete a substance-abuse evaluation before a judge decides on treatment?
sec12-card-sec12-F21.expected_back: Drivers under eighteen found to have driven under the influence by juvenile court, and drivers under twenty-one convicted of DUI, must undergo an alcohol or drug abuse evaluation, and the judge may order treatment.

sec12-card-sec12-F22.front: Where are open alcoholic drinks banned in a moving vehicle, and which three passenger spaces are exempt?
sec12-card-sec12-F22.memory_hook: Banned in cabins; campers, buses, limos
sec12-card-sec12-F22.expected_back: Nevada's open container law bans opened alcoholic beverages in the driver and passenger areas of a moving vehicle, except in motor home or house trailer living quarters and the passenger areas of commercial buses, limousines and taxis.

sec12-card-sec12-F23.front: How does a Nevada court treat an impaired-driving case when a child under fifteen was riding inside?
sec12-card-sec12-F23.expected_back: Having passengers under fifteen in the vehicle during a DUI is treated by the court as an aggravating factor in sentencing.

sec12-card-sec12-F24.front: What extra dollar fee gets tacked onto an impaired-driving conviction or plea when a chemical test was run?
sec12-card-sec12-F24.expected_back: A DUI conviction or guilty plea where a chemical test was done adds a sixty dollars fine to cover the cost of the analysis.

sec12-card-sec12-F25.front: Which five lane-keeping and steering mistakes warn you another driver on the road may be impaired?
sec12-card-sec12-F25.expected_back: Clues of an impaired driver include turning too widely, straddling the center line or lane markers, weaving or drifting, nearly hitting things, and driving into oncoming traffic.

sec12-card-sec12-F26.front: Which speed, braking, reaction, and nighttime-headlight behaviors point to an impaired driver?
sec12-card-sec12-F26.expected_back: More impairment clues: driving far too slowly, stopping in traffic for no reason, erratic or jerky braking, slow responses to signals, sudden speed changes, abrupt or illegal turns, and driving at night with headlights off.

sec12-card-sec12-R11.front: Which tailgating, multi-lane, turn-lane, and overcorrection clues also warn of an impaired motorist?
sec12-card-sec12-R11.expected_back: Following too closely, using two lanes, drifting off the road or straight through turn lanes, and swerving to correct course are also listed as clues to an impaired driver.

sec12-card-sec12-F28.front: Does a suspended or revoked Nevada license ever turn valid automatically when time runs out?
sec12-card-sec12-F28.expected_back: A suspended or revoked license is never reinstated automatically; you must reapply at a DMV office, present name, birth date and Social Security documents, meet any other requirements and pay reinstatement fees.

sec12-card-sec12-R13.front: Beyond reapplying with documents and fees, how can certain juvenile offenses affect unissued teen licenses?
sec12-card-sec12-R13.expected_back: Licenses lost to suspension or revocation require reapplying, documents, any other requirements and fees, and license issuance may be delayed for some juvenile offenses.

sec12-card-sec12-F29.front: Which three major on-road grounds suspend or revoke a Nevada license?
sec12-card-sec12-F29.memory_hook: Twelve points, impaired driving, walker-bike hits
sec12-card-sec12-F29.expected_back: A license can be suspended or revoked for twelve or more demerit points in twelve months, for DUI by test result or conviction, and for causing a collision with a pedestrian or bicyclist.

sec12-card-sec12-F30.front: What happens to your driving privilege if you ignore a required traffic-ticket court appearance?
sec12-card-sec12-F30.expected_back: Failing to appear in court as required after a traffic ticket can cost you your license.

sec12-card-sec12-F31.front: What dual penalty hits if you crash without insurance and damage or injury exceeds seven hundred fifty dollars?
sec12-card-sec12-F31.expected_back: If you have no liability insurance and a crash causes more than seven hundred fifty dollars in personal injury or property damage, both your driver license and your vehicle registration are suspended.

sec12-card-sec12-F32.front: Which three insurance-maintenance failures trigger a license or registration suspension?
sec12-card-sec12-F32.memory_hook: Missing proof, uninsured conviction, repeat lapses
sec12-card-sec12-F32.expected_back: Failure to maintain insurance leads to suspension when a required proof of financial responsibility is not provided, after a conviction for no insurance, or after repeated coverage lapses.

sec12-card-sec12-F33.front: Which three court, vandalism, or exhibition offenses can cost your Nevada license?
sec12-card-sec12-F33.expected_back: Owing overdue court-ordered child support, a graffiti conviction, and organizing or joining street racing or trick-driving displays can each cost a person the license.

sec12-card-sec12-R14.front: Who is covered—and on which properties—under Nevada's street-racing and trick-driving suspension law?
sec12-card-sec12-R14.memory_hook: Drivers and organizers; streets, public lots
sec12-card-sec12-R14.expected_back: The street racing and trick driving ground covers both taking part in and organizing an unauthorized speed contest or trick display, whether on a public highway or on premises the public can access.

sec12-card-sec12-F34.front: Which weapon, alcohol, and drug offenses can strip a juvenile's Nevada driver license?
sec12-card-sec12-F34.expected_back: Juveniles can lose the license for certain firearms offenses and for buying, drinking or possessing alcohol or using, possessing, selling or distributing controlled substances.

sec05-card-sec05-F01.front: What is the number-one cause of crashes in Nevada, and which three qualities do yielding rules depend on?
sec05-card-sec05-F01.expected_back: Not yielding when required is the top cause of crashes in Nevada, and the yielding rules depend on courtesy, common sense and cooperation.

sec05-card-sec05-F02.front: Does Nevada law ever grant someone automatic right-of-way, and what duty stays on the driver who may go first?
sec05-card-sec05-F02.expected_back: Nevada law does not hand anyone the right-of-way; it only says who has to yield, and even a driver who legally may go first must do everything possible to avoid a crash.

sec05-card-sec05-F03.front: At a Nevada intersection with no signs or signals, which vehicle should usually proceed first?
sec05-card-sec05-F03.expected_back: At an intersection with no signs or signals, the vehicle on your right should usually go first.

sec05-card-sec05-F04.front: Between a vehicle already inside the intersection and one just arriving, which goes first?
sec05-card-sec05-F04.expected_back: A vehicle that is already in the intersection goes before vehicles that are only now arriving.

sec05-card-sec05-F05.front: Who holds priority between a straight-through vehicle already in the intersection and a left-turning vehicle, and when may the left-turner go?
sec05-card-sec05-F05.expected_back: A vehicle going straight that is already in the intersection has priority over a vehicle turning left; the left-turner may go once it has yielded and signalled.

sec05-card-sec05-F06.front: To whom must you yield when pulling onto a main road from a minor street, private road, or driveway?
sec05-card-sec05-F06.expected_back: Drivers coming onto a main road from a minor road, a private road or a driveway must yield to all traffic on the main road and to pedestrians.

sec05-card-sec05-R02.front: How do the yield duties pair up for a left-turning intersection driver and a driver exiting a driveway?
sec05-card-sec05-R02.expected_back: A left-turning driver yields to straight-through traffic already in the intersection, and a driver leaving a driveway or private road yields to everything on the main road, pedestrians included.

sec05-card-sec05-F07.front: What must you do immediately when an emergency vehicle with flashing lights or a siren approaches from any direction?
sec05-card-sec05-F07.expected_back: When an emergency vehicle using its siren or flashing lights approaches from any direction, pull over at once to the right edge, staying out of any intersection, and wait stopped until it goes by.

sec05-card-sec05-F08.front: Who goes first at a Nevada four-way stop, and what must that driver still do before moving?
sec05-card-sec05-F08.expected_back: At a four-way stop, the driver who reached the intersection first goes first, after a complete stop.

sec05-card-sec05-R01.front: How does priority at an uncontrolled intersection differ from priority at a four-way stop?
sec05-card-sec05-R01.expected_back: At an uncontrolled intersection the vehicle on the right usually goes first, but at a four-way stop the order is set by who arrived and stopped first.

sec05-card-sec05-F09.front: Who must yield when entering a freeway from an on-ramp?
sec05-card-sec05-F09.expected_back: When joining a freeway, yield to the traffic already on it and enter only when it is safe.

sec05-card-sec05-F10.front: What is your duty toward bicyclists riding inside a bike lane or along a bike path?
sec05-card-sec05-F10.expected_back: Yield to bicyclists riding in a bike lane or on a bike path.

sec05-card-sec05-F11.front: How must Nevada drivers treat a funeral procession traveling with headlights switched on?
sec05-card-sec05-F11.expected_back: Yield to a funeral procession and let the vehicles with their headlights on pass together as one group.

sec05-card-sec05-F12.front: Who holds priority at crosswalks and intersections, and what precaution should pedestrians still take before stepping off?
sec05-card-sec05-F12.expected_back: Vehicles must give way to pedestrians in crosswalks and at intersections, yet before stepping off the curb they should make sure cars in both directions have stopped.

sec05-card-sec05-F13.front: What must you do when a blind or visually impaired pedestrian approaches with a guide animal or white cane?
sec05-card-sec05-F13.expected_back: A blind or visually impaired person on foot who uses a guide dog or other service animal, or carries a white cane or walking stick, has the right-of-way; drivers must yield, stop fully if needed and take care before going on (NRS 484B point two nine zero).

sec05-card-sec05-F14.front: Beyond posted signs, which road, traffic, visibility, and terrain factors must you weigh under Nevada's Basic Rule?
sec05-card-sec05-F14.memory_hook: Match speed to road, weather, traffic
sec05-card-sec05-F14.expected_back: Nevada's Basic Rule requires a reasonable or proper speed: on top of any posted limit, weigh the amount and type of traffic, the weather and how far you can see, the road surface, and whether the road is flat or steep, straight or curvy, wide or narrow.

sec05-card-sec05-F15.front: How can your legally safe speed compare with the posted speed limit when conditions deteriorate?
sec05-card-sec05-F15.expected_back: Never drive at a speed that puts yourself or anyone else in danger; depending on conditions, the safe speed may be well below the posted limit.

sec05-card-sec05-R04.front: How does a posted speed limit sign interact with Nevada's Basic Rule?
sec05-card-sec05-R04.expected_back: The posted limit is the upper bound for normal conditions, while the Basic Rule can demand a much lower speed when traffic, weather, visibility or the road surface call for it.

sec05-card-sec05-F16.front: What example Nevada speed limits apply in school zones and in business or residential areas?
sec05-card-sec05-F16.expected_back: Example Nevada speed limits: fifteen miles per hour in school zones, and twenty-five miles per hour in business and residential areas and school zones.

sec05-card-sec05-F17.front: What example Nevada speed limits apply approaching towns, on urban freeways or rural highways, and on rural interstates?
sec05-card-sec05-F17.expected_back: Example Nevada speed limits: forty-five miles per hour in reduced-speed areas leading into towns, sixty-five miles per hour on urban freeways and rural highways, and seventy miles per hour or more on rural interstate freeways.

sec05-card-sec05-F18.front: Why must you drop below posted speed limits when bad weather cuts visibility or slicks pavement?
sec05-card-sec05-F18.expected_back: Posted limits are set for normal driving conditions, so when bad weather cuts visibility or makes the road slick, lower your speed.

sec05-card-sec05-F19.front: Where must slower traffic travel when two or more lanes run in the same direction?
sec05-card-sec05-F19.expected_back: Driving too slowly is unsafe too, and where two or more lanes run in the same direction, slower traffic must move right and let others pass.

sec05-card-sec05-F20.front: Over a five-mile stretch, how few seconds do you save driving seventy miles per hour instead of sixty?
sec05-card-sec05-F20.expected_back: Speeding saves very little time: over five miles, driving seventy miles per hour instead of sixty miles per hour saves only forty-three seconds.

sec05-card-sec05-R03.front: How much time does driving seventy instead of sixty save over fifteen miles, and what wipes out that gain?
sec05-card-sec05-R03.expected_back: Covering fifteen miles at seventy miles per hour rather than sixty miles per hour saves just two minutes and nine seconds, and a ticket costs both time and money.

sec05-card-sec05-F21.front: Which design features make freeways generally the safest roads per mile?
sec05-card-sec05-F21.expected_back: Freeways are usually the safest roads because access is limited, traffic flows one way without stopping, and drivers meet no intersections, signals, railroad crossings or sharp curves.

sec05-card-sec05-F22.front: Which four preparation checks should you handle before starting a freeway trip?
sec05-card-sec05-F22.expected_back: Before a freeway trip, plan the route, check a map if you are unsure of the way, know your entrances and exits, and check the gas gauge.

sec05-card-sec05-F23.front: How must you enter a freeway, and which two signs warn that you picked an exit ramp by mistake?
sec05-card-sec05-F23.expected_back: Enter a freeway by the on-ramp; Do Not Enter and Wrong Way signs tell a driver who has made a mistake.

sec05-card-sec05-F24.front: How should you use the freeway acceleration lane, and why should you avoid stopping before merging?
sec05-card-sec05-F24.expected_back: In the merge or acceleration lane, look for a gap, signal, and accelerate until you are close to the freeway's speed; avoid stopping before the merge unless it cannot be helped, because stopping makes a slow, dangerous entry into fast traffic.

sec05-card-sec05-R05.front: How do responsibilities differ between a driver merging onto a freeway and drivers already on it?
sec05-card-sec05-R05.expected_back: Merging drivers must yield to traffic already on the freeway, while drivers already on it should watch for merging cars and adjust speed so merges stay smooth.

sec05-card-sec05-F25.front: Why does freeway traffic often move briskly compared with surface highways of the same limit, and how should you pace yourself?
sec05-card-sec05-F25.expected_back: Freeway traffic often moves faster than traffic on other highways with the same posted limit because there are fewer stop-and-go situations, so keep with the flow.

sec05-card-sec05-F26.front: Who belongs in the far-left lane on a multi-lane freeway, and why should you skip weaving between lanes?
sec05-card-sec05-F26.expected_back: On multi-lane freeways leave the far-left lane for faster traffic; hopping between lanes is always dangerous, raises crash risk and seldom saves time.

sec05-card-sec05-F27.front: At least how many seconds ahead should you scan on a freeway, and what movements should you watch for?
sec05-card-sec05-F27.expected_back: On the freeway, look far down the road, at least twenty to thirty seconds ahead, and watch for drivers changing lanes, passing or slowing.

sec05-card-sec05-R06.front: Which four checks and signals belong before every freeway lane change?
sec05-card-sec05-R06.expected_back: Before any freeway lane change, check the mirrors and glance over your shoulder at the blind spot, use your turn signal, and watch for other drivers' signals.

sec05-card-sec05-F28.front: How do you use an on-ramp meter when its signal lights are operating?
sec05-card-sec05-F28.expected_back: When a ramp meter is switched on, pull up to the stop line and stop on red, expect it to change faster than an intersection signal, wait for green, then follow the ramp and merge safely.

sec05-card-sec05-R07.front: How should drivers use a multi-lane freeway on-ramp equipped with separate ramp meters?
sec05-card-sec05-R07.expected_back: On an on-ramp with more than one lane, each lane has its own meter, and drivers are encouraged to use both lanes and follow the meter for their own lane.

sec05-card-sec05-F29.front: How is an HOV bypass lane marked on a metered ramp, and who may roll past the meter without stopping?
sec05-card-sec05-F29.expected_back: Some HOV bypass lanes on metered ramps are marked with a diamond on the pavement and have no meter, so a carpool of two or more people may use them without stopping.

sec05-card-sec05-F30.front: What does an overhead freeway lane signal showing a downward green arrow with OPEN mean?
sec05-card-sec05-F30.expected_back: Lane-use signal: a green arrow pointing down with OPEN means you may drive the posted speed limit in the lane beneath it.

sec05-card-sec05-F31.front: How does an overhead yellow X with CAUTION differ from a yellow X with MERGE?
sec05-card-sec05-F31.expected_back: Lane-use signal: a yellow X with CAUTION means the lane may be used with care because of possible slow traffic or debris, while a yellow X with MERGE means the lane is ending.

sec05-card-sec05-F32.front: What must you do when an overhead lane-use signal displays a red X with CLOSED?
sec05-card-sec05-F32.expected_back: Lane-use signal: a red X with CLOSED means you may not drive in that lane and must merge safely into an open lane.

sec05-card-sec05-R08.front: What is the core usability difference between a yellow X lane signal and a red X lane signal?
sec05-card-sec05-R08.expected_back: A yellow X still lets you use the lane, with care for slow traffic or debris or to prepare to merge out, whereas a red X closes the lane entirely.

sec05-card-sec05-R09.front: How do overhead freeway gantry signs guide you before, near, and past a crash or work zone?
sec05-card-sec05-R09.expected_back: Overhead freeway signals show reduced speed limits and lane closures for construction, debris or crashes, update as you get closer, and show the lanes open again after the incident.

sec05-card-sec05-F33.front: How many occupants do Nevada HOV lanes require, where are active hours listed, and which two vehicle types are exempt?
sec05-card-sec05-F33.expected_back: HOV lanes require two or more persons per vehicle, their hours vary by segment as shown on regulatory signs, and motorcycles and emergency vehicles answering an emergency may use them.

sec05-card-sec05-F34.front: Which two categories of multi-axle or towing vehicles are barred from Nevada HOV lanes?
sec05-card-sec05-F34.expected_back: Vehicles with more than two axles, and vehicle-and-trailer combinations, are not allowed in HOV lanes.

sec05-card-sec05-F35.front: Where may you legally cross into or out of a Nevada carpool lane, and what white line forbids crossing?
sec05-card-sec05-F35.expected_back: A double solid white line beside a carpool lane may not be crossed; enter or leave the carpool lane only where the line is broken white.

sec05-card-sec05-R10.front: Which three transportation goals are HOV lanes built to achieve?
sec05-card-sec05-R10.expected_back: HOV lanes exist to reward ridesharing and public transit, take congestion out of the regular lanes and improve overall traffic flow.

sec05-card-sec05-F36.front: Where should you begin slowing down when exiting a freeway, and to what target speed?
sec05-card-sec05-F36.expected_back: To leave a freeway, do not slow on the main lanes; wait until you are in the deceleration lane, then slow gradually to the posted exit-ramp speed.

sec05-card-sec05-F37.front: How far ahead of your freeway exit should you signal and move into the proper exit lane?
sec05-card-sec05-F37.expected_back: Signal and move into the correct lane a mile or more before your exit.

sec05-card-sec05-R11.front: How does Nevada's freeway exit numbering system help you prepare to leave?
sec05-card-sec05-R11.expected_back: Most freeway exits are numbered, and the same numbers usually appear on the major freeway signs, which helps you spot your exit early.

sec05-card-sec05-F38.front: What must you do—and never do—if you accidentally pass your freeway exit?
sec05-card-sec05-F38.expected_back: If you miss your exit, never turn around or back up; drive to the next exit, return in the opposite direction and take the exit from there.

sec05-card-sec05-F39.front: How do you make an emergency stop with four-wheel anti-lock brakes, and why?
sec05-card-sec05-F39.expected_back: With four-wheel anti-lock brakes, push the brake pedal down hard, hold it there firmly and steer where you want to go, because ABS pumps the brakes far faster than any driver could.

sec05-card-sec05-F40.front: What does it mean if the dashboard ABS warning light stays illuminated long after starting the engine?
sec05-card-sec05-F40.expected_back: If the ABS symbol stays lit long after the engine starts, the ABS is not working, but the conventional brakes still work.

sec05-card-sec05-F41.front: What pedal habit switches off anti-lock braking right in the middle of an emergency stop?
sec05-card-sec05-F41.expected_back: Pumping the brakes or letting off steady pedal pressure disengages the ABS.

sec05-card-sec05-R12.front: Which three ways can tell you whether an unfamiliar vehicle is equipped with anti-lock brakes?
sec05-card-sec05-R12.expected_back: You can tell whether a car has ABS from a lit ABS symbol on the dashboard just after starting the engine, from the owner's manual, or by asking the dealer.

sec05-card-sec05-R13.front: Why must you steer smoothly rather than jerking the wheel during an anti-lock brake stop?
sec05-card-sec05-R13.expected_back: During ABS braking, do not jerk or crank the steering wheel hard, since that can send the vehicle onto the shoulder or emergency lane; steer back into your lane once the hazard is clear.

sec05-card-sec05-R14.front: How does rear-wheel ABS on some light trucks differ from four-wheel ABS if the front tires lock?
sec05-card-sec05-R14.expected_back: Four-wheel ABS keeps every wheel from locking, while rear-wheel ABS, found only on some light trucks, protects just the rear wheels; if the front wheels lock, ease off the pedal until they roll again.

sec05-card-sec05-F42.front: Which type of collision happens more often than any other on Nevada streets and highways?
sec05-card-sec05-F42.expected_back: The rear-end collision is the most common crash type on Nevada's streets and highways.

sec05-card-sec05-R15.front: Which vehicle, driver, and environmental factors determine total stopping distance?
sec05-card-sec05-R15.expected_back: Stopping distance depends on vehicle type and weight, speed, tire and brake condition, road surface, reaction time, alertness or fatigue, and the weather.

sec05-card-sec05-R16.front: How do perception and reaction work together before physical braking even starts?
sec05-card-sec05-R16.expected_back: Perception is seeing and understanding why you must stop, reaction is the brain telling the foot to brake; together with moving the foot they make up perception and reaction distance.

sec05-card-sec05-F44.front: What do highway safety studies give as normal reaction time, and what makes it longer?
sec05-card-sec05-F44.expected_back: Highway safety studies put normal reaction time at two to two point five seconds, and it grows when decisions get complex or something unexpected happens.

sec05-card-sec05-R17.front: What is the exact difference between braking time and braking distance?
sec05-card-sec05-R17.expected_back: Braking time is how long the brakes and tire-road friction need to stop the vehicle, while braking distance is how far it travels during that time.

sec05-card-sec05-F43.front: When you double your driving speed—say from thirty to sixty—how much longer does braking distance become?
sec05-card-sec05-F43.expected_back: Doubling your speed, for example from thirty miles per hour to sixty miles per hour, makes the braking distance four times as long, not twice as long.

sec05-card-sec05-R18.front: How much can wet pavement increase stopping distance, and why is a season's first rain extra slick?
sec05-card-sec05-R18.expected_back: On a wet road stopping distance can be more than double the dry figure, and the first rain of a season is especially dangerous because oil mixes with water on the pavement.

sec05-card-sec05-F45.front: Between what speeds do most cars begin losing traction and hydroplaning in heavy rain?
sec05-card-sec05-F45.expected_back: In heavy rain most cars start to lose traction and hydroplane at speeds between thirty-five and fifty-five miles per hour, so slow down.

sec05-card-sec05-R19.front: At just thirty miles per hour on ice, how many feet does stopping take?
sec05-card-sec05-R19.expected_back: At thirty miles per hour on ice the stopping distance would be three hundred seventy-three feet, more than the length of a football field.

sec05-card-sec05-R20.front: On dry level pavement at twenty-five miles per hour, what is total stopping distance and its perception-reaction versus braking split?
sec05-card-sec05-R20.expected_back: For a typical car on dry, level pavement with a two point five second reaction time, stopping from twenty-five miles per hour takes about one hundred twenty-seven feet in all: ninety-two feet of perception and reaction plus thirty-five feet of braking.

sec05-card-sec05-R21.front: In the dry-pavement table at forty-five miles per hour, what is total stopping distance and its two parts?
sec05-card-sec05-R21.memory_hook: Two seventy-eight total, one sixty-five reaction
sec05-card-sec05-R21.expected_back: In the same table, stopping from forty-five miles per hour takes about two hundred seventy-eight feet in all, made up of one hundred sixty-five feet of perception and reaction distance and one hundred thirteen feet of braking distance.

sec07-card-sec07-F01.front: Which driving tasks do advanced driver assistance systems help with, and what can they NOT do?
sec07-card-sec07-F01.expected_back: Advanced driver assistance systems help with tasks such as staying in the lane, avoiding crashes, covering blind spots and keeping a space cushion, but they do not drive the vehicle by themselves.

sec07-card-sec07-F02.front: Which three sensory alerts do vehicle warning systems use, and what two problems do they warn about?
sec07-card-sec07-F02.expected_back: Vehicle warning systems alert the driver by sound, light or vibration that a crash is about to happen or that something has malfunctioned.

sec07-card-sec07-F03.front: What does it mean that most vehicle warning systems are passive?
sec07-card-sec07-F03.expected_back: Most warning systems are passive: they warn of a possible problem but do not stop the crash themselves, so the driver may still have to act.

sec07-card-sec07-R01.front: What is the primary job of vehicle warning technologies?
sec07-card-sec07-R01.expected_back: Warning technologies exist mainly to alert the driver in specific situations, whether a crash is near or a part of the vehicle is malfunctioning.

sec07-card-sec07-F04.front: When does a back-up warning activate, how does it alert you, and what checks must you still perform?
sec07-card-sec07-F04.expected_back: A back-up warning uses sensors behind the vehicle once you shift into reverse and alerts you by sound, vibration or both, yet you must still check mirrors, look over your shoulder and use any camera while backing.

sec07-card-sec07-F05.front: How does a blind-spot monitor alert you—especially when signaling—and what must you still do before changing lanes?
sec07-card-sec07-F05.expected_back: A blind spot monitor warns of vehicles in your blind spots with a symbol, sound or vibration, sometimes more strongly when you signal, but you must still check mirrors and look over your shoulder before a lane change.

sec07-card-sec07-F06.front: When does a rear camera switch on, and does its video view replace mirror and shoulder checks?
sec07-card-sec07-F06.expected_back: A rear camera turns on when you shift into reverse to show the area behind the vehicle, but it does not replace mirror and over-the-shoulder checks while backing.

sec07-card-sec07-R02.front: Where inside different vehicles might the rear-camera video feed appear?
sec07-card-sec07-R02.expected_back: Depending on the vehicle, the rear camera picture may show up in the rearview mirror, the sun visor, the center console screen or another spot.

sec07-card-sec07-F07.front: When does a sideview camera show an enlarged lane view, and how should you pair it?
sec07-card-sec07-F07.expected_back: A sideview camera shows an enlarged video view of the lane beside you when you signal or switch it on, works much like a blind spot monitor, and should be used together with mirrors and head checks.

sec07-card-sec07-R03.front: What exterior hardware do some newer vehicles replace with sideview cameras?
sec07-card-sec07-R03.expected_back: Some newer vehicles use sideview cameras instead of traditional side mirrors.

sec07-card-sec07-F08.front: How does a surround-view monitor help during parking, and what habits remain required?
sec07-card-sec07-F08.expected_back: A surround-view or around-view monitor helps with parking by showing a virtual bird's-eye view of the vehicle and nearby curbs, markings and cars, and it too should be used along with mirrors and head checks.

sec07-card-sec07-R04.front: Where are the cameras mounted in most surround-view systems, and what extra alert do some include?
sec07-card-sec07-R04.expected_back: In most surround-view systems one camera sits in the middle of the front bumper and two more look down from the side mirrors, and some add audio warnings when you get too close to an obstacle.

sec07-card-sec07-F09.front: When does a curve speed warning trigger, and who remains responsible for picking a safe speed?
sec07-card-sec07-F09.expected_back: A curve speed warning alerts you by sound, vibration or both when you approach a curve or exit too fast, but you remain responsible for choosing a safe speed.

sec07-card-sec07-F10.front: Around what speed range does pedestrian, bicycle, and obstacle detection operate, and what do some versions add?
sec07-card-sec07-F10.expected_back: Pedestrian, bicycle and obstacle detection works at low speeds, generally around twenty-five miles per hour, and some versions brake automatically.

sec07-card-sec07-F11.front: What does it mean when obstacle-detection beeps speed up and turn into a continuous tone?
sec07-card-sec07-F11.expected_back: With detection systems, beeps may speed up as the vehicle gets closer to an obstacle, and continuous beeping can mean a collision is imminent.

sec07-card-sec07-R05.front: What blind angle limits some pedestrian or cyclist detection systems, and where should you verify your car's limits?
sec07-card-sec07-R05.expected_back: Some detection systems only notice cyclists, pedestrians or obstacles directly in front of the vehicle and moving the same way, so read the owner's manual to learn how your car warns you.

sec07-card-sec07-F12.front: Why must you never rely on pedestrian, bicycle, or obstacle sensors—especially on city streets?
sec07-card-sec07-F12.expected_back: Do not rely on bicycle, pedestrian or obstacle detection; keep checking for people and objects yourself, especially in urban areas.

sec07-card-sec07-F13.front: What does a forward collision warning scan for, and does the warning system apply the brakes itself?
sec07-card-sec07-F13.expected_back: A forward collision warning scans ahead and warns of slower or stopped vehicles and objects so you can brake or swerve in time, but the warning alone does not brake for you.

sec07-card-sec07-F14.front: How does a lane departure warning alert you when your tires drift toward a lane stripe?
sec07-card-sec07-F14.expected_back: A lane departure warning uses visual, vibrating or sound alerts to tell you that you are drifting out of your lane so you can steer back to its center.

sec07-card-sec07-R11.front: Who does the steering when a standard lane departure warning goes off?
sec07-card-sec07-R11.expected_back: A lane departure warning leaves the steering to you: its alerts exist to prompt the driver to steer back toward the middle of the lane after an accidental drift.

sec07-card-sec07-F15.front: What does a constant solid tone from bumper parking sensors tell you?
sec07-card-sec07-F15.expected_back: Parking sensors signal how close objects are as you park; a constant tone means you are too close to an object.

sec07-card-sec07-F16.front: What specific hazard does a rear cross-traffic alert watch for while you back out?
sec07-card-sec07-F16.expected_back: A rear cross-traffic alert warns you when one or more vehicles are about to cross the path you are backing into.

sec07-card-sec07-R08.front: When does a high-speed alert chime, and how does it help?
sec07-card-sec07-R08.expected_back: A high speed alert sounds when you are speeding, helping you hold a safe speed.

sec07-card-sec07-F17.front: How do active driver-assistance technologies go beyond passive warnings in certain situations?
sec07-card-sec07-F17.expected_back: Driver assistance technologies perform part of the driving task in certain situations, either adjusting the vehicle themselves or helping the driver brake or steer.

sec07-card-sec07-R10.front: What makes a vehicle feature count as a safety-critical technology?
sec07-card-sec07-R10.expected_back: Safety-critical technologies are those that may prevent a crash or reduce how severe it is.

sec07-card-sec07-F18.front: When does automatic emergency braking clamp the brakes hard, and what two habits must you keep anyway?
sec07-card-sec07-F18.expected_back: Automatic emergency braking senses slow or stopped traffic or objects ahead and brakes hard if the driver does not respond, so keep scanning and keep a safe following distance anyway.

sec07-card-sec07-R06.front: What is the exact difference between forward collision warning and automatic emergency braking?
sec07-card-sec07-R06.expected_back: A forward collision warning only warns and leaves the braking to you, whereas automatic emergency braking applies the brakes itself if you fail to respond.

sec07-card-sec07-F19.front: What two steps does automatic reverse braking take when an obstacle appears behind you?
sec07-card-sec07-F19.expected_back: Automatic reverse braking warns with beeps or visual signals when an obstacle is detected while backing and applies the brakes at once if the driver does not react.

sec07-card-sec07-R07.front: How does a rear cross-traffic alert differ from automatic reverse braking?
sec07-card-sec07-R07.expected_back: A rear cross-traffic alert only warns that a vehicle is about to cross your backing path, whereas automatic reverse braking applies the brakes itself when you fail to react to a detected obstacle.

sec07-card-sec07-F20.front: How does lane-keeping assist act when you drift, what cancels it, and when does it fail to see lanes?
sec07-card-sec07-F20.expected_back: Lane keeping assist alerts you when you drift and may gently steer you back if you do not act; a nudge of the wheel cancels it, and it does not work when lane lines are faint or covered by snow or dirt.

sec07-card-sec07-F21.front: What can left-turn crash avoidance do during a low-speed left turn, and who still judges safe gaps?
sec07-card-sec07-F21.expected_back: Left turn crash avoidance watches oncoming traffic during low-speed left turns, can stop the car from moving into a gap that is too small, and brakes automatically if a crash is imminent, but you must still judge when it is safe to turn.

sec07-card-sec07-R09.front: If active safety tech reacts to a sudden hazard during your Nevada driving test, how is it scored?
sec07-card-sec07-R09.expected_back: Assistance technology can react faster than a person when a vehicle or object suddenly appears ahead, and if that happens during a practical driving test, the examiner decides at their discretion how it is scored.

sec07-card-sec07-F22.front: May you use convenience features like adaptive cruise control or automatic parallel parking during a Nevada driving exam?
sec07-card-sec07-F22.expected_back: Convenience technologies such as adaptive cruise control and automatic parallel parking do not demonstrate a required skill and are not permitted during the testing process.

sec07-card-sec07-F23.front: What does adaptive cruise control manage, and when does the handbook advise switching it off?
sec07-card-sec07-F23.expected_back: Adaptive cruise control speeds up or slows down to hold a following gap you choose, but you must stay aware of your surroundings, and it is advised not to use it in bad weather or other unsafe conditions.

sec07-card-sec07-R12.front: What three steps set up adaptive cruise control, and what extra capability do advanced versions add?
sec07-card-sec07-R12.memory_hook: Reach speed, switch on, pick gap
sec07-card-sec07-R12.expected_back: To use adaptive cruise control, reach your desired speed, switch it on and choose a short, medium or long following gap; advanced versions can slow, stop and restart in traffic jams.

sec07-card-sec07-R13.front: During automatic parallel parking, what does the car handle and what two duties stay with the driver?
sec07-card-sec07-R13.expected_back: Automatic parallel parking searches for a usable space and guides you into it with prompts such as pulling ahead, shifting to reverse and letting go of the wheel, but you remain responsible for braking and watching around you.

sec07-card-sec07-R14.front: What number range does the Society of Automotive Engineers use to classify driving automation from none to self-driving?
sec07-card-sec07-R14.expected_back: The Society of Automotive Engineers classifies driving automation in levels from zero to five, starting with vehicles that lack the technology and ending with self-driving vehicles.

sec07-card-sec07-F24.front: Which SAE automation tiers qualify a vehicle as autonomous under Nevada law?
sec07-card-sec07-F24.expected_back: In Nevada an autonomous vehicle is one with an automated driving system designed for driving-automation level three, four or five under the SAE J3016 standard, including fully autonomous vehicles (NRS 482A point zero three zero).

sec08-card-sec08-F01.front: What visibility limits and oncoming hazard make night driving always riskier than daytime driving?
sec08-card-sec08-F01.expected_back: Night driving is always harder and more hazardous than daytime driving because you see less, later and not as far, and oncoming headlight glare adds to the difficulty.

sec08-card-sec08-F02.front: How fast may you safely travel at night relative to the beam of your headlights?
sec08-card-sec08-F02.expected_back: At night, always be able to stop within the distance your headlights light up, and keep your speed under control and within posted limits.

sec08-card-sec08-F03.front: Where should you aim your eyes when bright oncoming headlights shine toward you at night?
sec08-card-sec08-F03.expected_back: Do not look straight into oncoming headlights; look down toward the right side of your lane, using the edge line or center line as a guide.

sec08-card-sec08-F04.front: What two rules cover sunglasses and windshield cleanliness for night driving?
sec08-card-sec08-F04.memory_hook: Zero sunglasses, clean glass both sides
sec08-card-sec08-F04.expected_back: Never wear sunglasses when driving at night, and keep the windshield clean inside and out.

sec08-card-sec08-R02.front: Why do pedestrians require extra driver vigilance after dark?
sec08-card-sec08-R02.expected_back: Pedestrians are hard to see at night, so stay especially watchful for them after dark.

sec08-card-sec08-R03.front: What share and count of Nevada fatal crashes occurred between six in the evening and eight fifty-nine at night in the handbook report?
sec08-card-sec08-R03.expected_back: Between two thousand fifteen and two thousand nineteen Nevada recorded two hundred seventy-six fatal crashes from six PM to eight fifty-nine PM, which was nineteen percent of all fatal crashes.

sec08-card-sec08-F05.front: During what clock window and visibility distance are headlights legally required in Nevada?
sec08-card-sec08-F05.expected_back: Headlights are required by law from a half hour after sunset to a half hour before sunrise, whenever there is not enough light, and whenever people or vehicles cannot be seen clearly at one thousand feet.

sec08-card-sec08-F06.front: Besides dusk-to-dawn and low sightlines, when else are headlights legally required or strongly advisable?
sec08-card-sec08-F06.memory_hook: Required by signs, smart in storms
sec08-card-sec08-F06.expected_back: Headlights are also required when an official traffic control device directs you to use them, and using them in rain, snow or fog is advisable.

sec08-card-sec08-F07.front: Where do high beams belong at night, and at what distances must you dim for oncoming versus followed vehicles?
sec08-card-sec08-F07.memory_hook: Five hundred oncoming, three hundred behind
sec08-card-sec08-F07.expected_back: Use high beams in open country at night, but switch to low beams at least five hundred feet before meeting an oncoming vehicle and three hundred feet before reaching a vehicle you are following.

sec08-card-sec08-R01.front: How do Nevada's two high-beam dimming distances compare between meeting and following another vehicle?
sec08-card-sec08-R01.expected_back: High beams belong in open country at night, but you must dim to low beams at least five hundred feet before an oncoming vehicle and at least three hundred feet behind a vehicle you follow.

sec08-card-sec08-F08.front: Is driving with only parking lights legal, and how may headlights warn a driver ahead before passing?
sec08-card-sec08-F08.expected_back: Do not drive with only the parking lights on; you may flash your headlights to warn a driver ahead that you plan to pass.

sec08-card-sec08-F09.front: What is the single most important adjustment in bad weather, and how much longer can slippery stops stretch?
sec08-card-sec08-F09.expected_back: The most important thing in bad weather is to slow down, since stopping distances on slippery roads can be two to ten times longer than on dry pavement.

sec08-card-sec08-R04.front: Why must you widen following space and track taillights closely in Nevada wind, fog, rain, or snow?
sec08-card-sec08-R04.expected_back: Nevada weather can change suddenly with wind, rain and snowstorms, and in fog, rain or snow other drivers struggle to see just as you do, so leave extra space and watch the tail lights ahead.

sec08-card-sec08-F10.front: Which three tire setups help on snowy or icy roads, and do they make sliding impossible?
sec08-card-sec08-F10.expected_back: For snowy or icy roads, fit chains, snow tires or all-weather radials, and remember that even well-equipped vehicles can slide.

sec08-card-sec08-F11.front: How should you pull away, check stopping grip, and approach corners on snow or ice?
sec08-card-sec08-F11.memory_hook: Start gently, test brakes, slow early
sec08-card-sec08-F11.expected_back: On snow or ice, start very slowly, test your brakes gently to learn how well you can stop, and begin slowing well before intersections and turns.
