sec08-card-sec08-F12.front: Why is no single speed ever completely safe on snowy or icy roads?
sec08-card-sec08-F12.expected_back: No speed is completely safe on snow and ice, because conditions change with sun, shade and sanding from one block or stretch of road to the next.

sec08-card-sec08-F13.front: How does slippery-road braking technique differ between standard brakes and anti-lock brakes?
sec08-card-sec08-F13.memory_hook: Light taps without, firm hold ABS
sec08-card-sec08-F13.expected_back: On slippery roads, gentle braking with a slow, light touch-and-release pattern helps you stop safely, but a vehicle with ABS needs firm, continuous pedal pressure for the anti-lock feature to work.

sec08-card-sec08-R05.front: Why should you check your owner's manual before winter arrives regarding ice braking?
sec08-card-sec08-R05.expected_back: Without ABS, brake on ice with a slow, light touch-and-release pattern, while with ABS you hold firm, continuous pressure on the pedal; check the owner's manual.

sec08-card-sec08-R06.front: Which three preparation and control habits keep snow and ice trips safer?
sec08-card-sec08-R06.memory_hook: Smooth inputs, clear glass, extra time
sec08-card-sec08-R06.expected_back: On snow and ice avoid sudden changes in speed or direction, keep windows and windshield clear, and allow extra time to reach your destination.

sec08-card-sec08-F14.front: Between which exact calendar dates may studded snow tires—or engaged retractable studs—be driven in Nevada?
sec08-card-sec08-F14.expected_back: Studded snow tires may be used only from October one through April thirty; tires with retractable studs are legal all year, but the studs may be engaged only within those dates.

sec08-card-sec08-F15.front: What does skidding mean physically, and on which four surfaces does it happen?
sec08-card-sec08-F15.memory_hook: Lost tire grip across slick surfaces
sec08-card-sec08-F15.expected_back: Skidding means the tires have lost traction; it happens most on ice or packed snow but also on wet pavement or gravel.

sec08-card-sec08-R07.front: Why should you check your owner's manual for skid recovery, and what mindset comes first?
sec08-card-sec08-R07.expected_back: Skid recovery differs by braking and steering system and by four-wheel or front-wheel drive, so the owner's manual is the source for your vehicle, and in any emergency stay calm.

sec08-card-sec08-F16.front: What sequence should you follow if your service brakes fail, and which gear position is forbidden?
sec08-card-sec08-F16.memory_hook: Pump, parking brake, downshift, never park
sec08-card-sec08-F16.expected_back: If the brakes fail, pump the pedal; if they still do not respond, use the parking brake and shift to a lower gear if possible, but never shift into park.

sec08-card-sec08-R09.front: Why should you shift into a lower gear before descending a long downhill stretch?
sec08-card-sec08-R09.expected_back: Use a lower gear when driving downhill for long stretches to avoid wearing out the brakes.

sec08-card-sec08-F18.front: What steps handle a stuck gas pedal from first quick try to safe roadside stop?
sec08-card-sec08-F18.expected_back: If the gas pedal sticks, quickly press it hard and release; if it stays stuck, shift to neutral, brake, and pull off to the right and stop, never shifting into park.

sec08-card-sec08-R08.front: How does your gearshift move differ between failed brakes and a stuck gas pedal, and what stays banned in both?
sec08-card-sec08-R08.expected_back: With failed brakes you shift to a lower gear and use the parking brake, while with a stuck gas pedal you shift to neutral and brake; in neither case do you shift into park.

sec08-card-sec08-F17.front: How do you test and dry out wet brakes after driving through deep water?
sec08-card-sec08-F17.memory_hook: Low gear, light brake, test two-hundred
sec08-card-sec08-F17.expected_back: After driving through deep water, test your brakes; dry them by driving slowly in low gear while braking lightly, testing about every two hundred feet until they work normally.

sec08-card-sec08-R10.front: What should you do if your windshield wipers quit working during heavy rain or snow?
sec08-card-sec08-R10.expected_back: When the wipers stop working during heavy rain or snow, reduce speed, roll the window down and lean out to see, and get off the highway to the right and stop as soon as you can.

sec08-card-sec08-R11.front: How can you guide yourself off the road if your headlights suddenly fail at night?
sec08-card-sec08-R11.expected_back: If the headlights fail, slow down and leave the roadway as soon as possible, using parking lights, turn signals or four-way flashers, which usually still work, to guide you.

sec08-card-sec08-F19.front: What immediate steps belong when smoke rises from under your hood?
sec08-card-sec08-F19.memory_hook: Pull off, cut ignition, hood care
sec08-card-sec08-F19.expected_back: If you see smoke rising from the engine area, slow, get off the road and shut off the ignition immediately, and open the hood with extreme caution.

sec08-card-sec08-F20.front: Why must you never throw water on a vehicle fire, what works instead, and how far back do you retreat if unstoppable?
sec08-card-sec08-F20.expected_back: Never use water on a vehicle fire, because burning gasoline floats and spreads; use a chemical extinguisher or sand or dirt, and if the fire cannot be stopped move at least one hundred feet away.

sec08-card-sec08-F21.front: When steering fails, how does your braking choice depend on whether the car tracks straight or drifts toward danger?
sec08-card-sec08-F21.expected_back: If steering fails, ease off the accelerator; if the car holds its lane, slow and brake gently with flashers on, but brake hard if it heads off the road or toward a vehicle or pedestrian.

sec08-card-sec08-F22.front: What four actions must you take—and which swerve must you avoid—when an oncoming car enters your lane?
sec08-card-sec08-F22.expected_back: If a vehicle comes at you in your lane, slow down, sound the horn, flash your headlights and pull as far right as is safe, without swerving into the lane it left.

sec08-card-sec08-F23.front: Which three driver factors fuel Nevada's deadly single-vehicle run-off-road crashes?
sec08-card-sec08-F23.expected_back: Running off the road causes serious single-vehicle crashes that account for many Nevada deaths, with fatigue, inattention and speeding as major factors.

sec08-card-sec08-F24.front: How do you safely recover after drifting onto an unpaved highway shoulder?
sec08-card-sec08-F24.memory_hook: Lift gas, hold straight, ease back
sec08-card-sec08-F24.expected_back: If you drift onto the shoulder, stay calm, lift off the gas, brake only carefully, grip the wheel firmly, and do not swerve back; stay on the shoulder until fully in control, then ease back onto the road.

sec08-card-sec08-F25.front: What must you do immediately in a tire blowout before touching the brake pedal?
sec08-card-sec08-F25.memory_hook: Grip firm, lift gas, skip brakes
sec08-card-sec08-F25.expected_back: In a tire blowout, grip the wheel firmly and ease off the gas without hitting the brakes, then brake gently only once the vehicle is under control and has slowed.

sec08-card-sec08-R12.front: How does early braking advice differ between a tire blowout and a shoulder drift?
sec08-card-sec08-R12.expected_back: In a blowout you must not hit the brakes until the vehicle is under control, whereas after drifting onto the shoulder you may brake, but only carefully; in both cases grip the wheel firmly and lift off the gas.

sec08-card-sec08-R13.front: Once a tire blowout is slowed and controlled, what three steps clear you from danger?
sec08-card-sec08-R13.expected_back: After a blowout, signal, pull safely off the road and warn others with parking lights or flashers.

sec08-card-sec08-R14.front: Where should a disabled vehicle sit, how do you warn approaching traffic, and what comes next?
sec08-card-sec08-R14.expected_back: With a disabled vehicle, get all four wheels off the roadway if possible, warn other drivers with parking lights, flashers or flares, and have it towed as soon as you can.

sec08-card-sec08-R15.front: Why is dry Nevada terrain prone to flash floods, and what happens once a vehicle starts floating?
sec08-card-sec08-R15.expected_back: Nevada's dry climate makes flash floods likely, especially in summer storms, spring thaw or long rains, and floating vehicles drift toward deeper, faster water where top-heavy ones may roll.

sec08-card-sec08-F26.front: What share of flash-flood deaths involve vehicles, and how shallow a film of water can break control?
sec08-card-sec08-F26.expected_back: More than half of all flash flood deaths involve vehicles, and less than one inch of water can make a driver lose control.

sec08-card-sec08-F27.front: How little water pushes a fast-moving car off the road, and what depth floats most vehicles?
sec08-card-sec08-F27.memory_hook: Six inches pushes, two feet floats
sec08-card-sec08-F27.expected_back: Most vehicles can float in two feet of water or less, and a car moving fast can be pushed off the road by only six inches of water.

sec08-card-sec08-F28.front: Why must you turn around instead of driving across any flooded roadway?
sec08-card-sec08-F28.expected_back: Never try to drive through a flooded road; turn around and take another route or wait for the water to go down, since its depth and whether the road beneath has washed out cannot be judged.

sec08-card-sec08-F29.front: What must you do immediately if your vehicle stalls in rising floodwater and exiting is safe?
sec08-card-sec08-F29.expected_back: If your vehicle stalls in rising flood water and it is safe, leave it at once and get to higher ground.

sec08-card-sec08-F30.front: What is the only sure flood-safety rule, and how must you treat road-closed barricades?
sec08-card-sec08-F30.expected_back: The only sure flood safety rule is to turn around and stay off flooded roads, and you must never drive around barricades that officials have put up.

sec08-card-sec08-R16.front: Why do nighttime storms and desert washes demand extra flood caution?
sec08-card-sec08-R16.expected_back: Be extra careful about floods at night, never cross flowing streams or water over the road, and when water rises fast turn around and move to higher ground away from creeks and flood channels.

sec08-card-sec08-F31.front: What color marks work-zone signs, cones, and barrels, and what roadway conditions should you anticipate inside?
sec08-card-sec08-F31.expected_back: Work zones are marked with orange signs, cones and barrels; lanes narrow, surfaces are rough and traffic may stop completely, so stay alert and expect stopped cars ahead.

sec08-card-sec08-F32.front: What legal consequence hits a driver who moves barriers or signs to sneak onto a closed road?
sec08-card-sec08-F32.expected_back: Moving barriers or signs to drive onto a closed road is illegal and carries double penalties for work-zone violations.

sec08-card-sec08-F33.front: What happens to speeding fines in Nevada work zones, and how do black-and-white speed signs differ from orange ones?
sec08-card-sec08-F33.memory_hook: Fines double, white binds, orange advises
sec08-card-sec08-F33.expected_back: Speeding fines double in work zones; black and white speed limit signs are regulatory, while orange speed limit signs are advisory and suggest slower, safer speeds.

sec08-card-sec08-R17.front: Between a black-and-white speed sign and an orange speed sign in a work zone, which sets the legal limit?
sec08-card-sec08-R17.expected_back: A black and white speed limit sign in a work zone is the legal limit, while an orange one is only an advisory, safer speed.

sec08-card-sec08-F34.front: Which four actions belong whenever orange work-zone signs appear ahead?
sec08-card-sec08-F34.memory_hook: Slow, scan crews, obey flaggers, merge
sec08-card-sec08-F34.expected_back: Whenever you see orange signs, slow down, watch for workers and equipment, follow flaggers' instructions and merge carefully and cooperatively.

sec08-card-sec08-R18.front: Why are nighttime work zones extra hazardous, and what often guides single-lane traffic through them?
sec08-card-sec08-R18.memory_hook: Low sight, drowsy drivers, pilot cars
sec08-card-sec08-R18.expected_back: Visibility in work zones may be lower, especially at night, so do not drive tired and watch for sleepy drivers; flaggers and pilot cars often control traffic.

sec08-card-sec08-F35.front: Which stopped emergency, utility, or service vehicles trigger Nevada's slow-down-and-prepare-to-stop law?
sec08-card-sec08-F35.expected_back: When approaching a stopped emergency, utility or service vehicle such as a police car, tow truck, NDOT vehicle or garbage truck, slow to a reasonable speed below the posted limit, proceed with caution and be ready to stop (NRS 484B point six zero seven).

sec08-card-sec08-F36.front: Which lane must you choose when passing a protected stopped emergency or service vehicle if conditions allow?
sec08-card-sec08-F36.expected_back: When passing such a stopped vehicle, move if possible into a lane not next to the one it occupies, unless road, traffic or weather conditions make that unsafe or impossible.

sec08-card-sec08-F37.front: Which two additional roadside situations trigger Nevada's slow-down protection duty?
sec08-card-sec08-F37.expected_back: The slow-down duty also applies when approaching a vehicle showing non-flashing blue lights in certain circumstances and when someone is repairing a vehicle.

sec08-card-sec08-F38.front: May non-emergency drivers stop casually along a highway shoulder marked for emergency use?
sec08-card-sec08-F38.expected_back: Drivers of non-emergency vehicles may not stop on a highway shoulder marked for emergency use.

sec08-card-sec08-R19.front: Which seven emergency, incident, or transit vehicles may drive on signed paved highway shoulders in Nevada?
sec08-card-sec08-R19.expected_back: Some emergency vehicles may drive on a paved highway shoulder where signs authorize it, including police, fire engines and ambulances, traffic incident management vehicles, tow cars, coroner vehicles and public transit buses (NRS 484B point two one zero).

sec08-card-sec08-R20.front: On what date did Nevada's authorized emergency shoulder-driving law take effect?
sec08-card-sec08-R20.expected_back: The shoulder-use rule for emergency vehicles took effect on January one, two thousand twenty-four.

sec09-card-sec09-R01.front: Roughly how many crashes happen each year between passenger cars and commercial vehicles?
sec09-card-sec09-R01.expected_back: The handbook puts crashes between cars and commercial vehicles at more than two hundred thousand a year, many of them avoidable.

sec09-card-sec09-F01.front: How do large commercial vehicles differ from passenger cars in handling, visibility, and stopping?
sec09-card-sec09-F01.memory_hook: Less agile, bigger blinds, longer stops
sec09-card-sec09-F01.expected_back: Large commercial vehicles cannot maneuver like cars, have much bigger blind spots, and need more time and space to slow down or stop.

sec09-card-sec09-F02.front: Who triggers most car-versus-truck crashes, and who suffers the worst injuries?
sec09-card-sec09-F02.expected_back: Most crashes between large trucks and smaller cars are caused by the car drivers, and the people in the cars are far more likely to be killed or hurt.

sec09-card-sec09-F03.front: What is the no-zone surrounding a large commercial truck or bus?
sec09-card-sec09-F03.expected_back: The no-zone is the set of blind spots around a large truck or bus, at its sides, rear and front, where a car effectively disappears from the driver's view.

sec09-card-sec09-F04.front: Why is hanging in a truck's or bus's right-side no-zone doubly dangerous?
sec09-card-sec09-F04.expected_back: The right-side no-zone is doubly dangerous because trucks and buses swing wide when turning right.

sec09-card-sec09-F05.front: What quick mirror check tells you whether a truck or bus driver can see your car alongside?
sec09-card-sec09-F05.expected_back: Do not linger beside a truck or bus: if you cannot see the driver's face in their side mirror, the driver cannot see you.

sec09-card-sec09-F06.front: How much stopping time and distance do heavy trucks and buses need compared with cars?
sec09-card-sec09-F06.expected_back: Large trucks and buses need nearly twice the time and distance cars need to stop, so cutting in front and slowing can get you rear-ended.

sec09-card-sec09-F07.front: When is it safe to pull back into the lane ahead of a truck you just passed, and how must you hold speed?
sec09-card-sec09-F07.memory_hook: Whole cab in mirror; keep pace
sec09-card-sec09-F07.expected_back: After passing a truck or bus, wait until its whole front shows in your rearview mirror before moving into its lane, and then do not slow down.

sec09-card-sec09-F08.front: Which three dangers make tailgating directly behind a truck or bus reckless?
sec09-card-sec09-F08.expected_back: Do not tailgate a truck or bus: its driver cannot see you directly behind, you cannot see the road beyond it, and a sudden stop leaves you nowhere to go.

sec09-card-sec09-R02.front: How does the front no-zone crash trap differ from the rear no-zone trap?
sec09-card-sec09-R02.expected_back: In the front no-zone the danger is cutting in too soon and slowing, which can get you rear-ended, while in the rear no-zone the danger is tailgating, where neither driver can see the other's situation.

sec09-card-sec09-F09.front: Why must you never sneak behind a commercial truck while it is backing up?
sec09-card-sec09-F09.expected_back: Never pass behind a commercial truck that is backing up, because its driver cannot see vehicles or people directly behind it.

sec09-card-sec09-F10.front: Why do trucks sometimes swing left before turning right, and what must you never try beside the curb?
sec09-card-sec09-F10.expected_back: Trucks and buses may swing wide left to make a right turn, or wide right to make a left turn, so never try to squeeze between one and the curb.

sec09-card-sec09-F11.front: What legal rights and lane privileges do motorcyclists hold on Nevada roads?
sec09-card-sec09-F11.expected_back: Motorcyclists have the same rights and responsibilities as other drivers, including the right to use a full traffic lane.

sec09-card-sec09-F12.front: When may two motorcycles or mopeds ride side by side in one lane, and how must they ride otherwise?
sec09-card-sec09-F12.expected_back: With the drivers' consent, motorcycles and mopeds may ride at most two abreast in a single lane; without consent they must ride staggered (NRS four hundred eighty-six point three five one).

sec09-card-sec09-F13.front: Why do oncoming motorcycles fool car drivers waiting to turn left?
sec09-card-sec09-F13.expected_back: Motorcycles are small, so they are harder to see, may seem farther away than they really are, and their speed is hard to judge.

sec09-card-sec09-F14.front: Why must you confirm what a motorcyclist is actually doing instead of trusting their turn signal?
sec09-card-sec09-F14.expected_back: Most motorcycle turn signals do not cancel themselves, so before a turn or lane change that depends on a rider's path, be sure what the rider is actually doing.

sec09-card-sec09-R03.front: Which two rider or bike movements tip you off that a motorcyclist is about to turn or shift lanes?
sec09-card-sec09-R03.expected_back: Clues to a motorcyclist's next move include the rider or passenger turning their head to look back and the rider starting to lean or tilt the motorcycle.

sec09-card-sec09-R04.front: Which two outside conditions can shove a motorcycle sideways inside or out of its lane?
sec09-card-sec09-R04.expected_back: Strong winds or a rough road surface can push a motorcycle out of its position on the road.

sec09-card-sec09-F15.front: How should you adjust when coming up behind a motorcycle in traffic?
sec09-card-sec09-F15.expected_back: Approaching a motorcycle from behind, begin slowing earlier than you would for a car and keep a generous gap.

sec09-card-sec09-F16.front: Why is dimming high beams even more critical when approaching a motorcycle than a car?
sec09-card-sec09-F16.expected_back: Always dim your headlights when approaching a motorcycle, because riders steer by balance and high-beam glare is more dangerous to them than to car or truck drivers.

sec09-card-sec09-F17.front: How should rain or slick pavement change your following distance behind a motorcycle?
sec09-card-sec09-F17.expected_back: Leave even more following distance behind a motorcycle when it is raining or the road is slippery.

sec09-card-sec09-F18.front: What credential addition must appear on a Nevada license to ride a motorcycle legally?
sec09-card-sec09-F18.expected_back: Riding a motorcycle requires a special endorsement on a Nevada driver's license.

sec09-card-sec09-F19.front: What motor-power cap and flat-ground top speed define a moped under Nevada law?
sec09-card-sec09-F19.expected_back: Nevada sets a moped apart by motor size, a maximum of two brake horsepower, and a top speed of thirty miles per hour on flat or nearly flat ground.

sec09-card-sec09-F20.front: Which lane must moped riders use, and what four exceptions allow leaving it?
sec09-card-sec09-F20.expected_back: Moped riders must stay in the far right lane unless there is only one lane, they are preparing a left turn within a quarter mile, the right lane is unsafe, or a police officer directs otherwise.

sec09-card-sec09-F21.front: What registration, insurance, and helmet rules govern mopeds in Nevada?
sec09-card-sec09-F21.expected_back: Mopeds must be registered with the DMV for a one-time fee but need no insurance, and moped riders and passengers must wear helmets in Nevada.

sec09-card-sec09-R05.front: How do Nevada motorcycles and mopeds contrast in licensing and lane placement?
sec09-card-sec09-R05.expected_back: Motorcycles need a license endorsement, while mopeds, limited in horsepower and to a top speed of thirty miles per hour, must keep to the far right lane in most situations.

sec09-card-sec09-R08.front: What degree of caution do drivers owe mopeds, and what duties apply to moped riders?
sec09-card-sec09-R08.memory_hook: Same motorcycle caution; extra rider duties
sec09-card-sec09-R08.expected_back: Drivers around mopeds take the same precautions as around motorcycles, and moped riders share the same rights and duties as other drivers plus extra ones tied to their vehicle's limits.

sec09-card-sec09-F22.front: When must you stop for a school bus displaying flashing red lights, and when may you proceed?
sec09-card-sec09-F22.memory_hook: Stop everywhere until lights turn off
sec09-card-sec09-F22.expected_back: You must stop at any location for a school bus showing a flashing red signal, and you may not pass it until the bus driver turns those lights off (NRS 484B point three five three).

sec09-card-sec09-F23.front: Who is required to stop for a flashing-red school bus on a divided highway?
sec09-card-sec09-F23.expected_back: On a divided highway, you have to stop for a school bus only when you are traveling in the same direction as the bus.

sec09-card-sec09-R06.front: How do school-bus stopping rules differ between an undivided road and a divided highway?
sec09-card-sec09-R06.expected_back: On an undivided road, traffic in both directions stops for a school bus with flashing red lights, but on a divided highway only traffic going the same direction as the bus must stop.

sec09-card-sec09-R07.front: What happens under Nevada law when a school-bus driver reports a car passing illegally?
sec09-card-sec09-R07.expected_back: Nevada lets school bus drivers report drivers who pass illegally to the school district and the DMV, and the vehicle's registered owner then receives a warning letter.

sec09-card-sec09-F29.front: Who is barred from riding in a pickup bed or flatbed on paved Nevada highways, and what two exceptions exist?
sec09-card-sec09-F29.expected_back: In Nevada, no one under eighteen may ride in a pickup bed or on a flatbed truck on a paved highway, except in a parade authorized by a local authority or while farming or ranching.

sec09-card-sec09-F24.front: What serious criminal traffic charge and license penalty can hit a driver who causes even a minor bicycle collision?
sec09-card-sec09-F24.expected_back: A motorist who causes even a minor collision with a bicycle, or deliberately interferes with a cyclist, may be charged with reckless driving, which can bring a license suspension.

sec09-card-sec09-R11.front: Does Nevada's ban on deliberate interference apply only to car drivers or to bicyclists too?
sec09-card-sec09-R11.expected_back: Cyclists may not deliberately interfere with motor vehicles, just as motorists may not deliberately interfere with cyclists.

sec09-card-sec09-F25.front: Where inside a travel lane do cyclists ride, and when may they move away from that edge?
sec09-card-sec09-F25.expected_back: Cyclists may ride in a traffic lane, keeping as far right as practicable unless they are preparing to turn or passing another vehicle.

sec09-card-sec09-R09.front: How must cyclists handle traffic lights and signs, and how should they use a pedestrian crosswalk?
sec09-card-sec09-R09.expected_back: Cyclists must obey all signs and signals, and a cyclist who crosses an intersection in a crosswalk should get off and walk across as a pedestrian.

sec09-card-sec09-R10.front: How often must a cyclist signal a turn, when may they skip it, and how may right turns be shown?
sec09-card-sec09-R10.expected_back: A cyclist must give a hand signal once before turning unless in a designated turn lane or both hands are needed for safe control, and may signal a right turn with the right arm.

sec09-card-sec09-F26.front: How must drivers treat approaching bicyclists when yielding right-of-way at intersections?
sec09-card-sec09-F26.expected_back: At intersections, motorists must yield to cyclists just as they would to other vehicles and pedestrians.

sec09-card-sec09-F27.front: May you drive, stop, or park in a marked bike lane—and what four narrow exceptions exist?
sec09-card-sec09-F27.expected_back: Motorists may not stop, park or drive in a bike lane or bike path except to enter or leave an alley or driveway, on official duty, when police direct it, or in an emergency.

sec09-card-sec09-F28.front: What passing-and-turning mistake must you never make near a cyclist, and when else must you check?
sec09-card-sec09-F28.expected_back: Never speed up to pass a cyclist just before you turn, and check for cyclists before opening a parked car's door or backing out of a driveway or lot.

sec09-card-sec09-R12.front: Why do kids on bicycles need extra caution, and what scan belongs before turning into driveways or corners?
sec09-card-sec09-R12.expected_back: Children and other inexperienced riders may not follow traffic rules, so give them extra care and expect the unexpected, and check both ways for cyclists when turning into an intersection or driveway.

sec09-card-sec09-R13.front: What gear and rules should cyclists follow, and which three risky habits should they avoid?
sec09-card-sec09-R13.expected_back: Cyclists should obey the law, wear a helmet and bright clothing and keep bikes repaired, and should not ride against traffic, wear headphones or earpieces, or ride at night without the required lights and reflectors.

sec09-card-sec09-F30.front: What legal duty do drivers owe pedestrians, and what charge can follow any pedestrian collision?
sec09-card-sec09-F30.expected_back: Drivers must use due care to avoid hitting a pedestrian, and a driver who causes any pedestrian collision, however minor, can face a reckless driving charge.

sec09-card-sec09-F31.front: When is it illegal to swing around and pass another car that is slowing or stopped ahead?
sec09-card-sec09-F31.expected_back: It is illegal to overtake a vehicle that is slowing or stopped until you have slowed enough to see why it slowed or stopped.

sec09-card-sec09-F32.front: Where do legal crosswalks exist even when zero white stripes are painted on the asphalt?
sec09-card-sec09-F32.expected_back: A crosswalk exists wherever two streets meet, including a T intersection, whether or not it is painted.

sec09-card-sec09-F33.front: Who holds the right-of-way when your traffic light turns green or when you turn right?
sec09-card-sec09-F33.expected_back: When your light turns green, yield to anyone still crossing, and pedestrians have the right-of-way over drivers turning right.

sec09-card-sec09-F34.front: For which pedestrians in a crosswalk must you slow, yield, or stop?
sec09-card-sec09-F34.expected_back: Yield, slow or stop for a pedestrian in a crosswalk on your half of the road or the half you are turning into, or one coming so close from the other half as to be in danger.

sec09-card-sec09-R15.front: How far across must a pedestrian get before a yielding driver may roll forward?
sec09-card-sec09-R15.expected_back: A vehicle yielding to a pedestrian should wait until the person has crossed into the lanes heading the other way before moving on.

sec09-card-sec09-R14.front: Where should pedestrians walk when a road has a sidewalk versus when none exists?
sec09-card-sec09-R14.expected_back: Where there is a sidewalk pedestrians should use it, and where there is none they should walk on the side of the road facing oncoming traffic.

sec09-card-sec09-R16.front: Around which five everyday community spots must drivers stay extra alert for pedestrians and kids?
sec09-card-sec09-R16.expected_back: Drive with extra care around pedestrians near schools, crosswalks, stop signs, signals and transit stops, especially when children are present.

sec09-card-sec09-R17.front: Which crossing, signal, eye-contact, and night-gear habits protect pedestrians?
sec09-card-sec09-R17.expected_back: Pedestrians should use crosswalks and obey their signals, not start on a flashing Don't Walk, look left, right and left again, make eye contact with stopping drivers, and at night carry a flashlight and wear reflective gear.

sec09-card-sec09-F35.front: Within what distance of a crosswalk should you stop for a blind pedestrian, and why?
sec09-card-sec09-F35.expected_back: When stopping for a blind or visually impaired pedestrian, stop no more than five feet from the crosswalk, since such a pedestrian uses your engine sound as a guide.

sec09-card-sec09-F36.front: How long should you wait for a blind pedestrian to decide, and what cane gesture means go?
sec09-card-sec09-F36.expected_back: Give a blind or visually impaired pedestrian time to decide, about three to four seconds; if the person steps back and pulls in the cane, you may go.

sec09-card-sec09-R18.front: Which four actions must you never take around a blind or visually impaired pedestrian?
sec09-card-sec09-R18.expected_back: Around a blind or visually impaired pedestrian, do not call out directions, do not honk, do not stop in the middle of the crosswalk and do not block the sidewalk.

sec09-card-sec09-R19.front: Why do hybrid and electric vehicles require heightened vigilance around blind pedestrians at crosswalks?
sec09-card-sec09-R19.expected_back: Stop at every crosswalk where pedestrians are waiting, look before any right turn, and be extra alert for blind pedestrians when driving a nearly silent electric vehicle.

sec10-card-sec10-F01.front: What maximum weight rating and total length may a non-commercial Nevada Class C driver tow?
sec10-card-sec10-F01.expected_back: A non-commercial Class C driver may tow a single vehicle or a combination as long as its gross vehicle weight rating does not exceed ten thousand pounds and the whole unit is seventy feet long or shorter.

sec10-card-sec10-F02.front: Which official Nevada handbook covers deeper towing rules and the J endorsement?
sec10-card-sec10-F02.expected_back: Drivers who want more towing information, or a J endorsement, should read the Nevada Non-Commercial A and B, J Endorsement Study Guide on the DMV website.

sec10-card-sec10-F05.front: How does gross vehicle weight differ from gross combination weight?
sec10-card-sec10-F05.expected_back: Gross vehicle weight is the total weight of one vehicle plus its load, while gross combination weight is the total of the powered unit, its trailer or trailers, and the load.

sec10-card-sec10-F06.front: What does gross combination weight rating measure?
sec10-card-sec10-F06.expected_back: Gross combination weight rating is the manufacturer's stated combined loaded weight for a vehicle and the vehicle it tows.

sec10-card-sec10-R01.front: How does actual gross combination weight differ from gross combination weight rating?
sec10-card-sec10-R01.expected_back: Gross combination weight is what the rig and load actually weigh, while the gross combination weight rating is the maximum combined loaded weight the manufacturer specifies.

sec10-card-sec10-R02.front: What does axle weight measure on a vehicle or trailer?
sec10-card-sec10-R02.expected_back: Axle weight is the weight one axle or one set of axles puts on the ground.

sec10-card-sec10-F07.front: Where do you read a tire's safe weight cap, and which two towing parts also carry ratings?
sec10-card-sec10-F07.expected_back: A tire's load rating, printed on its sidewall, is the most weight it can carry safely at a stated pressure; suspensions and coupling devices also carry maximum weight ratings.

sec10-card-sec10-F03.front: How does improperly loaded or loose trailer cargo endanger both traffic and your trailer?
sec10-card-sec10-F03.expected_back: Loading a trailer wrongly endangers you and others, since loose items can strike other road users and a quick stop or crash can damage the trailer's interior.

sec10-card-sec10-F04.front: What four performance problems hit an overloaded towing rig on hills and stops?
sec10-card-sec10-F04.expected_back: Overloading hurts steering, braking and speed control: an overloaded rig crawls up hills, gains too much speed downhill, needs longer to stop, and its overworked brakes can fail.

sec10-card-sec10-F08.front: How does load height affect rollover risk, and where must heavy items ride?
sec10-card-sec10-F08.expected_back: The higher a load's center of gravity, the more likely the vehicle is to overturn, so keep cargo as low as possible and put the heaviest items underneath or in lower compartments.

sec10-card-sec10-F09.front: What goes wrong with too much weight—versus too little weight—on the front steering axle?
sec10-card-sec10-F09.expected_back: Too much weight on the steering axle makes steering hard and can damage that axle and its tires, while too little weight up front can leave the steering axle too light to steer safely.

sec10-card-sec10-F10.front: What traction problem strikes when too little weight sits over the driving axles?
sec10-card-sec10-F10.expected_back: Too little weight on the driving axles gives poor traction and lets the drive wheels spin easily.

sec10-card-sec10-F11.front: What danger comes from loading one side heavier than the other, and how do you prevent tipping?
sec10-card-sec10-F11.expected_back: Uneven side-to-side loading can tip a trailer over, especially in turns; to prevent a rollover, take turns slowly and keep cargo close to the ground.

sec10-card-sec10-R05.front: What extra cargo risks accompany flatbed trailers and foul-weather towing?
sec10-card-sec10-R05.expected_back: Flatbed trailers carry a greater risk of the load shifting sideways or falling off, and in bad weather a poorly balanced rig may not stay balanced.

sec10-card-sec10-R08.front: What two final cargo and exterior checks belong right before pulling out with a trailer?
sec10-card-sec10-R08.expected_back: Pre-trip, make sure the load is balanced and secured and every outside storage compartment door is latched or locked.

sec10-card-sec10-F12.front: How does a load-distributing hitch work, and which trailers rely on it?
sec10-card-sec10-F12.expected_back: A load-distributing hitch spreads the tongue load across all axles of the tow vehicle and trailer to steady the tow vehicle, and is used for heavier utility, boat and travel trailers.

sec10-card-sec10-F13.front: Which three critical steps secure a ball-coupler trailer connection?
sec10-card-sec10-F13.memory_hook: Ball seated, latch locked, chains crossed
sec10-card-sec10-F13.expected_back: When hitching a ball coupler, the ball must be seated firmly in the coupler, the coupler safety latch secured down, and the safety chains attached and crossed.

sec10-card-sec10-F14.front: How must the hitch ball mount and trailer electrical cord be secured?
sec10-card-sec10-F14.expected_back: The ball mount must be locked into the tow vehicle's receiver with its pin and clip or other locking device, and the electric lines must be seated, locked and free of tangles or dragging.

sec10-card-sec10-R04.front: What metal integrity inspection belongs on the coupler hardware and trailer tongue before towing?
sec10-card-sec10-R04.memory_hook: All parts intact; straight uncracked tongue
sec10-card-sec10-R04.expected_back: Before towing with a ball hitch, confirm every coupling part is present and unbroken and the trailer tongue is not bent, cracked or damaged.

sec10-card-sec10-R03.front: How does a bumper ball-and-coupler setup differ from a fifth-wheel hitch in placement and stability?
sec10-card-sec10-R03.expected_back: A ball-and-hitch coupler joins a ball on the tow vehicle to a coupler on the trailer tongue, whereas a fifth-wheel hitch sits in a truck bed and locks onto a kingpin and is less prone to balance problems.

sec10-card-sec10-F15.front: Where does a fifth-wheel hitch mount, and what bed-space precaution does it require?
sec10-card-sec10-F15.expected_back: A fifth-wheel hitch mounts in a pickup bed and couples to the trailer's kingpin; it is very stable but uses most of the bed and needs the space behind it kept clear for turns.

sec10-card-sec10-F16.front: What must you lock before backing under a fifth-wheel kingpin, and what must you verify once jaws shut?
sec10-card-sec10-F16.expected_back: Before backing under a fifth-wheel trailer, lock the trailer brakes, and after the jaws close around the kingpin, make sure the locking lever is locked or the coupling is not properly seated.

sec10-card-sec10-R06.front: What hardware condition must the fifth-wheel mounting frame and trailer kingpin show?
sec10-card-sec10-R06.expected_back: Check that the fifth-wheel mounting assembly is solidly attached with no loose or missing parts and that the kingpin is not bent.

sec10-card-sec10-F17.front: What three visual signs confirm a fifth wheel is seated and lubricated properly?
sec10-card-sec10-F17.expected_back: A coupled fifth wheel must have no gap between the upper and lower coupling, the trailer must sit flat on the skid plate, and the plate must be greased as required.

sec10-card-sec10-R07.front: What must you inspect on fifth-wheel cords, the support platform, and the release arm?
sec10-card-sec10-R07.expected_back: Fifth-wheel electric lines must not be chafed, spliced or worn, the platform supporting the skid plate must be free of cracks, and the release arm must be engaged with any safety latch in place.

sec10-card-sec10-F18.front: How do you physically test your hitch before rolling out, and what cord slack is needed?
sec10-card-sec10-F18.expected_back: Test the hitch by pulling gently forward in low gear against the locked trailer brakes, then look at the connection; chains and electric lines should be secure with enough slack for turns.

sec10-card-sec10-F19.front: At which mileage and time milestones should you re-check your trailer and tie-downs on a trip?
sec10-card-sec10-F19.expected_back: On a long trip, re-inspect the trailer and its load-securing devices within the first fifty miles, then again after three hours or one hundred fifty miles of driving, and ideally at every break.

sec10-card-sec10-F20.front: Is signaling turns and lane changes while towing merely polite advice or Nevada law?
sec10-card-sec10-F20.expected_back: Signalling your intentions while towing is required by law as well as being important for safety.

sec10-card-sec10-R10.front: What human lapse causes major towing crashes, and how do you counter it?
sec10-card-sec10-R10.expected_back: A lack of awareness is a major cause of crashes, so use your mirrors often, signal, and make other drivers aware of your vehicle even when it is in plain sight.

sec10-card-sec10-F21.front: Surprisingly, why do empty trucks take longer to stop than loaded ones?
sec10-card-sec10-F21.expected_back: Empty trucks actually need longer stopping distances than loaded ones, because they have less traction and can bounce and lock their wheels.

sec10-card-sec10-R09.front: How does cargo weight affect brake heat versus overall truck-suspension design?
sec10-card-sec10-R09.expected_back: A heavier vehicle makes the brakes work harder and absorb more heat, yet heavy-vehicle brakes, tires, springs and shocks work best when fully loaded.

sec10-card-sec10-R11.front: Why does managing front, rear, and side space matter even more when towing than in a solo car?
sec10-card-sec10-R11.expected_back: Large vehicles take up more space and need more room to stop and turn, so managing the space around a towing rig matters even more than in a car.

sec10-card-sec10-F22.front: How does steering wheel direction differ at the start of backing a trailer versus a solo car?
sec10-card-sec10-F22.expected_back: When backing a single vehicle you turn the top of the steering wheel toward where you want to go, but when backing a trailer you turn it the opposite way, then follow the trailer once it starts turning.

sec10-card-sec10-R12.front: What two-part steering motion backs a trailer smoothly around a turn?
sec10-card-sec10-R12.expected_back: Backing a car, turn the top of the wheel toward where you want to go; backing a trailer, turn it the opposite way at first and then follow the trailer.

sec10-card-sec10-F23.front: What smart parking habit lets you skip risky trailer backing altogether?
sec10-card-sec10-F23.expected_back: Backing is always dangerous, so avoid it when you can, and park so you can pull forward when leaving.

sec10-card-sec10-F24.front: What inspection and speed rule apply every single time before backing a trailer?
sec10-card-sec10-F24.expected_back: Before backing a trailer, get out and walk around to check your path and clearance to the sides and overhead, then back as slowly as possible.

sec10-card-sec10-R16.front: Which high obstacles are easiest to miss in side mirrors unless you step out before backing?
sec10-card-sec10-R16.expected_back: Before backing into an area, get out and look for overhanging trees, branches or electric wires, which are easy to miss while reversing.

sec10-card-sec10-F25.front: Which way do you turn the top of the steering wheel if your trailer drifts off line while backing?
sec10-card-sec10-F25.expected_back: If the trailer starts drifting off course while backing, correct at once by turning the top of the steering wheel toward the drift.

sec10-card-sec10-F26.front: Toward which side of the rig should you always try to back and turn—even if circling the block?
sec10-card-sec10-F26.expected_back: Back and turn toward the driver's side whenever possible, even if it means circling the block, because backing toward the right side is very dangerous.

sec10-card-sec10-F27.front: Where should a backing helper stand, and what must you agree on before shifting into reverse?
sec10-card-sec10-F27.expected_back: Use a helper standing near the rear where you can see them, and agree on hand signals, including one for stop, before you begin backing.

sec10-card-sec10-R13.front: What three habits keep straight-line trailer backing stress-free?
sec10-card-sec10-R13.expected_back: While backing a trailer, try to set up a straight-line path, watch the mirrors for drift, and pull forward to reposition whenever needed.

sec10-card-sec10-F28.front: How should you swing wide for a tight right trailer turn without inviting cars to sneak inside?
sec10-card-sec10-F28.expected_back: On a right turn that needs extra room, turn wide only as you finish the turn and keep the trailer's rear near the curb; do not swing wide left at the start, which invites drivers to pass on your right.

sec10-card-sec10-F29.front: What should you do—and never do—if finishing a tight turn requires crossing into an oncoming lane?
sec10-card-sec10-F29.expected_back: If you must cross into oncoming traffic to turn, give oncoming vehicles room to pass or stop, but do not back up for them.

sec10-card-sec10-F30.front: How far into an intersection must you pull before turning left with a trailer, and why?
sec10-card-sec10-F30.expected_back: On a left turn with a trailer, reach the center of the intersection before turning, because turning early lets off-tracking swing the vehicle's left side into other traffic.

sec10-card-sec10-F31.front: Which lane must a towing rig always pick when two side-by-side left-turn lanes are offered?
sec10-card-sec10-F31.expected_back: With two left-turn lanes, always use the right-hand one, since starting from the inside lane may force you to swing right into drivers you cannot see.

sec10-card-sec10-R14.front: What goes wrong turning left too early versus starting from the inside dual left lane?
sec10-card-sec10-R14.memory_hook: Early clips left; inner swings right
sec10-card-sec10-R14.expected_back: Turning left too early lets off-tracking carry your left side into vehicles beside you, while starting from the inner of two left-turn lanes risks swinging right into drivers you cannot see.

sec10-card-sec10-F32.front: Why must a towing rig wait for a much wider traffic gap to cross or merge?
sec10-card-sec10-F32.expected_back: A towing rig accelerates slowly, so it needs a much bigger gap to cross or enter traffic, more so when heavily loaded; be sure you can clear the road before traffic arrives.

sec10-card-sec10-F33.front: Which three real-world factors make posted bridge clearance signs untrustworthy?
sec10-card-sec10-F33.expected_back: Do not trust posted heights at bridges and overpasses, since repaving or packed snow may have lowered the clearance, and an empty trailer rides higher than a loaded one.

sec10-card-sec10-F34.front: What should you do whenever you doubt your rig can clear an overhead bridge or structure?
sec10-card-sec10-F34.expected_back: If you doubt you can fit under an object, go slowly, and if still unsure, take another route; low bridges may not be marked.

sec10-card-sec10-R15.front: How should you position a tall trailer when sloped pavement tilts the roof toward roadside trees or signs?
sec10-card-sec10-R15.expected_back: Roads that tilt a vehicle can bring it into signs or trees at the edge, so where that is a risk drive a little closer to the center of the road.

sec10-card-sec10-F35.front: Why must heavily loaded rigs crawl carefully across raised train tracks and drainage dips?
sec10-card-sec10-F35.expected_back: Heavily loaded vehicles have little ground clearance, so cross raised railroad tracks and drainage channels carefully to avoid getting hung up or dragging.

sec10-card-sec10-F36.front: When towing a multi-trailer combination, where must the heaviest trailer always sit?
sec10-card-sec10-F36.expected_back: In a combination of towed vehicles, the heaviest vehicle must always be placed first behind the towing vehicle, with the lighter one at the rear.

sec10-card-sec10-R18.front: How do combination rigs compare with single vehicles in size, skill, and rollover history?
sec10-card-sec10-R18.expected_back: Combinations of vehicles are heavier and longer than single vehicles, need more driving skill, and have been involved in many crashes where only the trailer overturned.

sec10-card-sec10-F37.front: What triggers the crack-the-whip effect on trailers, and how must you steer to prevent it?
sec10-card-sec10-F37.expected_back: Trailers have a crack-the-whip effect, caused by rearward amplification and worse with more trailers, which can flip a trailer during a quick lane change, so steer gently and smoothly.

sec10-card-sec10-R17.front: What does a rearward amplification score of two point zero mean, and how high do triples reach?
sec10-card-sec10-R17.expected_back: In the rearward amplification chart, a value of two point zero means the rear trailer is twice as likely to overturn as the truck, and triples reach three point five.

sec10-card-sec10-R19.front: Why do empty combination rigs stop worse than loaded ones, and how should you compensate?
sec10-card-sec10-R19.memory_hook: Stiff springs skip; scan, gap wide
sec10-card-sec10-R19.expected_back: Empty combination rigs take longer to stop than loaded ones because stiff springs and strong brakes give poor traction, so allow long following distances and look far ahead to brake early.

sec10-card-sec10-R20.front: When is a trailer jackknife likeliest, and how do you catch it before recovery becomes impossible?
sec10-card-sec10-R20.memory_hook: Empty or light; check mirrors braking
sec10-card-sec10-R20.expected_back: A trailer jackknife is more likely when the trailer is empty or lightly loaded; spot it early in the mirrors whenever you brake hard, because once the trailer leaves the lane a jackknife is very hard to stop.

sec10-card-sec10-F38.front: How do you recover when locked trailer wheels start skidding—and why skip the trailer hand brake?
sec10-card-sec10-F38.expected_back: If trailer wheels lock and the trailer starts to skid, release the brakes to regain traction, and do not use the trailer hand brake to straighten the rig, since trailer braking caused the skid.

sec11-card-sec11-F01.front: What type of insurance must every registered motor vehicle in Nevada carry?
sec11-card-sec11-F01.expected_back: All Nevada motorists must comply with mandatory insurance and financial responsibility laws, and every registered motor vehicle in the state must be covered by liability insurance.

sec11-card-sec11-R01.front: When do Nevada's minimum liability coverage amounts legally apply to you?
sec11-card-sec11-R01.expected_back: Nevada law sets minimum liability insurance amounts that apply whenever you drive or own a vehicle in the state.

sec11-card-sec11-F02.front: Which two formats satisfy Nevada's rule for carrying proof of vehicle insurance?
sec11-card-sec11-F02.expected_back: Keep the insurer's Evidence of Insurance Card in the vehicle, or have it ready in electronic form to show on a mobile device.

sec11-card-sec11-F03.front: What are Nevada's minimum liability dollar limits for injury or death to one person versus two or more?
sec11-card-sec11-F03.expected_back: Nevada's minimum liability coverage is twenty-five thousand dollars for injury or death of one person in a crash and fifty thousand dollars for injury or death of two or more people in one crash.

sec11-card-sec11-F04.front: What minimum dollar amount of property-damage liability must a Nevada policy include per crash?
sec11-card-sec11-F04.expected_back: Nevada's minimum liability coverage also includes twenty thousand dollars for damage to or destruction of other people's property in any one crash.

sec11-card-sec11-F05.front: What does Nevada's electronic liability insurance verification system do behind the scenes?
sec11-card-sec11-F05.expected_back: NV LIVE, the Nevada Liability Insurance Validation Electronically program, works with licensed insurers to flag registrations whose insurance has ended or lapsed.

sec11-card-sec11-F06.front: What fee and fine range hit when a registration is suspended for an unreplaced insurance lapse?
sec11-card-sec11-F06.expected_back: If a registration is suspended for an insurance lapse with no replacement coverage for that period, you pay a reinstatement fee plus fines starting at two hundred fifty dollars and reaching up to one thousand seven hundred fifty dollars for each vehicle on that policy.

sec11-card-sec11-R03.front: If a lapsed insurance policy covered three family cars, how are Nevada's lapse fines charged?
sec11-card-sec11-R03.expected_back: Lapse fines and the reinstatement fee apply to each registered vehicle that the lapsed policy covered.

sec11-card-sec11-F07.front: Beyond registration fines, what two license or insurance penalties can follow a coverage lapse?
sec11-card-sec11-F07.expected_back: Further penalties for an insurance lapse can include an SR-twenty-two requirement, a thirty-day driver license suspension, or both.

sec11-card-sec11-F08.front: How does crash and insurance info reach the state licensing agency when police investigate at the scene?
sec11-card-sec11-F08.expected_back: When law enforcement investigates a crash, the officer sends your insurance information and a description of the damage or injuries to the DMV.

sec11-card-sec11-F09.front: When police do not investigate at the scene, what damage or injury threshold triggers a ten-day state crash report?
sec11-card-sec11-F09.memory_hook: Seven-fifty damage or injury, ten days
sec11-card-sec11-F09.expected_back: If police do not investigate a crash that causes seven hundred fifty dollars or more in damage or injures anyone, you must send a Report of Crash Form, the SR-one, to the DMV within ten days.

sec11-card-sec11-R02.front: How does crash reporting differ when an officer investigates versus when no officer responds?
sec11-card-sec11-R02.expected_back: A police-investigated crash reaches the DMV through the officer's report, while a crash without police investigation that injures anyone or causes seven hundred fifty dollars or more in damage needs your own SR-one within ten days.

sec11-card-sec11-F10.front: Who must complete the state Report of Crash form, and where can you obtain a copy?
sec11-card-sec11-F10.memory_hook: Drivers or owners; state, police, online
sec11-card-sec11-F10.expected_back: The SR-one must be completed by anyone who was the driver or the registered owner of a vehicle in the crash, and the form is available at DMV offices, the Nevada Highway Patrol, local police and the DMV website.

sec11-card-sec11-F11.front: Which three questions does the state Financial Responsibility Section decide after a reported crash?
sec11-card-sec11-F11.expected_back: After a crash, the DMV Financial Responsibility Section decides who was at fault, whether every vehicle and driver was insured, and the total liability.

sec11-card-sec11-F12.front: What three consequences face an uninsured driver found at fault in a Nevada crash?
sec11-card-sec11-F12.expected_back: An at-fault driver without liability insurance may have the license or registration suspended, must post a deposit with the DMV to cover crash costs, or must arrange payment with the other parties.

sec11-card-sec11-F13.front: What happens if you ignore your legal duty to report a qualifying crash to the state?
sec11-card-sec11-F13.expected_back: Failing to report a crash to the DMV can lead to suspension of your driver license, your vehicle registration, or both.

sec11-card-sec11-F14.front: What is Nevada's state-monitored reinstatement proof-of-insurance certificate, and how does it work?
sec11-card-sec11-F14.expected_back: An SR-twenty-two is liability insurance on a driver license that lets the DMV monitor the insurance of a suspended or revoked driver through reports from the insurer, and it may be required for reinstatement.

sec11-card-sec11-F15.front: When does monitored reinstatement coverage actually begin, how often do you file it, and when should you buy it?
sec11-card-sec11-F15.expected_back: SR-twenty-two coverage starts when you actually reinstate, you file the form only once, and you should not buy it until every other reinstatement requirement is met.

sec11-card-sec11-R04.front: How does Nevada's crash-reporting form differ from its monitored proof-of-insurance filing?
sec11-card-sec11-R04.expected_back: The SR-one is a crash report you file, while the SR-twenty-two is proof-of-insurance coverage that the DMV monitors when reinstating a suspended or revoked driver.

sec11-card-sec11-R05.front: Who determines how much monitored reinstatement insurance coverage costs?
sec11-card-sec11-R05.expected_back: The price of SR-twenty-two coverage depends on how the insurance company structures it.

sec11-card-sec11-F16.front: Which four actions come first whenever you are involved in a crash?
sec11-card-sec11-F16.memory_hook: Stop, aid injured, warn, call police
sec11-card-sec11-F16.expected_back: At a crash, stop, get medical help for anyone injured, warn traffic and notify law enforcement.

sec11-card-sec11-F17.front: What should you do with drivable cars after a property-damage-only fender bender with zero injuries?
sec11-card-sec11-F17.expected_back: In a fender bender with only property damage and no injuries, move the vehicle if it can be moved safely to a spot that does not block traffic, then return to the scene.

sec11-card-sec11-R06.front: How do your opening steps differ between an injury crash and a minor drivable fender bender?
sec11-card-sec11-R06.memory_hook: Injuries get aid; property clears lanes
sec11-card-sec11-R06.expected_back: If a crash involves injuries, the first duties are to stop, get medical help and warn traffic; the move-it-aside rule covers a fender bender with property damage only and a vehicle that can be moved safely.

sec11-card-sec11-F18.front: Which five pieces of identification and vehicle data must drivers exchange after a crash?
sec11-card-sec11-F18.expected_back: Exchange your name, address, driver license number, registration and insurance information with every other driver involved.

sec11-card-sec11-F19.front: What must you do if you bump an unattended parked vehicle or roadside property?
sec11-card-sec11-F19.memory_hook: Give owner or leave five details
sec11-card-sec11-F19.expected_back: If you hit an unattended vehicle or other property, give the owner your name, address, license number, registration and insurance details, in person or in a note left behind.

sec11-card-sec11-F20.front: How does Nevada classify a driver license, and what happens if you stop driving safely?
sec11-card-sec11-F20.expected_back: A Nevada driver license is a privilege, and it can be suspended, revoked or canceled if you stop driving safely and obeying the rules.

sec11-card-sec11-F21.front: What events post to your Nevada driving record—and do tickets from other states follow you home?
sec11-card-sec11-F21.expected_back: Crashes and traffic convictions go on your driving record, including violations committed in other states.

sec11-card-sec11-F22.front: How many years do ordinary tickets stay reportable to insurers versus impaired-driving convictions on your record?
sec11-card-sec11-F22.expected_back: Most violations can be reported to your insurer for three years, while convictions related to driving under the influence stay on the record for seven years.

sec11-card-sec11-R07.front: How do the three-year and seven-year retention timelines compare on a Nevada driving history?
sec11-card-sec11-R07.expected_back: Most violations stay reportable to insurers for three years, while DUI-related convictions stay on the record for seven years.

sec11-card-sec11-F23.front: When do demerit points land on your Nevada record, and across what rolling time window are they tallied?
sec11-card-sec11-F23.expected_back: Every traffic violation carries demerit points, added once a court sends the DMV notice of a conviction or civil infraction, and points are counted over a twelve-month period.

sec11-card-sec11-F24.front: How many demerit points collected inside twelve months trigger automatic license suspension?
sec11-card-sec11-F24.expected_back: Receiving twelve or more demerit points in any twelve-month period means your license will be suspended.

sec11-card-sec11-F25.front: When can an approved traffic safety course shave demerit points, how many come off, and how often?
sec11-card-sec11-F25.expected_back: With three to eleven points, completing a DMV-approved traffic safety course removes up to three points, but only once in any twelve-month period, and the conviction itself stays in your driving history.

sec11-card-sec11-R09.front: When do traffic-school point reductions actually take effect, and does the state warn risky drivers?
sec11-card-sec11-R09.expected_back: Points from traffic school are removed only when the school reports your completion for credit, and the DMV will notify you if unsafe driving puts your license status in jeopardy.

sec11-card-sec11-F26.front: Why do major convictions like impaired driving or causing substantial bodily harm carry zero demerit points?
sec11-card-sec11-F26.expected_back: A conviction for a major offense such as DUI or causing substantial bodily harm revokes the license; these offenses carry no demerit points.

sec11-card-sec11-R08.front: How does a twelve-point demerit suspension differ from a major-offense revocation?
sec11-card-sec11-R08.expected_back: Points-based suspension comes from reaching twelve points within twelve months, while revocation follows a single major conviction such as DUI that carries no points at all.

sec11-card-sec11-F27.front: How many demerit points hit for reckless driving versus careless driving or failing to render crash aid?
sec11-card-sec11-F27.memory_hook: Reckless eight; careless or hit-and-run six
sec11-card-sec11-F27.expected_back: Demerit points: reckless driving is eight points, and careless driving or failing to give information or render aid at a crash scene is six points.

sec11-card-sec11-R10.front: How do the Nevada demerit-point values of reckless driving and careless driving compare?
sec11-card-sec11-R10.expected_back: Reckless driving carries eight demerit points while careless driving carries six.

sec11-card-sec11-F28.front: Which four everyday tailgating, right-of-way, pedestrian, and red-light violations cost four points each?
sec11-card-sec11-F28.expected_back: Demerit points: following too closely, failing to yield the right-of-way, failing to yield to a pedestrian, and disobeying a traffic signal or stop sign are four points each.

sec11-card-sec11-F29.front: Which three slow-driving, headlight, and weather-speed violations carry two demerit points each?
sec11-card-sec11-F29.expected_back: Demerit points: impeding traffic or driving too slowly, failing to dim headlights, and a prima facie speed violation or driving too fast for conditions are two points each.

sec11-card-sec11-R11.front: Which speeding bracket matches the two-point penalty for driving too fast for conditions?
sec11-card-sec11-R11.expected_back: A prima facie speed violation or driving too fast for conditions costs two points, the same as speeding eleven to twenty miles per hour over the limit.

sec11-card-sec11-F30.front: How do Nevada speeding points climb by ten-mile-per-hour brackets from one over up past forty-one over?
sec11-card-sec11-F30.expected_back: Speeding points rise with speed over the limit: one to ten miles per hour over is one point, eleven to twenty is two points, twenty-one to thirty is three points, thirty-one to forty is four points, and forty-one miles per hour or more is five points.

sec11-card-sec11-R12.front: Is the handbook's point chart exhaustive, and how do commercial license holders fare?
sec11-card-sec11-R12.expected_back: The point list is only partial, and holders of a commercial driver license may face extra penalties and points for some violations.

sec11-card-sec11-R13.front: What can you check for free by setting up an online account on the state licensing website?
sec11-card-sec11-R13.expected_back: A free online account through the DMV website shows license status and expiration, a driver history printout, and full lists of demerit points, violation codes and court details.

sec11-card-sec11-F31.front: Which four dishonest acts involving a Nevada driver license or application are illegal?
sec11-card-sec11-F31.expected_back: It is illegal to give false information on a Nevada license application, to alter your license, to lend it to anyone, or to use another person's license.

sec01-card-sec01-F01.front: Who must hold a Nevada driver license to drive on state roads, and which two groups are exempt?
sec01-card-sec01-F01.expected_back: Anyone who lives or works in Nevada and wants to drive on its streets and highways needs a Nevada license; employees from border states and military members stationed in Nevada are the stated exceptions.

sec01-card-sec01-F02.front: How many days after becoming a Nevada resident do you have to apply for a state driver license?
sec01-card-sec01-F02.expected_back: Someone who moves to Nevada from another state has thirty days after becoming a resident to apply for a Nevada driver license.

sec01-card-sec01-F03.front: What minimum age, office visit, and four personal proofs are required to apply for a standard Nevada license?
sec01-card-sec01-F03.expected_back: An applicant fills out an application, visits a full-service DMV office, must be at least sixteen years old, and proves full legal name, age, Nevada residency and a Social Security Number if one was ever issued.

sec01-card-sec01-F04.front: Is a Social Security Number required when applying for a Nevada Driver Authorization Card?
sec01-card-sec01-F04.expected_back: A Social Security Number is not needed to get a Driver Authorization Card (DAC).

sec01-card-sec01-F05.front: How long does a first-time Nevada license last for an applicant under sixty-five, and what shortens that term?
sec01-card-sec01-F05.expected_back: A first-time Nevada driver license for someone under sixty-five runs eight years ending on the birthday, unless limited-term immigration documents set expiration to the DHS-verified departure date or one year if DHS gives no date.

sec01-card-sec01-F06.front: When does a Nevada license expire if limited-term immigration papers proved your name and birth date?
sec01-card-sec01-F06.expected_back: If limited-term immigration documents were used as proof of name and birth date, the license expires on the departure date verified electronically by DHS, or after one year when DHS supplies no date.

sec01-card-sec01-F07.front: What is the maximum number of years any Nevada driver license or ID card may remain valid?
sec01-card-sec01-F07.expected_back: Under NRS four hundred eighty-three point two nine zero a Nevada driver license or identification card can never be valid for longer than eight years.

sec01-card-sec01-F08.front: How does card validity differ between a driver license and an ID card for Nevadans aged sixty-five and older?
sec01-card-sec01-F08.expected_back: Licenses for drivers aged sixty-five and older are valid for four years, while identification cards are valid for eight years.

sec01-card-sec01-F09.front: Who must co-sign a license application for someone under eighteen, and what legal responsibility do they take on?
sec01-card-sec01-F09.expected_back: An applicant under eighteen needs a co-signer (a custodial parent, a legal guardian or another person allowed by NRS four hundred eighty-three point three zero zero), and that co-signer shares liability for damage the minor causes by negligent or willful driving.

sec01-card-sec01-R01.front: Compare standard validity periods for an under-sixty-five license, a sixty-five-plus license, and a Nevada ID card?
sec01-card-sec01-R01.expected_back: A first-time license for someone under sixty-five runs eight years unless limited-term immigration documents set a shorter expiration, a license for someone sixty-five or older runs four years, and an identification card runs eight years.

sec01-card-sec01-R02.front: How does the Social Security proof rule contrast between a standard license and a Driver Authorization Card?
sec01-card-sec01-R02.expected_back: A driver license applicant must prove a Social Security Number if one was issued, but a Driver Authorization Card applicant needs no Social Security Number at all.

sec01-card-sec01-F10.front: How many driver licenses or ID cards may a Nevada resident hold, and what happens to your old out-of-state card?
sec01-card-sec01-F10.expected_back: A Nevada resident may hold only one driver license or ID card, so a card from another state, US territory or foreign country must be surrendered; it is voided and handed back.

sec01-card-sec01-F11.front: Which exam must every new Nevada resident take, and when can the remaining tests be waived?
sec01-card-sec01-F11.expected_back: A new resident always takes the vision test, and the other tests can be waived only when every one of the listed transfer conditions is met.

sec01-card-sec01-F12.front: What ticket limit and license-status history must a new resident show to qualify for a test waiver?
sec01-card-sec01-F12.expected_back: Waiver condition: fewer than three moving violations in the past four years, and no suspension, revocation or cancellation of the license.

sec01-card-sec01-F13.front: How far back must a transferring resident's record stay free of DUI convictions to waive extra testing?
sec01-card-sec01-F13.expected_back: Waiver condition: no DUI conviction within the past seven years.

sec01-card-sec01-F14.front: What restriction rule, license-class match, and minimum age finish the new-resident test-waiver checklist?
sec01-card-sec01-F14.expected_back: Waiver conditions: no restriction on the driving privilege that calls for an evaluation, a valid out-of-state license of the same class being applied for, and an age of twenty-one or older.

sec01-card-sec01-F15.front: Must an active-duty US service member stationed in Nevada obtain a Nevada license if holding a valid home-state card?
sec01-card-sec01-F15.expected_back: An active-duty member of the US Armed Forces who holds a valid home-state license does not need a Nevada license.

sec01-card-sec01-F16.front: Under what three conditions may tourists, out-of-state students, and seasonal residents drive here without a Nevada license?
sec01-card-sec01-F16.expected_back: Non-residents such as out-of-state students, tourists and seasonal residents may drive in Nevada without a Nevada license if they are at least sixteen, hold a valid home-state license and obey Nevada traffic and financial responsibility laws.

sec01-card-sec01-F17.front: Which two national databases screen every applicant, and what happens if another state blocked your driving privilege?
sec01-card-sec01-F17.expected_back: Every driver record is run through two national databases, the Problem Driver Pointer System and the CDL Information System, and a privilege suspended, revoked, canceled or denied elsewhere blocks a Nevada license until that issue is cleared, though an ID card may still be possible meanwhile.

sec01-card-sec01-R03.front: Between vision, knowledge, and road exams, which is never waived for new residents and which can be?
sec01-card-sec01-R03.expected_back: The vision test is always given to a new resident, while the knowledge and road tests may be waived only when all of the transfer conditions hold.

sec01-card-sec01-R04.front: How does the rule for active-duty military drivers compare with the rule for visiting students or tourists?
sec01-card-sec01-R04.expected_back: An active-duty service member needs only a valid home-state license, while a non-resident student, tourist or seasonal resident must also be at least sixteen and follow Nevada traffic and financial responsibility laws.

sec01-card-sec01-F18.front: What document standard proves full legal name and birth date, and what are common examples?
sec01-card-sec01-F18.expected_back: Proof of full legal name and date of birth is one unexpired original or certified document, for example a state-issued birth certificate, a valid US passport or passport card, a Consular Report of Birth Abroad (FS-two hundred forty), or another state's license, permit or ID bearing a DHS-approved Real ID mark.

sec01-card-sec01-F19.front: Where does a Nevada Department of Corrections ID card work as identity proof, and where does it fall short?
sec01-card-sec01-F19.expected_back: A Nevada Department of Corrections ID card can prove name and birth date, but not for a Real ID.

sec01-card-sec01-F20.front: Does another state's Real ID marked limited term count as proof of name and birth date in Nevada?
sec01-card-sec01-F20.expected_back: An out-of-state Real ID marked limited term does not prove name and birth date; acceptable immigration documents have to be shown instead.

sec01-card-sec01-F21.front: Which common certificates and non-Nevada cards are rejected as proof of legal name and age?
sec01-card-sec01-F21.expected_back: These do not prove name and age: a hospital-issued birth certificate, a license or ID from another US state, territory or foreign country, a foreign birth certificate, a Border Crossing Card or a Consular Identification Card.

sec01-card-sec01-F22.front: What must you bring if your current legal name no longer matches your primary birth or identity record?
sec01-card-sec01-F22.expected_back: When your current name differs from your identity document, bring legal proof of the change such as a marriage certificate, a divorce decree that mentions the name change, a spouse's death certificate, an adoption record or a court order, as an original or certified copy.

sec01-card-sec01-R05.front: Contrast a Nevada Corrections ID card against an out-of-state limited-term Real ID as identity proof?
sec01-card-sec01-R05.expected_back: A Nevada Department of Corrections ID card proves name and birth date for a standard card but not for Real ID, while another state's limited-term Real ID proves neither.

sec01-card-sec01-R06.front: Which older Resident Alien Card version does the Nevada DMV accept, and which versions are refused?
sec01-card-sec01-R06.expected_back: An old Resident Alien Card printed with no expiration date is accepted as a Permanent Resident Card; any other version of the Resident Alien Card is refused as proof of name, birth date or lawful status.

sec01-card-sec01-R07.front: Will the Nevada DMV force holders of an undated Resident Alien Card to replace it on their own?
sec01-card-sec01-R07.expected_back: The DMV will not force holders of the undated card to replace it unless DHS requests it, and the card rules may change with Department of Homeland Security policy.

sec01-card-sec01-R08.front: What companion document must accompany an expired I-ninety-four form at the DMV?
sec01-card-sec01-R08.expected_back: An expired I-ninety-four, whether with a permanent-resident passport stamp or with a US visa, must be paired with a Notice of Action (I-seven hundred ninety-seven) that shows an approved extension.

sec01-card-sec01-R09.front: What label goes onto a Nevada card issued from temporary work papers, and how are immigration papers checked?
sec01-card-sec01-R09.expected_back: Limited-term documents such as an Employment Authorization Card (I-seven hundred sixty-six) produce a card marked Limited Term, and every immigration document is electronically checked for lawful status.

sec01-card-sec01-F23.front: Which original records prove your Social Security Number, and what kind of paystub is rejected?
sec01-card-sec01-F23.expected_back: Proof of Social Security Number is a Social Security card, a W-two or IRS Form one thousand ninety-nine showing the full number, or a paystub with full legal name; handwritten paystubs are refused and every document must be an original showing the complete number.

sec01-card-sec01-F24.front: What special sign-off do alternative identity or SSN documents need, and what card can they never support?
sec01-card-sec01-F24.expected_back: Alternative documents for name, age and Social Security Number need supervisory approval and can never be used to issue a Real ID card.

sec01-card-sec01-R15.front: What formatting and certification rules apply when submitting a translated document at the DMV?
sec01-card-sec01-R15.expected_back: Translated documents must cover the entire original, be typed or printed electronically, and carry a signed statement in which the translator certifies the translation is complete and accurate and that they are fluent in both languages.

sec01-card-sec01-F25.front: What visual marking sets a Nevada Real ID apart from a standard Nevada license or ID?
sec01-card-sec01-F25.expected_back: A Real ID license or ID shows a gold Nevada outline with a star cutout, while a standard card carries the words NOT FOR REAL ID PURPOSES.

sec01-card-sec01-F26.front: Between which two card tiers may eligible Nevada applicants choose, and what five items must the DMV verify?
sec01-card-sec01-F26.expected_back: Nevada applicants may choose either a Real ID compliant card or a standard card, and the DMV must verify identity, birth date, Social Security Number, lawful status and primary residential address.

sec01-card-sec01-F27.front: How many residency documents must a Real ID applicant bring, and what examples qualify?
sec01-card-sec01-F27.expected_back: A Real ID applicant presents two documents proving Nevada residency that show the correct residential address, such as utility bills, mortgage statements, rental agreements or bank statements.

sec01-card-sec01-R10.front: How do a Real ID card and a standard card differ in printed markings and federal compliance?
sec01-card-sec01-R10.expected_back: A Real ID card has the gold Nevada outline and star cutout and meets federal standards, while a standard card says NOT FOR REAL ID PURPOSES and does not.

sec01-card-sec01-R11.front: How are alternative identity documents treated for a standard card compared with a Real ID card?
sec01-card-sec01-R11.expected_back: Alternative identity documents can support a standard card with supervisory approval but are never accepted for a Real ID card.

sec01-card-sec01-R12.front: What security goals drove Congress to pass the Real ID Act?
sec01-card-sec01-R12.expected_back: The Real ID Act of May two thousand five aims to fight terrorism, identity theft and other crimes by tightening the security of state-issued identification.

sec01-card-sec01-R13.front: What paperwork must a current standard Nevada license holder bring to upgrade to Real ID, and how is it handled?
sec01-card-sec01-R13.expected_back: A standard Nevada license holder who upgrades to Real ID must again show documents for name, birth date, Social Security Number and Nevada residential address, and they may be scanned, stored and electronically verified.

sec01-card-sec01-F28.front: How long does a Driver Authorization Card last, when must you carry it, and how are updates handled?
sec01-card-sec01-F28.expected_back: A Driver Authorization Card is valid for four years, expires on the holder's birthday and must be carried whenever the holder drives; renewals and address changes are done in person only.

sec01-card-sec01-F29.front: Which single identity records allow an applicant to qualify on the one-document list for a DAC?
sec01-card-sec01-F29.expected_back: For a DAC you may show one document from the main identity list, or one of a US military ID, a US military dependent ID, a US Armed Forces discharge document or a US Certificate of Degree of Indian Blood.

sec01-card-sec01-F30.front: If not using a single primary record, how many documents from the secondary foreign or out-of-state list establish DAC identity?
sec01-card-sec01-F30.expected_back: A DAC applicant may instead show two documents from a second list: a license, ID or DAC from another state, DC or a US territory, a foreign passport, a foreign birth certificate, a Mexican Federal Electoral Card, a Consular Identification Card or a similar foreign-government document.
