sec01-card-sec01-F31.front: For what official purposes can a Driver Authorization Card not be used, and how is application data protected?
sec01-card-sec01-F31.expected_back: A DAC is not valid for federal or state identification and cannot establish eligibility for Nevada benefits, licenses or services, and DAC application information is not used to decide legal presence or immigration status.

sec01-card-sec01-R14.front: How does a Driver Authorization Card function behind the wheel versus at an ID check?
sec01-card-sec01-R14.expected_back: A Driver Authorization Card works like a license for driving and follows the same rules unless the handbook says otherwise, yet it cannot serve as identification for any federal or state purpose.

sec01-card-sec01-F32.front: Which original Nevada card, permit, or license applicants must prove a physical Nevada residential address?
sec01-card-sec01-F32.expected_back: Applicants for an original Real ID or standard ID card, instruction permit or driver license must prove a Nevada residential address, and DAC applicants must do so at original issuance.

sec01-card-sec01-F33.front: How many residency documents are needed, and what dating rules govern the two document groups?
sec01-card-sec01-F33.expected_back: Residency is proven with originals or certified copies of any two listed documents showing a Nevada residential address; one group of documents must be dated within sixty days, the other group may be the last one issued.

sec01-card-sec01-F34.front: When can a hotel, motel, RV park, or campground receipt count toward proving Nevada residency?
sec01-card-sec01-F34.expected_back: A hotel, motel, RV park or campground record counts as residency proof only if it shows at least thirty consecutive days of living in Nevada.

sec01-card-sec01-F35.front: What two options let a parent or guardian prove Nevada residency for an applicant under eighteen?
sec01-card-sec01-F35.expected_back: For an applicant under eighteen, a parent or guardian can prove the applicant's residence with two listed documents or by signing a DMV-approved form confirming they share the same address.

sec01-card-sec01-R16.front: Which three department-approved DMV forms can establish Nevada residency in special living situations?
sec01-card-sec01-R16.expected_back: The three department-approved residency forms are the Relief Agency or Shelter Certification (DMV one hundred fifteen), the Property Owner Residency Affidavit (DMV one hundred sixteen) and the Certification of Nevada Residency (DMV five).

sec01-card-sec01-R17.front: Which homeowner statement and election record appear on Nevada's acceptable residency document list?
sec01-card-sec01-R17.expected_back: A notarized statement from the owner of the home saying the applicant physically lives there is one of the listed residency documents, as is a voter registration card from a county clerk or the county registrar of voters.

sec01-card-sec01-F36.front: What gets added to your Nevada license if you need glasses or contacts to pass the DMV eye screening?
sec01-card-sec01-F36.expected_back: If you need glasses or contact lenses to meet the vision standard, a restriction is placed on your license.

sec01-card-sec01-F37.front: What three subject areas does the Nevada knowledge test cover, and what testing formats or languages exist?
sec01-card-sec01-F37.expected_back: The knowledge test checks highway signs and markings, traffic laws and safe driving practices on automated equipment or paper; an oral exam can be requested and Basic Class C testing is also offered in Spanish.

sec01-card-sec01-F38.front: How much does Nevada charge for initial knowledge and skills testing versus each retest before issuance?
sec01-card-sec01-F38.expected_back: Initial knowledge and skills tests carry a twenty-five dollars fee, and each retest needed before the license is issued costs ten dollars.

sec01-card-sec01-F39.front: Which paperwork and ten equipment items does the DMV examiner inspect before your road test starts?
sec01-card-sec01-F39.expected_back: Before the road test the examiner checks the registration and plates, proof of insurance, headlights, taillights, brake lights, turn signals, horn, seat belts, tires and windshield wipers.

sec01-card-sec01-F40.front: What mechanical and cabin standards must a road-test car meet, and who may ride along?
sec01-card-sec01-F40.expected_back: The test vehicle must be safe with working brakes, speedometer and muffler and a clean, safe seat for the examiner, and no passengers or animals may ride along.

sec01-card-sec01-F41.front: Which core driving maneuvers does the road examiner grade, and what happens if you break a traffic law?
sec01-card-sec01-F41.expected_back: The road test scores how you prepare, control the car, enter traffic, use lanes, control speed, turn, park, back up, stop, pass and watch traffic, and you may be asked to stop on a grade; breaking a traffic law during the test is penalized.

sec01-card-sec01-F42.front: What happens if you touch a cell phone during the Nevada drive test, and which electronic aids are banned?
sec01-card-sec01-F42.expected_back: Using a cell phone during the drive test is an automatic failure, and aids such as parking assist and cruise control may not be used.

sec03-card-sec03-F01.front: How does the Nevada handbook rate seat belts for crash survival, and is wearing one optional?
sec03-card-sec03-F01.expected_back: Nevada calls seat belts your best protection against injury or death in a crash, and wearing them is required by law, not just advised.

sec03-card-sec03-F02.front: In the twenty-twenty crash data cited by the Nevada handbook, what percentage of highway fatalities were unbelted drivers?
sec03-card-sec03-F02.expected_back: In two thousand twenty, drivers who were not wearing seat belts made up twenty-three point zero three percent of Nevada highway fatalities, an increase of one point one five percent over two thousand sixteen.

sec03-card-sec03-F03.front: How many unbelted vehicle occupants died in Nevada across the five-year span from twenty-sixteen to twenty-twenty?
sec03-card-sec03-F03.expected_back: From two thousand sixteen to two thousand twenty, three hundred forty-five unbelted vehicle occupants were killed in Nevada.

sec03-card-sec03-F04.front: What seat-belt equipment must any passenger car from model year nineteen sixty-eight or newer carry?
sec03-card-sec03-F04.expected_back: A car of model year nineteen sixty-eight or newer must have lap-type seat belts for the front-seat passengers.

sec03-card-sec03-F05.front: Which seat belts and harnesses are required in cars from model year nineteen seventy or newer?
sec03-card-sec03-F05.expected_back: A car of model year nineteen seventy or newer must have lap-type belts for every passenger plus shoulder harnesses for the front seat.

sec03-card-sec03-R03.front: How did mandatory seat-belt equipment expand from model year nineteen sixty-eight to nineteen seventy?
sec03-card-sec03-R03.expected_back: Model year nineteen sixty-eight brought lap belts for front-seat passengers, while model year nineteen seventy brought lap belts for every passenger and front-seat shoulder harnesses.

sec03-card-sec03-F06.front: Beginning at what passenger age must everyone wear a safety belt whenever the seat has one?
sec03-card-sec03-F06.expected_back: The driver and every passenger aged six or older must wear a safety belt whenever the vehicle has one.

sec03-card-sec03-F07.front: What age threshold and height threshold require a child to ride in an approved child restraint system in Nevada?
sec03-card-sec03-F07.expected_back: Children under six, and children shorter than fifty-seven inches, must ride in an approved child restraint system (NRS 484B point one five seven).

sec03-card-sec03-F08.front: What penalties can a driver face for failing to secure a young or short child in an approved restraint?
sec03-card-sec03-F08.expected_back: Failing to restrain a child under six or under fifty-seven inches can lead to fines, community service, a license suspension, or a combination of these.

sec03-card-sec03-R04.front: How can breaking Nevada's child-restraint law directly threaten the driver's own license?
sec03-card-sec03-R04.expected_back: For children, the restraint law reaches the driver's license itself, since failing to restrain a young child can bring a license suspension as well as fines or community service.

sec03-card-sec03-F09.front: Where and facing which direction must a child under age two ride in Nevada?
sec03-card-sec03-F09.expected_back: A child under two must ride in a rear-facing child restraint system in the back seat.

sec03-card-sec03-F10.front: Which two dangerous belt or lap shortcuts must you never use with a child passenger?
sec03-card-sec03-F10.expected_back: Never hold a child on your lap or share one safety belt between a child and another person.

sec03-card-sec03-R01.front: What transitions happen at age two, age six, and fifty-seven inches under Nevada restraint law?
sec03-card-sec03-R01.expected_back: Age two marks the rear-facing back-seat rule, age six marks both the start of the adult belt requirement and the end of the under-six restraint rule, though a child still under fifty-seven inches keeps needing a restraint.

sec03-card-sec03-F11.front: When is it illegal to leave a child aged seven or younger inside a vehicle, and what supervisor age changes that?
sec03-card-sec03-F11.expected_back: Do not leave a child aged seven or younger alone in a vehicle when conditions pose a significant risk to the child's health and safety, unless a person at least twelve years old is supervising within sight (NRS two hundred two point four eight five).

sec03-card-sec03-F12.front: What does Nevada law state about leaving dogs or cats in extreme temperatures, and what can responders do?
sec03-card-sec03-F12.expected_back: Leaving a dog or cat unattended in a vehicle during extreme heat or cold is illegal, and police officers, firefighters and other officials are allowed to use reasonable force to free the animal (NRS two hundred two point four eight seven).

sec03-card-sec03-F13.front: What criminal classification applies to violating Nevada's unattended-child or unattended-pet vehicle laws?
sec03-card-sec03-F13.expected_back: Breaking the unattended-child or unattended-pet law is a misdemeanor.

sec03-card-sec03-R02.front: Which two specific age cutoffs define Nevada's unattended-child-in-vehicle rule?
sec03-card-sec03-R02.expected_back: When conditions pose a significant risk to a child's health and safety, a child aged seven or younger cannot be left unattended in a vehicle unless supervised within sight by someone at least twelve years old.

sec03-card-sec03-R05.front: How does the legal trigger for leaving a young child unattended differ from the trigger for a dog or cat?
sec03-card-sec03-R05.expected_back: The unattended-child rule turns on significant risk to the child's health and safety, while the dog-or-cat rule turns on extreme heat or cold; both are misdemeanors.

sec03-card-sec03-F14.front: What physical job do booster seats and belt-positioning seats perform for growing children?
sec03-card-sec03-F14.expected_back: Booster seats and belt-positioning seats raise or position a child so the vehicle's seat belt can secure the child safely.

sec03-card-sec03-F15.front: What federal approval and fit checks should you verify on a child seat before driving?
sec03-card-sec03-F15.expected_back: Before travelling with a child, check that the restraint is approved by the US Department of Transportation under the Federal Motor Vehicle Safety Standards and suits the child's size and weight.

sec03-card-sec03-F16.front: Whose instructions or approved methods must you follow when installing a child restraint?
sec03-card-sec03-F16.expected_back: A child restraint must be installed safely and securely, following the manufacturer's instructions or another method approved by NHTSA.

sec03-card-sec03-F17.front: Which direction must infants always face in a car, and what parts of the body does that protect?
sec03-card-sec03-F17.expected_back: Infants are always buckled in facing the rear, because a rear-facing seat supports the baby's head and shields the neck and spine in most crashes.

sec03-card-sec03-R07.front: How does a booster seat secure a child differently than a rear-facing infant seat?
sec03-card-sec03-R07.expected_back: A booster or belt-positioning seat works with the vehicle's own seat belt, while a rear-facing seat holds the infant itself and protects the head, neck and spine.

sec03-card-sec03-R08.front: What three essential checks guarantee safe child-restraint travel on every trip?
sec03-card-sec03-R08.expected_back: Safe child travel needs three checks: a DOT-approved restraint, a seat that fits the child's size and weight, and an installation that follows the manufacturer or NHTSA.

sec03-card-sec03-F18.front: Where is the safest place for children to ride, and how should the seat be set if an older child must ride up front?
sec03-card-sec03-F18.expected_back: The back seat is generally the safest place for children; an older child who must ride in front should have the vehicle seat moved as far back as it goes.

sec03-card-sec03-F19.front: What restraint setup keeps a child's head back out of an inflating airbag's path?
sec03-card-sec03-F19.expected_back: To keep a child's head away from an inflating airbag, use a restraint with a full harness or a properly fitted shoulder and lap belt.

sec03-card-sec03-F20.front: Which passengers can suffer severe airbag injuries even during a minor fender-bender or sudden stop?
sec03-card-sec03-F20.expected_back: Passengers who are unbuckled or sitting too close to an airbag can be badly hurt even in a minor collision or a sudden stop.

sec03-card-sec03-F21.front: Why must a rear-facing infant never be placed in front of an active passenger-side airbag?
sec03-card-sec03-F21.expected_back: Never place an infant in the front seat of a car that has a passenger-side airbag, because the airbag bursts out of the dashboard at two hundred miles per hour and can strike the back of the baby's head through the safety seat.

sec03-card-sec03-R06.front: Contrast front-seat airbag rules for an older child when necessary versus an infant?
sec03-card-sec03-R06.expected_back: Older children may ride up front only when necessary and with the seat pushed fully back, but an infant may never ride in front of a passenger-side airbag.

sec04-card-sec04-F02.front: How often should you inspect tire wear, and how does the penny test confirm safe tread depth?
sec04-card-sec04-F02.expected_back: Inspect tires for wear and damage once a month or before a long trip; in the penny test, if tread covers any part of Lincoln's head placed in the shallowest groove, the tread depth is safe, and less tread sharply cuts grip in bad conditions.

sec04-card-sec04-R01.front: What five checks and adjustments should you complete inside the cabin before starting the engine?
sec04-card-sec04-R01.expected_back: Before starting the engine, set the seat for a clear view and easy reach of every control, clean the windshield and windows, buckle up yourself and your passengers, check that you feel calm, and adjust the rear and side mirrors.

sec04-card-sec04-R02.front: Once the engine is running, what should you check and do before pulling into motion?
sec04-card-sec04-R02.expected_back: Once the engine runs, check the fuel gauge and warning lights, keep the stereo low enough to hear traffic, switch on headlights, signal or wipers if needed, and before moving stop, look and listen for traffic, cyclists and pedestrians.

sec04-card-sec04-F03.front: What three core functions do highway signs serve, and why are their shapes and colors standardized?
sec04-card-sec04-F03.expected_back: Signs serve three purposes, to regulate, to warn and to inform, and their shapes and colors carry set meanings so the message is read quickly.

sec04-card-sec04-F04.front: What traffic messages belong to red, green, yellow or yellow-green, and white sign backgrounds?
sec04-card-sec04-F04.memory_hook: Red stops, green guides, yellow warns
sec04-card-sec04-F04.expected_back: Sign colors: red means stop, no or do not; green gives direction or guidance; yellow or yellow-green is a general warning; white marks a regulation, law or rule.

sec04-card-sec04-F05.front: What do orange, blue, and brown highway sign colors each indicate?
sec04-card-sec04-F05.memory_hook: Orange work, blue services, brown parks
sec04-card-sec04-F05.expected_back: Sign colors: orange warns of road construction or repair, blue points to driver services such as food and lodging, and brown marks recreation and scenic information.

sec04-card-sec04-F06.front: What messages are carried by octagon, diamond, rectangle, and inverted-triangle sign shapes?
sec04-card-sec04-F06.memory_hook: Octagon stops, triangle yields, diamond warns
sec04-card-sec04-F06.expected_back: Sign shapes: an eight-sided octagon means stop, a diamond means warning, a rectangle gives regulations or directions, and an inverted triangle means yield right-of-way.

sec04-card-sec04-F07.front: What do pennant, pentagon, circle, crossbuck, and shield shapes each mean on the road?
sec04-card-sec04-F07.memory_hook: Pennant pass-ban, pentagon school, round rail
sec04-card-sec04-F07.expected_back: Sign shapes: a pennant means no passing, a five-sided pentagon marks school zones and crossings, a circle warns of a railroad crossing ahead, a crossbuck marks the crossing itself and a shield is a route marker.

sec04-card-sec04-R03.front: How does a round railroad sign differ in placement and meaning from an X-shaped crossbuck?
sec04-card-sec04-R03.expected_back: Both a circle and a crossbuck relate to trains, but the round sign warns that a crossing is ahead while the X-shaped crossbuck marks where the tracks actually are.

sec04-card-sec04-R04.front: Which sign shape marks school zones and crossings, and which marks no-passing zones?
sec04-card-sec04-R04.expected_back: A pentagon is the school-zone and school-crossing shape, whereas a pennant is the no-passing shape.

sec04-card-sec04-R06.front: What shape are route markers typically, and which three highway systems do they identify?
sec04-card-sec04-R06.expected_back: Route signs are usually shields, though shapes and colors differ, and they show US, Interstate and state route numbers.

sec04-card-sec04-F15.front: What shape are most work-zone signs, how must you drive through them, and how are tickets penalized?
sec04-card-sec04-F15.memory_hook: Orange diamonds, obey flaggers, higher fines
sec04-card-sec04-F15.expected_back: Most work-area signs are diamond-shaped; drivers must slow down and obey posted signs and any flaggers, and violations in work zones carry increased fines.

sec04-card-sec04-R10.front: What job do cones, drums, and barricades perform in construction zones day and night?
sec04-card-sec04-R10.expected_back: Cones, drums and barricades steer drivers through work areas and can carry warning lights for night work.

sec04-card-sec04-F08.front: Where must your wheels stop first at a stop sign, and how do you handle a blind cross street?
sec04-card-sec04-F08.expected_back: At a stop sign, stop completely behind the crosswalk or stop line, and if the cross street is hidden, ease forward slowly until you can tell it is safe.

sec04-card-sec04-F09.front: Where do you stop and whom do you yield to when a stop sign has no painted line or crosswalk?
sec04-card-sec04-F09.expected_back: Where no stop line or crosswalk exists, slow and stop if needed at the point closest to the intersection that gives a view of oncoming through traffic, then yield to pedestrians and cross traffic before going.

sec04-card-sec04-F10.front: Which vehicles take priority ahead of you when pulling up to a four-way stop?
sec04-card-sec04-F10.expected_back: At a four-way stop, wait for vehicles already in the intersection and let vehicles that arrived before you go first.

sec04-card-sec04-F11.front: How does a yield sign operate compared with a stop sign, and which four road users take priority?
sec04-card-sec04-F11.expected_back: A yield sign works like a stop sign except you may keep moving without a full stop when it is safe; slow down and yield to pedestrians, through traffic, drivers already on the highway and vehicles making a U-turn.

sec04-card-sec04-R05.front: What single requirement separates every stop sign from a yield sign when the intersection looks empty?
sec04-card-sec04-R05.expected_back: A stop sign always requires a full stop, while a yield sign requires slowing and yielding but lets you continue without stopping when the way is clear.

sec04-card-sec04-F12.front: What must you do when an emergency vehicle approaches running red lights and siren, and where must you never stop?
sec04-card-sec04-F12.expected_back: When a police car, fire engine, ambulance or other emergency vehicle approaches with its siren and red lights on, pull to the right edge and stop until it has passed, but never stop inside an intersection.

sec04-card-sec04-F16.front: How must you handle an intersection when all overhead traffic signals lose power and go dark?
sec04-card-sec04-F16.expected_back: When traffic lights are out, come to a full stop, yield to pedestrians and to vehicles already stopped or in the intersection, then proceed with caution.

sec04-card-sec04-F17.front: Where must you stop at a steady red light when not turning, and when may you move forward?
sec04-card-sec04-F17.expected_back: At a red light, stop completely behind the crosswalk or stop line, or before entering the intersection if neither exists, and stay stopped until the light turns green.

sec04-card-sec04-F18.front: Under what conditions may you turn right against a steady red traffic light in Nevada?
sec04-card-sec04-F18.expected_back: Unless a sign prohibits it, you may turn right on red after a complete stop, signalling first and waiting until vehicles and pedestrians are clear.

sec04-card-sec04-F19.front: How should you respond to a steady yellow light before versus after entering the intersection?
sec04-card-sec04-F19.memory_hook: Stop outside, clear inside, never race
sec04-card-sec04-F19.expected_back: A steady yellow light warns that red is coming: stop if you have not entered the intersection, keep going and clear it if you already have, and never speed up to beat the light.

sec04-card-sec04-F20.front: Which directions may you travel on a standard green light, and what limits that?
sec04-card-sec04-F20.expected_back: A green light allows going straight, turning right or turning left unless a sign forbids the turn.

sec04-card-sec04-F21.front: Contrast the required driver action at a flashing red light versus a flashing yellow light?
sec04-card-sec04-F21.expected_back: A flashing red light means a full stop and going only when the road is clear and you have the right-of-way, exactly like a stop sign, while a flashing yellow light means proceed with caution.

sec04-card-sec04-F22.front: What does a lit red arrow prohibit, and may you turn in that direction after stopping?
sec04-card-sec04-F22.expected_back: A red arrow forbids the movement it points to, and drivers facing it must stop unless they are entering for a movement another signal allows.

sec04-card-sec04-F23.front: How does a steady yellow arrow differ in meaning from a flashing yellow arrow?
sec04-card-sec04-F23.expected_back: A steady yellow arrow warns that the arrow is about to turn red and you should clear the intersection; a flashing yellow arrow lets you turn after yielding to oncoming traffic and pedestrians.

sec04-card-sec04-F24.front: What protection does a green arrow provide, and whom must you still yield to anyway?
sec04-card-sec04-F24.expected_back: A green arrow lets you go the way it points and protects the turn from other traffic, yet you must still yield to pedestrians, bicycles and vehicles already in the intersection.

sec04-card-sec04-F25.front: Under what exact street layout and steps is a left turn on a red light legal in Nevada?
sec04-card-sec04-F25.expected_back: A left turn on red is allowed only from a one-way street onto another one-way street whose traffic flows to the left, after signalling, stopping fully and yielding, unless a sign, arrow or officer forbids it.

sec04-card-sec04-R07.front: Distinguish a steady yellow ball, a flashing yellow ball, and a flashing yellow arrow?
sec04-card-sec04-R07.expected_back: A steady yellow light means stop if you can before entering, a flashing yellow light means go ahead with caution, and a flashing yellow arrow means turn only after yielding to oncoming traffic and pedestrians.

sec04-card-sec04-R08.front: Why is turning right on red common while turning left on red applies in only one street setup?
sec04-card-sec04-R08.expected_back: Right on red is allowed after a full stop wherever no sign forbids it, but left on red is allowed only from one one-way street onto another whose traffic flows left.

sec04-card-sec04-R09.front: What required action do a flashing red signal and a dark powerless traffic light share?
sec04-card-sec04-R09.expected_back: A flashing red light and a dark, non-working signal both call for a full stop before proceeding, the first treated exactly like a stop sign.

sec04-card-sec04-F26.front: When no separate pedestrian signal is present, how must walkers obey red, yellow, and green traffic lights?
sec04-card-sec04-F26.expected_back: Pedestrians at intersections must obey traffic signals: on red they do not cross, on yellow they must not start across, and on green they may cross, unless a pedestrian signal or officer directs otherwise.

sec04-card-sec04-F27.front: What does an illuminated WALK word or walking-person symbol require from nearby drivers?
sec04-card-sec04-F27.expected_back: A lit WALK sign or walking-person symbol lets pedestrians cross in the signal's direction, and the drivers of all vehicles must give them the right-of-way.

sec04-card-sec04-F28.front: In Nevada, how does a flashing upraised hand with a countdown timer differ from a flashing hand without numbers?
sec04-card-sec04-F28.expected_back: A flashing DON'T WALK or upraised hand with a countdown timer still lets pedestrians start, but they must finish crossing before the count reaches zero; without a countdown, a flashing hand means they may not start.

sec04-card-sec04-F29.front: What must pedestrians on the curb versus already in the street do when a steady DON'T WALK hand shows?
sec04-card-sec04-F29.expected_back: A steady DON'T WALK or upraised hand means no pedestrian may start crossing, and anyone already lawfully in the road must get to a curb, sidewalk, safety zone or other safe place as soon as possible.

sec04-card-sec04-R11.front: May a pedestrian step out on a green turn arrow alone, and what rule governs marked crosswalks?
sec04-card-sec04-R11.expected_back: Pedestrians facing a green turn arrow may not cross unless a pedestrian signal or officer allows it, and where a crosswalk is marked they must use it.

sec04-card-sec04-R12.front: Where do most pedestrian fatalities occur, and who holds safety responsibility?
sec04-card-sec04-R12.expected_back: Most pedestrian deaths happen mid-block, between intersections, and both drivers and pedestrians share responsibility, so drivers should always be ready to yield.

sec04-card-sec04-F41.front: What offense grade applies to disobeying a Nevada school crossing guard, and when may you drive across?
sec04-card-sec04-F41.expected_back: Disobeying a school crossing guard is a misdemeanor in Nevada, and drivers must wait until the guard has fully left the crosswalk.

sec04-card-sec04-F42.front: What are Nevada's two school-zone speed limits, when do timed zones run, and what if yellow beacons are off during class?
sec04-card-sec04-F42.expected_back: School-zone speed limits are fifteen or twenty-five miles per hour and apply on school days from half an hour before classes start until half an hour after they end, unless posted otherwise; if flashing yellow lights are off during class time, the regular limit applies.

sec04-card-sec04-F43.front: When are U-turns prohibited in a Nevada school zone, and when are they allowed?
sec04-card-sec04-F43.expected_back: U-turns in a school zone are banned except when no children are present, on days without school, outside the half-hour windows around the school day, or when signs or lights show the zone is not in effect.

sec04-card-sec04-R20.front: Which two posted speed limits govern Nevada school zones, and how do beacons clarify active times?
sec04-card-sec04-R20.expected_back: School-zone limits are either fifteen or twenty-five miles per hour, and some zones use flashing yellow lights to show when the lower limit is in effect.

sec04-card-sec04-F30.front: What two colors are pavement lines, and what do broken white lines indicate?
sec04-card-sec04-F30.expected_back: Pavement markings are white or yellow, and broken white lines divide lanes moving the same way; stay inside your lane without straddling, and pass only when safe.

sec04-card-sec04-F31.front: What does a solid white stripe mean between same-direction lanes, and what road borders does it mark?
sec04-card-sec04-F31.memory_hook: No lane changes, marks right edge
sec04-card-sec04-F31.expected_back: A solid white line between same-direction lanes means no lane changes and no passing, and solid white also marks the highway edge and the line between a travel lane and the shoulder.

sec04-card-sec04-F32.front: What traffic split do yellow lines mark, and how do broken and solid yellow lines differ?
sec04-card-sec04-F32.memory_hook: Opposite flow, broken passes, solid holds
sec04-card-sec04-F32.expected_back: Yellow lines divide traffic moving in opposite directions: a broken yellow line allows passing when safe, while a solid yellow line means do not cross or pass and also marks the left edge of multi-lane divided highways.

sec04-card-sec04-F33.front: Along a double yellow centerline with one broken and one solid stripe, when is passing forbidden?
sec04-card-sec04-F33.memory_hook: Forbidden when solid hugs your side
sec04-card-sec04-F33.expected_back: With double yellow lines, you may not pass if the line on your side is solid.

sec04-card-sec04-F34.front: Where must you stop at painted crosswalks, and what applies at intersections without painted crosswalk lines?
sec04-card-sec04-F34.expected_back: Always stop before a crosswalk, and at intersections where no crosswalk is painted you must still yield to pedestrians.

sec04-card-sec04-F35.front: How is a center left-turn lane painted, what maneuvers are allowed, and what uses are banned?
sec04-card-sec04-F35.expected_back: A center left-turn lane, edged by solid and broken yellow lines, may be crossed only to turn left onto or off the highway and is never a travel or passing lane.

sec04-card-sec04-F36.front: Under Nevada law, what is the maximum distance you may travel inside a center turn lane before turning left versus after entering?
sec04-card-sec04-F36.expected_back: You may drive no more than two hundred feet in a center turn lane before turning left, and no more than fifty feet in it after turning onto the highway before merging (NRS 484B point two two three).

sec04-card-sec04-R13.front: How does a broken white lane line contrast with a solid white line between same-direction lanes?
sec04-card-sec04-R13.expected_back: Broken white separates same-direction lanes and allows passing when safe, while solid white between same-direction lanes forbids lane changes and passing.

sec04-card-sec04-R14.front: What overarching rule separates white roadway markings from yellow centerline markings?
sec04-card-sec04-R14.expected_back: White lane lines separate same-direction traffic and white markings also mark road edges, shoulders, crosswalks and stop lines, whereas yellow lines separate opposite-direction traffic.

sec04-card-sec04-R15.front: What do wide white stop lines and short dotted white lines each mark on the pavement?
sec04-card-sec04-R15.expected_back: Stop lines are wide white lines across a lane where you stop with a view of traffic from every direction, and dotted white lines either carry a lane line through an intersection or mark freeway exit-only lanes.

sec04-card-sec04-F14.front: What actions do railroad crossing warning signs call for as you approach the tracks?
sec04-card-sec04-F14.expected_back: Railroad crossing signs warn you to slow and possibly stop; look both ways and stay off the tracks whenever a train is approaching.

sec04-card-sec04-F37.front: At least how far back from the nearest rail must you stop when a train approaches?
sec04-card-sec04-F37.expected_back: At a railroad crossing with a stop sign you must stop, and when a train is coming you must stop at least fifteen feet from the tracks.

sec04-card-sec04-F38.front: Which two vehicle categories must stop at railroad crossings even when signals stay dark and tracks look clear?
sec04-card-sec04-F38.expected_back: Passenger buses and trucks hauling flammable or dangerous materials must stop at railroad crossings even when no signal shows and no train is coming.

sec04-card-sec04-F39.front: What is the rule at a lowered railroad gate versus at flashing red crossing lights without a gate?
sec04-card-sec04-F39.expected_back: Never drive around a lowered crossing gate even if no train is visible, and when crossing lights flash you must stop and may go only if no train is visible or it is safe.

sec04-card-sec04-F40.front: Within what distance of the nearest railroad rail is parking strictly prohibited?
sec04-card-sec04-F40.expected_back: Never park within fifty feet of the nearest rail of a railroad.

sec04-card-sec04-R16.front: Contrast Nevada's minimum stopping distance for an approaching train against its no-parking distance from rails?
sec04-card-sec04-R16.expected_back: Stop at least fifteen feet from the tracks when a train comes, but never park within fifty feet of the nearest rail.

sec04-card-sec04-R17.front: What two precautions apply at multi-track railroad crossings?
sec04-card-sec04-R17.expected_back: At a crossing with more than one set of tracks, wait for a clear view in both directions before starting across, and never shift gears while on the tracks.

sec04-card-sec04-R18.front: What three facts explain why motorists must always yield at a railroad crossbuck?
sec04-card-sec04-R18.expected_back: A train cannot stop in time to avoid a car, its speed is hard to judge, and a crossbuck means drivers must yield to trains.

sec04-card-sec04-R19.front: What three steps must you take immediately if your vehicle stalls across railroad tracks?
sec04-card-sec04-R19.expected_back: If your vehicle stalls on the tracks, get out at once, find the blue Emergency Notification System sign at the crossing, and notify the railroad and local police.

sec02-card-sec02-F01.front: Along with a parent or guardian co-signer, what document must an applicant under eighteen sign?
sec02-card-sec02-F01.expected_back: An applicant under eighteen for a license, DAC or instruction permit needs a parent or guardian to co-sign and must sign an affidavit acknowledging the penalties that apply to young drivers.

sec02-card-sec02-F02.front: What chemical test reading triggers a young-driver license revocation in Nevada, and how long does it last?
sec02-card-sec02-F02.expected_back: A young driver's license can be revoked for one hundred eighty-five days when a blood, breath or urine test shows an alcohol level of at least zero point zero two percent but less than zero point zero eight percent by weight.

sec02-card-sec02-F03.front: How long is a young driver's license revoked if a court finds they drove impaired by alcohol or controlled substances?
sec02-card-sec02-F03.expected_back: Any court finding that a young driver drove under the influence of alcohol or a controlled substance also brings a one hundred eighty-five-day revocation.

sec02-card-sec02-F04.front: Which graffiti, drug, or alcohol offenses can suspend or delay a young person's license for up to two years?
sec02-card-sec02-F04.expected_back: Graffiti or defacing property, crimes tied to alcohol or a controlled substance, any use, possession, sale or distribution of a controlled substance, or buying, drinking or possessing alcohol can each mean suspension or delayed issuance for up to two years.

sec02-card-sec02-F05.front: How long are driving privileges suspended or delayed for a first versus second youth firearm violation?
sec02-card-sec02-F05.expected_back: Handling or possessing a firearm in violation of NRS two hundred two point three zero zero means suspension or delayed issuance for up to one year, and two years for a second offense.

sec02-card-sec02-F06.front: What license suspension or permit delay penalties apply to first and repeat habitual truancy offenses?
sec02-card-sec02-F06.expected_back: A first habitual-truancy offense brings a suspension of thirty days to six months or a thirty-day delay; a second or later offense brings sixty days to one year or a sixty-day delay (NRS three hundred ninety-two point one four eight).

sec02-card-sec02-F07.front: How long is your license suspended for joining or helping stage an unauthorized speed contest or trick-driving display?
sec02-card-sec02-F07.expected_back: A conviction for joining or organizing an unauthorized speed contest, or for driving in or facilitating an unauthorized trick driving display, brings a suspension of six months to two years.

sec02-card-sec02-F08.front: How do first-time DUI penalties for a young driver compare with penalties for drivers over twenty-one?
sec02-card-sec02-F08.expected_back: A young driver who becomes a first-time DUI offender faces the same penalties as a driver over twenty-one.

sec02-card-sec02-R01.front: Contrast what happens to a young driver at a low alcohol reading versus a full first-time DUI?
sec02-card-sec02-R01.expected_back: A low alcohol reading between zero point zero two percent and zero point zero eight percent already costs a young driver a one hundred eighty-five-day revocation, while a first DUI offense puts the young driver under the full adult penalties.

sec02-card-sec02-F09.front: Which two completed records must a teen bring to the drive test, and what ink rule applies?
sec02-card-sec02-F09.expected_back: A teen applying for a license or DAC must present a driver's education Certificate of Completion and the Beginning Driver Experience Log (DMV Form DLD-one hundred thirty), filled in with blue or black ink before arriving for the drive test.

sec02-card-sec02-F10.front: Which signed school form must every instruction-permit applicant under eighteen turn in at the DMV?
sec02-card-sec02-F10.expected_back: Anyone under eighteen applying for an instruction permit must give the DMV a DMV-three hundred one Certification of Attendance signed by the principal or a designated school official confirming minimum attendance.

sec02-card-sec02-F11.front: What does a minor who already finished high school submit with the attendance form, and how fresh must the signature be?
sec02-card-sec02-F11.expected_back: A minor who has finished school submits the DMV-three hundred one with a copy of a high school diploma or an equivalency (GED, HiSET or TASC), and the form must be signed and dated within the previous sixty days.

sec02-card-sec02-R02.front: What must a student suspended for habitual truancy bring to the DMV to reinstate driving privileges?
sec02-card-sec02-R02.expected_back: A student previously declared a habitual truant under NRS three hundred ninety-two point one four four whose license or permit was suspended must bring a new DMV-three hundred one showing current attendance before driving privileges are reinstated.

sec02-card-sec02-F12.front: Through what two classroom formats can a Nevada teen complete driver's education?
sec02-card-sec02-F12.expected_back: Driver's education can be completed at a local DMV-approved school or online through a DMV-approved school.

sec02-card-sec02-F13.front: Who qualifies to log extra behind-the-wheel hours instead of driver's education, and how many hours are required?
sec02-card-sec02-F13.expected_back: Only a teen living more than thirty miles from an approved school who cannot take an online class may instead log one hundred hours of behind-the-wheel driving, ten of them in the dark.

sec02-card-sec02-F14.front: How many total and nighttime supervised driving hours must teens living within thirty miles of an approved school log?
sec02-card-sec02-F14.expected_back: Teens within thirty miles of an approved driver's education school must complete fifty hours of supervised driving, ten of them at night, recorded on the official DMV form.

sec02-card-sec02-R03.front: Compare total and nighttime logged hours on Nevada's standard teen path versus the remote rural path?
sec02-card-sec02-R03.expected_back: The standard path is fifty supervised hours with ten at night; the remote path for teens beyond thirty miles of a school and without internet access is one hundred hours with ten in the dark.

sec02-card-sec02-R04.front: How does the lighting rule change if those one hundred remote-path practice hours are for a motorcycle license?
sec02-card-sec02-R04.expected_back: For a motorcycle license on the remote path, all one hundred practice hours must be driven in daylight only.

sec02-card-sec02-F15.front: What three blemishes must stay completely off a minor's record for six months before licensing?
sec02-card-sec02-F15.expected_back: A minor must go six months without an at-fault crash, a moving violation conviction or any alcohol or drug conviction before receiving a license.

sec02-card-sec02-F16.front: How long is a Nevada instruction permit valid, and when must it be in your possession?
sec02-card-sec02-F16.expected_back: A Nevada instruction permit is valid for one year and must be carried whenever the holder drives.

sec02-card-sec02-F17.front: What minimum age, tests, and adult authorization are required to get a Nevada instruction permit?
sec02-card-sec02-F17.expected_back: To get a permit you must be at least fifteen and a half, complete an application, pass a vision test and a knowledge test on traffic laws, signs, markings and safe driving, and have a parent or guardian available to authorize it.

sec02-card-sec02-F18.front: What age, driving experience, and seating position are required for someone supervising a Class C permit holder?
sec02-card-sec02-F18.expected_back: A Class C permit holder may drive only with a licensed driver who is twenty-one or older, has at least one year of licensed experience and sits in the seat beside the permit holder.

sec02-card-sec02-F19.front: How long must an applicant under eighteen hold an instruction permit before applying for a driver license?
sec02-card-sec02-F19.memory_hook: Hold permit at least six months
sec02-card-sec02-F19.expected_back: Applicants under eighteen must hold an instruction permit for at least six months before applying for a license.

sec02-card-sec02-F20.front: What passenger restriction applies during the first six months for new sixteen- and seventeen-year-old licensees?
sec02-card-sec02-F20.expected_back: For their first six months of driving, new licensees who were sixteen or seventeen at issuance may not carry passengers under eighteen except immediate family members (NRS four hundred eighty-three point two five two three).

sec02-card-sec02-F21.front: Between what hours may a minor not drive unless traveling for a scheduled event, and when does that curfew end?
sec02-card-sec02-F21.expected_back: A minor may not drive between ten p.m. and five a.m. unless driving to or from a scheduled event, and this curfew lasts until the driver turns eighteen regardless of when the license was issued.

sec02-card-sec02-R05.front: How does supervisor positioning differ between a Class C car permit and a motorcycle or moped permit?
sec02-card-sec02-R05.expected_back: A Class C permit supervisor sits in the seat beside you, while a motorcycle or moped permit supervisor must ride a motorcycle within direct sight and may not be in a car or truck.

sec02-card-sec02-R06.front: Which three operating restrictions govern a Class M or M-Z motorcycle or moped permit holder?
sec02-card-sec02-R06.expected_back: A Class M or M-Z permit holder rides in daylight only, carries no passengers and stays off limited-access highways and freeways.

sec02-card-sec02-R07.front: What are the three distinct six-month milestones that apply to teen licensing in Nevada?
sec02-card-sec02-R07.expected_back: Three different six-month rules apply to Nevada teens: hold the permit at least six months, carry no non-family passengers under eighteen for the first six months of licensed driving, and stay crash- and conviction-free for six months before licensing.

sec02-card-sec02-F22.front: Which exams apply across every Nevada license class, and when is a road test added?
sec02-card-sec02-F22.expected_back: Every license class requires vision and knowledge tests, and a road test in the type of vehicle to be driven may also be required.

sec02-card-sec02-F23.front: What two additional exams must a Class C driver pass to add motorcycle privileges?
sec02-card-sec02-F23.expected_back: A Class C holder who also wants to ride a motorcycle must pass a written test on motorcycle laws and practices and a motorcycle drive test.

sec02-card-sec02-F24.front: Which Nevada driver license classes allow riding a moped on public streets?
sec02-card-sec02-F24.expected_back: Any Nevada driver license class lets you ride a moped, or you can apply for a Class M license restricted to mopeds only.

sec02-card-sec02-F25.front: What vehicles, maximum towed weight, and overall combination length does a standard Class C license cover?
sec02-card-sec02-F25.expected_back: Class C covers cars, vans and pickups and may tow a vehicle of ten thousand pounds or less, and any combination of vehicles may not exceed seventy feet.

sec02-card-sec02-F26.front: What do Nevada license restriction codes B, F, G, six, seven, eight, and JN each stand for?
sec02-card-sec02-F26.expected_back: Common restriction codes are B for glasses or contacts, F for added rearview mirrors, G for daylight driving only, six for a yearly vision exam, seven for a yearly medical letter, eight for a yearly driving test and JN for instruction permit.

sec02-card-sec02-R08.front: What vehicle categories belong to Nevada License Classes A, B, and M?
sec02-card-sec02-R08.memory_hook: A heavy combos, B singles, M
sec02-card-sec02-R08.expected_back: Class A covers combinations rated over twenty-six thousand pounds GCWR with a trailer over ten thousand pounds, Class B covers a single vehicle over twenty-six thousand pounds GVWR that may tow under ten thousand pounds, and Class M covers motorcycles and mopeds.

sec02-card-sec02-R09.front: Where are the extra knowledge and skills tests for commercial motor vehicle operators detailed?
sec02-card-sec02-R09.expected_back: Commercial drivers must pass additional knowledge and skills tests described in the separate Commercial Driver's License Handbook.

sec02-card-sec02-F27.front: What does a license endorsement authorize, and how do you earn each one?
sec02-card-sec02-F27.expected_back: An endorsement allows driving a vehicle that needs more skill than a typical vehicle, and each one needs additional tests.

sec02-card-sec02-F28.front: What does a J endorsement let a Class C driver tow, and where does Class A take over?
sec02-card-sec02-F28.expected_back: The J endorsement lets a Class C driver tow a vehicle or combination rated above ten thousand pounds, provided the combination stays within seventy feet and twenty-six thousand pounds; above twenty-six thousand pounds a Class A license is required.

sec02-card-sec02-R10.front: Which three groups qualify for the F endorsement commercial exemption, and what farm limits apply?
sec02-card-sec02-R10.expected_back: The F endorsement is a commercial-license exemption for firefighters operating fire equipment, for military members driving military vehicles on active duty, and for farm employees or family hauling supplies within one hundred fifty miles of the farm unless they are a common or contract carrier or carry placarded hazardous materials.

sec02-card-sec02-R11.front: Which three thresholds classify a vehicle used in commerce as a commercial motor vehicle?
sec02-card-sec02-R11.expected_back: A commercial motor vehicle is one used in commerce with a weight rating of twenty-six thousand one pounds or more, or designed for sixteen or more people including the driver, or carrying hazardous materials.

sec02-card-sec02-R12.front: How long does a Nevada motorcycle permit last for minors, seventeen-plus teens, and adults eighteen or older?
sec02-card-sec02-R12.expected_back: A motorcycle permit issued between fifteen and a half and eighteen lasts one year, but one issued after age seventeen expires on the eighteenth birthday; at eighteen or older it lasts six months and can be renewed only once every five years.

sec02-card-sec02-R13.front: What can waive DMV motorcycle tests, and what happens if you fail the DMV motorcycle skills test twice?
sec02-card-sec02-R13.memory_hook: Safety course waives, two fails bar
sec02-card-sec02-R13.expected_back: Passing an approved motorcycle safety course may replace the motorcycle tests, but failing the DMV motorcycle skills test two or more times permanently bars future motorcycle permits (NRS four hundred eighty-three point two eight zero).

sec02-card-sec02-R14.front: What minimum age, exams, and protective gear apply to earning and riding on a Nevada motorcycle license?
sec02-card-sec02-R14.expected_back: A motorcycle license requires age sixteen, a vision test, the general and motorcycle knowledge tests and the Motorcycle Operators Skills Test, and riders must wear a helmet.

sec02-card-sec02-F29.front: Where is your license expiration printed, and who bears legal responsibility if a mailed notice never arrives?
sec02-card-sec02-F29.expected_back: The expiration date is printed on the front of the license, and renewing on or before it is the driver's responsibility even though a renewal notice is mailed.

sec02-card-sec02-F30.front: Which three tests can the DMV require at renewal to re-evaluate a driver or set restrictions?
sec02-card-sec02-F30.expected_back: Renewal may call for vision, knowledge and on-road driving tests to re-evaluate the driver and decide on restrictions.

sec02-card-sec02-F31.front: Does Nevada automatically extend military licenses past expiration, and how do out-of-state active-duty members renew?
sec02-card-sec02-F31.expected_back: Nevada does not automatically extend licenses for military personnel, but active-duty members temporarily out of state may renew by mail.

sec02-card-sec02-F32.front: Within how many days must you report an address or legal name change to the Nevada DMV?
sec02-card-sec02-F32.expected_back: Nevada law requires you to report any change of address or name to the DMV within thirty days.

sec02-card-sec02-F33.front: How may standard drivers update an address compared with CDL holders and anyone changing a legal name?
sec02-card-sec02-F33.expected_back: Addresses can be changed online, at a DMV office or by mail with form DMV-twenty-two, but CDL holders must do it in person; name changes are always made in person with legal proof of the new name.

sec02-card-sec02-F34.front: Which two distinct groups can qualify for a Nevada restricted license?
sec02-card-sec02-F34.expected_back: Restricted licenses may go to drivers aged fourteen and fifteen who show family hardship or need to drive to and from school, and to people who have served half of a suspension or revocation.

sec02-card-sec02-R15.front: Why is a Nevada restricted license considered a special-circumstance exception rather than a standard shortcut?
sec02-card-sec02-R15.expected_back: A restricted license is a special-circumstance exception: drivers of fourteen or fifteen qualify only with family hardship or a school-travel need, and others only after serving half of a suspension or revocation.

sec02-card-sec02-R16.front: What should you do right away if your license is lost, stolen, or worn unreadable, and how can it be issued?
sec02-card-sec02-R16.expected_back: A lost, stolen or illegible license should be replaced immediately with a duplicate, online or in person, and the DMV may use the record and photo already on file.

sec02-card-sec02-F35.front: What minimum age applies to a Nevada ID card, and how long does it remain valid?
sec02-card-sec02-F35.expected_back: A Nevada ID card requires age ten or older and lasts eight years, expiring on the birthday unless limited-term immigration documents were used.

sec02-card-sec02-F36.front: What happens to your driving privilege and prior cards when Nevada issues you a state ID card, and who is exempt?
sec02-card-sec02-F36.expected_back: Being issued an ID card automatically surrenders your driving privilege and any ID card from Nevada or another state, whether or not you have it with you; seasonal resident ID applicants are the exception.

sec02-card-sec02-F37.front: How do traffic tickets affect a Nevada ID card holder who wants a driver license later?
sec02-card-sec02-F37.expected_back: Traffic citations issued to an ID card holder count against future driving privileges, and twelve or more demerits in twelve months means the privilege must be reinstated before a license can be issued.

sec02-card-sec02-R17.front: When does a Nevada ID card expire if issued using limited-term immigration documents?
sec02-card-sec02-R17.expected_back: An ID card based on limited-term immigration documents expires on the departure date, or one year after issuance when no date is listed.

sec02-card-sec02-R18.front: What two steps allow a former service member to add a veteran designation onto a Nevada license or ID?
sec02-card-sec02-R18.expected_back: An honorably discharged veteran can add a veteran designation at an initial or renewal license or ID by bringing proof of honorable discharge and signing a release to the Nevada Department of Veterans Services.

sec02-card-sec02-R19.front: What paperwork is needed to display an optional medical indicator symbol on the front of your card?
sec02-card-sec02-R19.expected_back: An optional medical indicator, shown as a recognized medical symbol on the front of the card, needs a completed Confidential Physician Report (DMV Form DLD-seven) naming one listed medical code.

sec02-card-sec02-F38.front: When can Organ Donor status be added to a card, and what does a minor's parent commit to on the form?
sec02-card-sec02-F38.expected_back: Organ Donor can be added to a license or ID card at original issuance, renewal or an address change, and a minor's parent or guardian signs an affidavit on the DMV-two accepting that they cannot amend or revoke the donation.

sec02-card-sec02-R20.front: How does the DMV collect organ-donor contributions, and where do Gift of Life Education Fund dollars go?
sec02-card-sec02-R20.expected_back: The DMV takes contributions for the Anatomical Gift Account during licensing and through Organ Donor license plates, and gifts of one dollar or more to the Gift of Life Education Fund go to the University of Nevada School of Medicine.

sec02-card-sec02-R21.front: What warning signs suggest possible sex trafficking, and what safety rule must observers always follow?
sec02-card-sec02-R21.expected_back: Possible signs of sex trafficking include not knowing one's whereabouts, not holding one's own ID or passport, controlled communication and a fearful or submissive manner, and a suspected trafficker should never be confronted.

sec02-card-sec02-F39.front: Who sets Nevada DMV fees, and what do an original license and instruction permit cost under age sixty-five?
sec02-card-sec02-F39.expected_back: Fees are set by Nevada state law and can change; under age sixty-five an original license costs forty-one dollars and twenty-five cents and an instruction permit twenty-two dollars and twenty-five cents.

sec02-card-sec02-F40.front: Compare Nevada's license reinstatement cost after an alcohol or drug offense versus any other suspension?
sec02-card-sec02-F40.expected_back: Reinstatement after an alcohol or controlled-substance offense costs one hundred twenty dollars plus a thirty-five dollars victim's fee, while reinstatement for any other offense costs seventy-five dollars.

sec02-card-sec02-F41.front: Which three fee categories apply when restoring driving privileges after a suspension, revocation, or cancellation?
sec02-card-sec02-F41.expected_back: Any suspension, revocation or cancellation requires paying the reinstatement fee, the original-license fee and any testing fees that apply.

sec02-card-sec02-R22.front: What reduced fees apply to drivers aged sixty-five and older and to youth ID cards for ages ten through seventeen?
sec02-card-sec02-R22.expected_back: Drivers sixty-five and older pay seventeen dollars and twenty-five cents for an original, duplicate, renewal or instruction permit, and ID cards for ages ten to seventeen cost nine dollars and twenty-five cents.

sec02-card-sec02-R23.front: What does a standalone address-change card cost, and how do initial test and retest fees compare?
sec02-card-sec02-R23.expected_back: A change of address alone costs three dollars and twenty-five cents, and each knowledge and skills retest costs ten dollars after the twenty-five dollars initial test fee.

sec02-card-sec02-R24.front: What extra fee must a commercial driver pay when reinstating a suspended CDL?
sec02-card-sec02-R24.expected_back: Reinstating a commercial license also requires paying a non-CDL reinstatement fee.

sec06-card-sec06-F01.question_text: At least how many seconds ahead should you look in town, and how far is that at thirty miles per hour?
sec06-card-sec06-F01.teaching_text: Staring only at the bumper ahead hides red lights and double-parked vans a block downstreet.

sec06-card-sec06-R01.question_text: How do you count-check your twelve-second look-ahead, and how far ahead should you scan at freeway speed?
sec06-card-sec06-R01.teaching_text: Reaching your chosen landmark before one-thousand-twelve proves your eyes are aimed too low.

sec06-card-sec06-F02.question_text: At forty miles per hour or less, what is the minimum following gap, and what do most instructors recommend?
sec06-card-sec06-F02.teaching_text: Two seconds barely covers dry alert reaction, which is why instructors push up to four seconds.

sec06-card-sec06-R02.question_text: How do you use a roadside object to test whether you are following at least two seconds back?
sec06-card-sec06-R02.teaching_text: Passing that signpost before saying one-thousand-two means you are tailgating inside your reaction zone.

sec06-card-sec06-F03.question_text: Almost how many seconds does stopping from fifty-five miles per hour take even under ideal conditions?
sec06-card-sec06-F03.teaching_text: When ideal highway braking takes nearly seven seconds, two-second town spacing leaves zero chance to stop.

sec06-card-sec06-R03.question_text: How should you position yourself relative to traffic packs to keep room to maneuver?
sec06-card-sec06-R03.teaching_text: Sitting between vehicle packs in the lane with open escape outs prevents getting boxed into someone's crash.

sec06-card-sec06-F04.question_text: In what exact left-right order should you look right before entering an intersection?
sec06-card-sec06-F04.teaching_text: Cross traffic from your left reaches your driver-side door first, earning both the first and final check.

sec06-card-sec06-F05.question_text: When is making a cell-phone voice call legal while driving in Nevada?
sec06-card-sec06-F05.teaching_text: Holding a phone to your ear or on speaker in your hand violates Nevada's handheld wireless ban.

sec06-card-sec06-F06.question_text: Which non-voice handheld device actions are prohibited while driving in Nevada?
sec06-card-sec06-F06.teaching_text: Typing texts, reading messages, or searching web pages by hand steals eyes and draws primary citations.

sec06-card-sec06-F07.question_text: Under what exact condition may a Nevada driver use a handheld wireless device while moving?
sec06-card-sec06-F07.teaching_text: Reporting an active emergency qualifies when pulling over would be dangerous, impractical, or inadvisable.

sec06-card-sec06-F08.question_text: What three steps should you take as soon as police lights flash behind you, especially at night?
sec06-card-sec06-F08.teaching_text: Switching on your cabin dome light after pulling clear reassures the approaching officer at night.
sec06-card-sec06-F08.must_match_memory_hook: Pull clear, stay in, dome light

visual_sync.text_span: Pull clear, stay in, dome light

sec06-card-sec06-F09.question_text: Where should your hands stay during a police stop, and when should you reach for your documents?
sec06-card-sec06-F09.teaching_text: Digging into a dark glovebox before the officer reaches your window looks dangerous from behind.

sec06-card-sec06-R04.question_text: What category of violations causes most police traffic stops?
sec06-card-sec06-R04.teaching_text: Speeding, missed signals, rolled stops, or lane drifts draw stops even when drivers slipped unintentionally.

sec06-card-sec06-R05.question_text: In what order do officers usually conduct a stop, and where is the proper place to contest a ticket?
sec06-card-sec06-R05.teaching_text: Officers verify license, registration, and insurance before explaining the stop, and arguments belong strictly in court.
sec06-card-sec06-R05.must_match_memory_hook: Give papers calmly, contest in court

visual_sync.text_span: Give papers calmly, contest in court

sec06-card-sec06-F10.question_text: To whom must you yield when entering a roundabout, and which direction does all traffic circulate?
sec06-card-sec06-F10.teaching_text: Traffic inside the circle always moves counterclockwise to your right and holds priority over every entrance.

sec06-card-sec06-F11.question_text: In a two-lane roundabout, which movements use the left lane and which use the right lane?
sec06-card-sec06-F11.teaching_text: Both lanes allow going straight, whereas right turns take the right lane and left or U-turns take left.

sec06-card-sec06-F12.question_text: How fast should you drive inside a roundabout, and which signal do you switch on to exit?
sec06-card-sec06-F12.teaching_text: Flashing your right signal approaching your exit tells waiting drivers at the next leg they can enter.

sec06-card-sec06-R06.question_text: Who is the raised concrete truck apron around a roundabout's center island built for, and what should cars do?
sec06-card-sec06-R06.teaching_text: Long semi-trailers track rear wheels onto the raised apron on tight turns, so never crowd beside trucks.
sec06-card-sec06-R06.must_match_memory_hook: Big trailers use apron, cars off

visual_sync.text_span: Big trailers use apron, cars off

sec06-card-sec06-R07.question_text: What two safe options do bicyclists have for navigating a roundabout?
sec06-card-sec06-R07.teaching_text: Hugging the outer curb invites car squeeze-outs, so cyclists either claim the lane or walk crosswalks.
sec06-card-sec06-R07.must_match_memory_hook: Take full lane or walk crosswalks

visual_sync.text_span: Take full lane or walk crosswalks

sec06-card-sec06-R08.question_text: Where must pedestrians cross at a roundabout, and where must they never step?
sec06-card-sec06-R08.teaching_text: Cutting straight across circulating lanes to the center island surprises drivers watching curved paths.

sec06-card-sec06-F13.question_text: For which five everyday vehicle actions does Nevada law—not mere courtesy—require signaling?
sec06-card-sec06-F13.teaching_text: Brake lights and blinkers are statutory commands whenever you alter direction or drop speed.

sec06-card-sec06-F14.question_text: Using your left arm, how do you hand-signal a left turn, a right turn, and slowing or stopping?
sec06-card-sec06-F14.teaching_text: Broken bulb wires or bright bike rides put all three left-arm positions right onto written exams.
sec06-card-sec06-F14.must_match_memory_hook: Straight left, up right, down stop

visual_sync.text_span: Straight left, up right, down stop

sec06-card-sec06-F15.question_text: How many feet ahead must you signal a turn on city streets versus on open Nevada highways?
sec06-card-sec06-F15.teaching_text: Watch Nevada's split—city streets require one hundred feet while open highways triple that to three hundred.
sec06-card-sec06-F15.must_match_memory_hook: One hundred city, three hundred highway

visual_sync.text_span: One hundred city, three hundred highway

sec06-card-sec06-F16.question_text: Which lane do you use to turn right, and what is forbidden once inside a reserved right-turn lane?
sec06-card-sec06-F16.teaching_text: Continuing straight out of a dedicated right-turn lane T-bones drivers turning right from beside you.

sec06-card-sec06-F17.question_text: How must your front wheels point while waiting to turn left, and which lanes connect on a two-way road?
sec06-card-sec06-F17.teaching_text: Pre-cocked left wheels shove your car straight into oncoming traffic if someone rear-ends you while waiting.

sec06-card-sec06-R09.question_text: Which lane must you enter immediately after turning right, and when may you move to another lane?
sec06-card-sec06-R09.teaching_text: Hold the nearest right lane through the turn and signal a separate lane change well past the corner.

sec06-card-sec06-R10.question_text: What final checks belong right before turning, and what should you do once settled in the new lane?
sec06-card-sec06-R10.teaching_text: Leaving a turn signal blinking down the block tricks cross-street drivers into pulling out ahead of you.

sec06-card-sec06-F18.question_text: What are the mirror, signal, and blind-spot rules for changing lanes, and where must you never change lanes?
sec06-card-sec06-F18.teaching_text: Switching lanes mid-intersection blindsides turning traffic expecting you to hold your entry lane.

sec06-card-sec06-F19.question_text: Where are U-turns generally legal in Nevada, and from which lanes do you start them?
sec06-card-sec06-F19.teaching_text: Unless restricted, Nevada permits safe U-turns initiated from the far-left travel lane or center left-turn lane.

sec06-card-sec06-F20.question_text: When are U-turns legal across double yellow lines, at green signals, and on divided highways?
sec06-card-sec06-F20.teaching_text: Unlike passing bans, double yellow stripes allow safe U-turns where sightlines and district rules permit.

sec06-card-sec06-R12.question_text: What three center barriers on a divided highway may you never drive across for a U-turn?
sec06-card-sec06-R12.teaching_text: Two sets of double yellow lines act as a virtual concrete median that cannot be crossed.

sec06-card-sec06-F21.question_text: At which four roadway locations or traffic conditions are U-turns flatly illegal?
sec06-card-sec06-F21.teaching_text: Spinning around on railroad rails or one-way streets creates immediate wrong-way or train hazards.

sec06-card-sec06-F22.question_text: How many feet of clear visibility in both directions are required when curves, hills, rain, or fog limit sight?
sec06-card-sec06-F22.teaching_text: Watch Nevada's two U-turn numbers—general obstructed sightlines forbid U-turns below two hundred clear feet.
sec06-card-sec06-F22.must_match_memory_hook: Two hundred clear feet both ways

visual_sync.text_span: Two hundred clear feet both ways

sec06-card-sec06-R13.question_text: Near a roadway grade, what visibility minimum applies to U-turns, and who else can ban them?
sec06-card-sec06-R13.teaching_text: Steep grades demand five hundred feet of clear view both ways, and state or local agencies can post bans.

sec06-card-sec06-F23.question_text: What buildings count inside a Nevada business district for U-turn rules, and where may you turn around there?
sec06-card-sec06-F23.teaching_text: Nevada counts apartments, churches, multifamily complexes, and public buildings inside business districts—never flip mid-block.

sec06-card-sec06-R11.question_text: How does U-turn legality in a residential district compare with a business district?
sec06-card-sec06-R11.teaching_text: Residential U-turns work when signs or signals protect you from oncoming cars, whereas business districts require intersections or openings.

sec06-card-sec06-F24.question_text: May you make a U-turn in front of a fire station or pull into its driveway to turn around?
sec06-card-sec06-F24.teaching_text: Emergency bay doors can roll open without warning, sending heavy rigs straight down the apron.

sec06-card-sec06-F25.question_text: What two shortcuts are always illegal when passing another vehicle in Nevada?
sec06-card-sec06-F25.teaching_text: Punching above the posted speed limit or swinging onto gravel shoulders draws tickets on any pass.

sec06-card-sec06-F26.question_text: Which three conditions must line up before passing on the left on a two-lane, two-way road?
sec06-card-sec06-F26.teaching_text: The dashed yellow stripe must sit on your side of the center line alongside wide-open sightlines.

sec06-card-sec06-F27.question_text: Within how many feet of a street intersection or railroad crossing—plus which other zones—is two-lane passing banned?
sec06-card-sec06-F27.teaching_text: Cross-street turns and trains turn deadly inside one hundred feet, alongside blind hills, curves, and double yellows.
sec06-card-sec06-F27.must_match_memory_hook: Within one hundred feet, curves, hills

visual_sync.text_span: Within one hundred feet, curves, hills

sec06-card-sec06-R14.question_text: How far ahead must you signal left before passing in business or residential areas versus elsewhere?
sec06-card-sec06-R14.teaching_text: Passing uses the exact same one-hundred-foot urban and three-hundred-foot rural signal distances as turns.
sec06-card-sec06-R14.must_match_memory_hook: One hundred town, three hundred open

visual_sync.text_span: One hundred town, three hundred open

sec06-card-sec06-F28.question_text: When is it safe to pull back into your right-hand lane after overtaking a vehicle?
sec06-card-sec06-F28.teaching_text: Seeing the overtaken car in your interior mirror confirms you will not clip their front bumper.

sec06-card-sec06-F29.question_text: What two actions must you take when a driver behind you signals to pass?
sec06-card-sec06-F29.teaching_text: Edging slightly right inside your lane widens sightlines, while accelerating traps the passer head-on.

sec06-card-sec06-F30.question_text: Why must you never pass on the left of a vehicle making or signaling a left turn?
sec06-card-sec06-F30.teaching_text: Overtaking on the left puts your car straight through the exact driveway or cross street they are turning into.

sec06-card-sec06-F31.question_text: On a highway with two lanes in your direction, when is driving below the speed limit in the far-left lane illegal?
sec06-card-sec06-F31.teaching_text: Holding up faster vehicles behind you while cruising under the limit in the left lane breaks Nevada law.

sec06-card-sec06-R16.question_text: In which six situations does Nevada's slow-left-lane prohibition NOT apply?
sec06-card-sec06-R16.teaching_text: Urban streets, left-turn prep, police orders, on-duty emergency rigs, bad hazards, and active overtaking are all exempt.
sec06-card-sec06-R16.must_match_memory_hook: Cities, left turns, police, hazards, passing

visual_sync.text_span: Cities, left turns, police, hazards, passing

sec06-card-sec06-F32.question_text: When is passing on the right allowed in Nevada, and what surface boundary may you never cross?
sec06-card-sec06-F32.teaching_text: Unstriped wide asphalt does not authorize right-side passing, and dropping tires off pavement is illegal.

sec06-card-sec06-R15.question_text: Why is passing on the right riskier even where marked multi-lane roads allow it?
sec06-card-sec06-R15.teaching_text: Drivers expect overtakes on their driver side and easily miss cars tucked along their right quarter panel.

sec06-card-sec06-F33.question_text: What is Nevada's preferred lane rule when passing a cyclist, and what minimum clearance applies on a single lane?
sec06-card-sec06-F33.teaching_text: Move completely into an adjacent same-way lane when safe, or leave at least three full feet of space.

sec06-card-sec06-F34.question_text: May motor vehicles drive along a marked bicycle lane in Nevada?
sec06-card-sec06-F34.teaching_text: Marked bike lanes are dedicated cyclist travel space, never an extra turn chute or passing shoulder.

sec06-card-sec06-F35.question_text: What three steps belong every time you park and step out of your vehicle?
sec06-card-sec06-F35.teaching_text: Swinging a street-side door open blindly clips cyclists and passing mirrors—always check behind first.
sec06-card-sec06-F35.must_match_memory_hook: Engine off, brake set, check door

visual_sync.text_span: Engine off, brake set, check door

sec06-card-sec06-F36.question_text: Which direction must a parked vehicle face, and within how many inches of the curb must both wheels sit?
sec06-card-sec06-F36.teaching_text: Watch state differences—Nevada gives eighteen inches from the curb for both front and rear wheels.

sec06-card-sec06-F37.question_text: From how many feet away in both directions must other drivers be able to see your parked vehicle?
sec06-card-sec06-F37.teaching_text: Parking just beyond a blind bend or crest hides your bumper inside approaching stopping distance.
sec06-card-sec06-F37.must_match_memory_hook: Visible two hundred feet both ways

visual_sync.text_span: Visible two hundred feet both ways

sec06-card-sec06-F38.question_text: Why must you never twist the ignition key to the lock position while your vehicle is rolling?
sec06-card-sec06-F38.teaching_text: Clicking into lock snaps the steering pin shut on your next wheel turn, freezing steering straight ahead.

sec06-card-sec06-F39.question_text: What parking rule does each painted curb color set—white, green, yellow, red, and blue?
sec06-card-sec06-F39.teaching_text: Red forbids any stopping at all, blue requires disabled credentials, white drops passengers or mail, yellow loads, green times.

sec06-card-sec06-R17.question_text: Which visual clues warn that a curbside parked vehicle is about to pull out or open into your lane?
sec06-card-sec06-R17.teaching_text: Puffing tailpipe vapor, white reverse lamps, or a cracked driver door give seconds of warning to ease left.

sec06-card-sec06-R18.question_text: If forced to stop along a highway, where should your wheels sit and when must warning lights shine?
sec06-card-sec06-R18.teaching_text: Clear all four tires off pavement and run flashers or parking lights from sunset to sunrise or low visibility.

sec06-card-sec06-R19.question_text: How should you align your car where no curb or markings exist, and what lights apply in emergency bays?
sec06-card-sec06-R19.teaching_text: Angling tail-out on an unmarked shoulder juts into lanes, and freeway pullouts always need active flashers.

sec06-card-sec06-R20.question_text: How long a space, side gap, bumper alignment, and initial wheel turn start right-side parallel parking?
sec06-card-sec06-R20.teaching_text: Pick a gap five feet longer than your car, line up two to three feet beside, and crank right.

sec06-card-sec06-R21.question_text: What landmark cue tells you to straighten your wheels while parallel parking, and what goes wrong too late or overdone?
sec06-card-sec06-R21.teaching_text: Staying right bangs your rear tire into the curb, while cranking too far left scrapes their rear bumper.

sec06-card-sec06-R22.question_text: At what curb distance, gear setting, and brake step do you finish parallel parking?
sec06-card-sec06-R22.teaching_text: Automatics shift into park while manuals go into first gear or reverse alongside a set parking brake.

sec06-card-sec06-F40.question_text: What core goal governs aiming your front tires when parking on any hill?
sec06-card-sec06-F40.teaching_text: If brakes ever slip on a slope, angled front tires wedge into concrete or roll safely off pavement.

sec06-card-sec06-R23.question_text: Across downhill, uphill without a curb, and uphill with a curb, which is the only case where tires turn away?
sec06-card-sec06-R23.teaching_text: Downhill and curbless uphill both turn right toward the edge—only uphill against a curb turns away.
sec06-card-sec06-R23.must_match_memory_hook: Only uphill with curb turns left

visual_sync.text_span: Only uphill with curb turns left

sec06-card-sec06-F41.question_text: How far from a fire hydrant must you stay where parallel parking is allowed versus angle parking?
sec06-card-sec06-F41.teaching_text: Angled tails stick farther out toward hose hookups, adding five extra feet onto Nevada's fifteen-foot parallel buffer.

sec06-card-sec06-F42.question_text: Within how many feet of a crosswalk or of a highway roadside traffic signal is parking prohibited?
sec06-card-sec06-F42.teaching_text: Twenty feet keeps pedestrians visible stepping off curbs, while thirty feet keeps signal heads unobstructed.

sec06-card-sec06-F43.question_text: How far must you park from a fire-station driveway on the same side versus the opposite side?
sec06-card-sec06-F43.teaching_text: Long hook-and-ladder rigs swing wide across center lines, needing seventy-five feet clear across the street.

sec06-card-sec06-R25.question_text: How do Nevada's fifteen-, twenty-, and thirty-foot parking buffers line up across hydrants, crosswalks, and signals?
sec06-card-sec06-R25.teaching_text: Grouping angle hydrants and crosswalks together at twenty separates fifteen parallel hydrants from thirty signals cleanly.
sec06-card-sec06-R25.must_match_memory_hook: Fifteen parallel, twenty angle-crosswalk, thirty signal

visual_sync.text_span: Fifteen parallel, twenty angle-crosswalk, thirty signal

sec06-card-sec06-R24.question_text: At which seven street, structure, or lane locations is non-emergency parking never allowed?
sec06-card-sec06-R24.teaching_text: Intersections, double-parked lanes, work zones, sidewalks, driveways, bridges, tunnels, and bike lanes stay strictly off-limits.

sec06-card-sec06-F44.question_text: Who must be in the vehicle to use an accessible parking space, and what is Nevada's minimum fine for violators?
sec06-card-sec06-F44.teaching_text: Borrowing a relative's placard while running solo errands carries at least a two-hundred-fifty-dollar fine.

sec06-card-sec06-R27.question_text: Why are placard holders asked to spare accessible stalls that have striped loading zones when possible?
sec06-card-sec06-R27.teaching_text: Wheelchair ramps and side lifts cannot deploy inside narrow regular stalls without that wide striped loading aisle.

sec06-card-sec06-R26.question_text: What should you do if your car breaks down on a freeway, and why shouldn't you walk down the highway?
sec06-card-sec06-R26.teaching_text: Walking along fast freeway shoulders is deadly, and patrolling troopers stop automatically to assist stranded cars.

sec12-card-sec12-F01.question_text: How does alcohol impair your brain and coordination, and how much does crash risk jump past point zero eight?
sec12-card-sec12-F01.teaching_text: Delayed processing and clumsy hand-eye timing multiply your odds of wrecking up to thirtyfold above the limit.

sec12-card-sec12-F02.question_text: Do impaired-driving dangers come only from street drugs, or from legal prescriptions and over-the-counter medicine too?
