sec12-card-sec12-F02.teaching_text: A doctor's prescription label never shields you from crashing or arrest if pills dull your reflexes.

sec12-card-sec12-F03.question_text: Even though recreational cannabis is legal in Nevada, what blood nanogram cutoffs make driving or physical control unlawful?
sec12-card-sec12-F03.teaching_text: Legal adult purchase never legalizes impaired driving above two nanograms active cannabis or five metabolite per milliliter.

sec12-card-sec12-R03.question_text: What roadway-death share in two thousand sixteen and injury-crash total from twenty-twelve to twenty-fifteen does the handbook cite?
sec12-card-sec12-R03.teaching_text: Thousands of injured Nevadans and nearly a third of traffic deaths prove impaired driving devastates real families.

sec12-card-sec12-R12.question_text: How many people died—and what percentage of all Nevada traffic deaths did alcohol cause—in two thousand nineteen?
sec12-card-sec12-R12.teaching_text: Seeing alcohol behind forty-two percent of all roadway fatalities explains why Nevada enforces strict zero-mercy revocations.

sec12-card-sec12-F04.question_text: Which two separate penalty tracks hit a driver under Nevada impaired-driving law?
sec12-card-sec12-F04.teaching_text: Even if a criminal court charge gets reduced later, the state licensing agency's administrative action still stands.

sec12-card-sec12-R04.question_text: How does an administrative impaired-driving penalty differ from a criminal penalty?
sec12-card-sec12-R04.teaching_text: Administrative license revocation runs independently through the licensing agency no matter how your courtroom case ends.

sec12-card-sec12-F05.question_text: What tests can an officer require under Implied Consent, and what if you refuse on a first offense?
sec12-card-sec12-F05.teaching_text: Driving in Nevada implies consent to testing, and officers can seek a compelled blood draw even first-time.

sec12-card-sec12-F06.question_text: How long is your driving privilege revoked for a first test refusal versus a second refusal inside seven years?
sec12-card-sec12-F06.teaching_text: Saying no to chemical testing revokes your license a full year immediately—or three years with prior refusal.

sec12-card-sec12-F07.question_text: Which chemical test findings automatically revoke your privilege under Nevada's Illegal Per Se Law?
sec12-card-sec12-F07.teaching_text: Per se means the test number alone proves violation at point zero eight alcohol or any controlled substance.

sec12-card-sec12-R01.question_text: How does Implied Consent differ from Illegal Per Se in what triggers revocation?
sec12-card-sec12-R01.teaching_text: Whether you refuse the tube or blow point zero eight, one of those two laws revokes your license.

sec12-card-sec12-F08.question_text: What alcohol concentration triggers administrative license loss for a driver under twenty-one?
sec12-card-sec12-F08.teaching_text: Even a single drink pushes young drivers past point zero two, letting the officer seize the license roadside.

sec12-card-sec12-R02.question_text: How does the per se alcohol cutoff for adults twenty-one and up compare with drivers under twenty-one?
sec12-card-sec12-R02.teaching_text: Keep those two decimals straight—underage tolerance drops four times lower than the adult point zero eight line.

sec12-card-sec12-F09.question_text: Does blowing below point zero eight percent guarantee you cannot be arrested and convicted of impaired driving?
sec12-card-sec12-F09.teaching_text: Point zero eight is not a safe harbor if weaving, slurred speech, or failed field tests show impairment.

sec12-card-sec12-F10.question_text: What procedural right can you request through the state licensing agency whenever you lose your license?
sec12-card-sec12-F10.teaching_text: Filing a hearing request lets an administrative law officer review whether agency suspension or revocation rules were met.

sec12-card-sec12-F12.question_text: At what alcohol concentration does administrative per se action kick in for a commercial license holder?
sec12-card-sec12-F12.teaching_text: Heavy commercial operators face half the standard adult cutoff, losing privileges starting right at point zero four.

sec12-card-sec12-R08.question_text: How strictly does alcohol affect commercial license holders, and how severe can repeat penalties get?
sec12-card-sec12-R08.teaching_text: Even detectable alcohol below per se affects commercial status, and serious or repeat offenses end careers permanently.

sec12-card-sec12-F11.question_text: How many days does an administrative illegal per se revocation last, and what else can follow?
sec12-card-sec12-F11.teaching_text: Exceeding point zero eight or testing positive for drugs triggers six-plus months revoked, monitored insurance, and court charges.

sec12-card-sec12-F13.question_text: How long is a driver under twenty-one revoked on the penalty chart at point zero two percent alcohol?
sec12-card-sec12-F13.teaching_text: Youth offenders at point zero two face that exact same one hundred eighty-five-day revocation plus monitored insurance.

sec12-card-sec12-F14.question_text: What revocation, jail-or-service, and fine ranges hit on a first impaired-driving conviction?
sec12-card-sec12-F14.teaching_text: Even offense number one brings two days to six months jail or forty-eight-plus service hours and up to a thousand-dollar fine.

sec12-card-sec12-F15.question_text: What class fee and possible treatment order apply to a first impaired-driving offender?
sec12-card-sec12-F15.teaching_text: Offenders fund their own education class—averaging around one hundred fifty dollars—plus court-ordered treatment at point zero eight.

sec12-card-sec12-R09.question_text: Can days already served under administrative revocation count toward a first criminal revocation?
sec12-card-sec12-R09.teaching_text: Crediting prior administrative days keeps the combined revocation aligned with the one hundred eighty-five-day floor.

sec12-card-sec12-F16.question_text: What revocation, jail, fine, and service penalties hit for a second conviction within seven years?
sec12-card-sec12-F16.teaching_text: Offense two jumps to a full year revoked, ten days to six months custody, up to thousand-dollar fines, and hundred-plus service hours.

sec12-card-sec12-R05.question_text: How do custody and community-service minimums compare between a first offense and a second within seven years?
sec12-card-sec12-R05.teaching_text: While offense one allows community service instead of two jail days, offense two mandates ten days custody plus hundred-plus hours.

sec12-card-sec12-R07.question_text: Beyond jail and fines, what plate and supervision consequences can accompany a second conviction inside seven years?
sec12-card-sec12-R07.teaching_text: Courts can suspend vehicle plates and mandate up to twelve full months of clinical substance supervision.

sec12-card-sec12-F17.question_text: What revocation, state prison term, fine, and treatment minimum apply to a third offense within seven years?
sec12-card-sec12-F17.teaching_text: Offense three becomes a felony carrying state prison up to six years, two-to-five-thousand-dollar fines, and three-year treatment.

sec12-card-sec12-F18.question_text: What revocation, prison sentence, and fine hit when impaired driving causes death or serious bodily harm?
sec12-card-sec12-F18.teaching_text: Even with a clean prior record, hurting or killing someone impaired brings up to twenty years behind bars.

sec12-card-sec12-R06.question_text: How do minimum and maximum impaired-driving fines climb across first, second, and third or injury offenses?
sec12-card-sec12-R06.teaching_text: Locking in four hundred, seven hundred fifty, and two thousand to five thousand nails every fine-comparison question.

sec12-card-sec12-F19.question_text: How can an impaired-driving offender regain restricted driving privileges right away, and who pays?
sec12-card-sec12-F19.teaching_text: Breath-tested ignition locks must be installed at the offender's own expense on every vehicle they touch.

sec12-card-sec12-F20.question_text: How long does a licensed driver under eighteen lose their license if juvenile court finds impaired driving?
sec12-card-sec12-F20.teaching_text: Juvenile court status gives zero discount on the mandatory one hundred eighty-five-day license revocation.

sec12-card-sec12-R10.question_text: How do revocation length and ignition-interlock reinstatement options for minors compare with adults?
sec12-card-sec12-R10.teaching_text: Teen drivers face the exact same one hundred eighty-five-day revocation and interlock requirements as adults.

sec12-card-sec12-F21.question_text: Which underage impaired drivers must complete a substance-abuse evaluation before a judge decides on treatment?
sec12-card-sec12-F21.teaching_text: Nevada mandates professional alcohol-or-drug screening for every impaired offender below legal drinking age.

sec12-card-sec12-F22.question_text: Where are open alcoholic drinks banned in a moving vehicle, and which three passenger spaces are exempt?
sec12-card-sec12-F22.teaching_text: Driver and passenger seats stay strictly dry outside motorhome living quarters or hired bus, taxi, and limo cabins.
sec12-card-sec12-F22.must_match_memory_hook: Banned in cabins; campers, buses, limos

visual_sync.text_span: Banned in cabins; campers, buses, limos

sec12-card-sec12-F23.question_text: How does a Nevada court treat an impaired-driving case when a child under fifteen was riding inside?
sec12-card-sec12-F23.teaching_text: Endangering passengers under fifteen triggers enhanced judicial punishment above standard baseline minimums.

sec12-card-sec12-F24.question_text: What extra dollar fee gets tacked onto an impaired-driving conviction or plea when a chemical test was run?
sec12-card-sec12-F24.teaching_text: Convicted offenders reimburse lab testing directly through a mandatory sixty-dollar chemical analysis fee.

sec12-card-sec12-F25.question_text: Which five lane-keeping and steering mistakes warn you another driver on the road may be impaired?
sec12-card-sec12-F25.teaching_text: Spotting wide swings, line-straddling, near misses, or wrong-way drift lets you hang way back and call police.

sec12-card-sec12-F26.question_text: Which speed, braking, reaction, and nighttime-headlight behaviors point to an impaired driver?
sec12-card-sec12-F26.teaching_text: Impaired drivers often overcompensate by crawling, stopping mid-lane randomly, jerking brakes, or forgetting night headlights.

sec12-card-sec12-R11.question_text: Which tailgating, multi-lane, turn-lane, and overcorrection clues also warn of an impaired motorist?
sec12-card-sec12-R11.teaching_text: Blasting straight ahead out of a turn-only lane or whipping back onto pavement signals severe impairment.

sec12-card-sec12-F28.question_text: Does a suspended or revoked Nevada license ever turn valid automatically when time runs out?
sec12-card-sec12-F28.teaching_text: Driving the day after your suspension calendar ends is still illegal until you reapply, show documents, and pay fees.

sec12-card-sec12-R13.question_text: Beyond reapplying with documents and fees, how can certain juvenile offenses affect unissued teen licenses?
sec12-card-sec12-R13.teaching_text: Even before a teen holds a license, juvenile violations can push back the date they qualify to get one.

sec12-card-sec12-F29.question_text: Which three major on-road grounds suspend or revoke a Nevada license?
sec12-card-sec12-F29.teaching_text: Hitting twelve demerit points, failing or convicted of impaired driving, or striking a walker or cyclist pulls privileges.
sec12-card-sec12-F29.must_match_memory_hook: Twelve points, impaired driving, walker-bike hits

visual_sync.text_span: Twelve points, impaired driving, walker-bike hits

sec12-card-sec12-F30.question_text: What happens to your driving privilege if you ignore a required traffic-ticket court appearance?
sec12-card-sec12-F30.teaching_text: Ignoring a minor traffic citation turns a payable ticket into a license suspension and bench-warrant headache.

sec12-card-sec12-F31.question_text: What dual penalty hits if you crash without insurance and damage or injury exceeds seven hundred fifty dollars?
sec12-card-sec12-F31.teaching_text: Crossing seven hundred fifty dollars uninsured freezes both your right to drive and your car's registration plates.

sec12-card-sec12-F32.question_text: Which three insurance-maintenance failures trigger a license or registration suspension?
sec12-card-sec12-F32.teaching_text: Failing to file required proof, getting convicted of driving uninsured, or stacking lapses shuts privileges down.
sec12-card-sec12-F32.must_match_memory_hook: Missing proof, uninsured conviction, repeat lapses

visual_sync.text_span: Missing proof, uninsured conviction, repeat lapses

sec12-card-sec12-F33.question_text: Which three court, vandalism, or exhibition offenses can cost your Nevada license?
sec12-card-sec12-F33.teaching_text: Unpaid child support, spray-paint graffiti convictions, and street racing or trick shows all strip driving privileges.

sec12-card-sec12-R14.question_text: Who is covered—and on which properties—under Nevada's street-racing and trick-driving suspension law?
sec12-card-sec12-R14.teaching_text: Setting up cones in an open shopping-center parking lot or promoting a sideshow suspends organizers alongside drivers.
sec12-card-sec12-R14.must_match_memory_hook: Drivers and organizers; streets, public lots

visual_sync.text_span: Drivers and organizers; streets, public lots

sec12-card-sec12-F34.question_text: Which weapon, alcohol, and drug offenses can strip a juvenile's Nevada driver license?
sec12-card-sec12-F34.teaching_text: Juveniles lose licenses for firearm offenses or possessing alcohol or drugs even nowhere near a motor vehicle.

sec05-card-sec05-F01.question_text: What is the number-one cause of crashes in Nevada, and which three qualities do yielding rules depend on?
sec05-card-sec05-F01.teaching_text: Failing to yield tops Nevada's collision stats because safe intersections rely on shared courtesy, common sense, and cooperation.

sec05-card-sec05-F02.question_text: Does Nevada law ever grant someone automatic right-of-way, and what duty stays on the driver who may go first?
sec05-card-sec05-F02.teaching_text: Insisting on going first when another driver blows a stop sign still breaks your legal duty to avoid collisions.

sec05-card-sec05-F03.question_text: At a Nevada intersection with no signs or signals, which vehicle should usually proceed first?
sec05-card-sec05-F03.teaching_text: Neighborhood corners without signs demand an early foot off the gas so cars to your right clear safely.

sec05-card-sec05-F04.question_text: Between a vehicle already inside the intersection and one just arriving, which goes first?
sec05-card-sec05-F04.teaching_text: Approaching drivers must let anyone already crossing clear the intersection box before nosing into lanes.

sec05-card-sec05-F05.question_text: Who holds priority between a straight-through vehicle already in the intersection and a left-turning vehicle, and when may the left-turner go?
sec05-card-sec05-F05.teaching_text: Cutting left across oncoming straight traffic causes broadside impacts unless you signal, yield, and take an open gap.

sec05-card-sec05-F06.question_text: To whom must you yield when pulling onto a main road from a minor street, private road, or driveway?
sec05-card-sec05-F06.teaching_text: Pulling out of a shopping plaza or side lane puts both sidewalk pedestrians and main-road vehicles ahead of you.

sec05-card-sec05-R02.question_text: How do the yield duties pair up for a left-turning intersection driver and a driver exiting a driveway?
sec05-card-sec05-R02.teaching_text: Exam scenarios combine both rules—left-turners yield to straight intersection cars while driveway exits yield to cars and walkers.

sec05-card-sec05-F07.question_text: What must you do immediately when an emergency vehicle with flashing lights or a siren approaches from any direction?
sec05-card-sec05-F07.teaching_text: Stopping inside an intersection traps fire engines and ambulances right where they need turning space most.

sec05-card-sec05-F08.question_text: Who goes first at a Nevada four-way stop, and what must that driver still do before moving?
sec05-card-sec05-F08.teaching_text: Arriving earliest never excuses rolling the sign—you still owe a complete stop before claiming your turn.

sec05-card-sec05-R01.question_text: How does priority at an uncontrolled intersection differ from priority at a four-way stop?
sec05-card-sec05-R01.teaching_text: Test writers mix up these two—no signs favors the right-hand car, whereas four stop signs go by arrival order.

sec05-card-sec05-F09.question_text: Who must yield when entering a freeway from an on-ramp?
sec05-card-sec05-F09.teaching_text: Through-lane freeway vehicles never owe an entering car their spot—you time your merge into a safe gap.

sec05-card-sec05-F10.question_text: What is your duty toward bicyclists riding inside a bike lane or along a bike path?
sec05-card-sec05-F10.teaching_text: Turning right across a striped bike lane without yielding causes classic right-hook crashes with cyclists.

sec05-card-sec05-F11.question_text: How must Nevada drivers treat a funeral procession traveling with headlights switched on?
sec05-card-sec05-F11.teaching_text: Cutting between cars displaying lit headlights breaks up the escort group and violates procession yield rules.

sec05-card-sec05-F12.question_text: Who holds priority at crosswalks and intersections, and what precaution should pedestrians still take before stepping off?
sec05-card-sec05-F12.teaching_text: Legal crosswalk priority will not stop heavy steel if a distracted driver misses your step off the curb.

sec05-card-sec05-F13.question_text: What must you do when a blind or visually impaired pedestrian approaches with a guide animal or white cane?
sec05-card-sec05-F13.teaching_text: Nevada law grants absolute pedestrian priority to service-animal and white-cane users, requiring full stops whenever needed.

sec05-card-sec05-F14.question_text: Beyond posted signs, which road, traffic, visibility, and terrain factors must you weigh under Nevada's Basic Rule?
sec05-card-sec05-F14.teaching_text: Steep curvy mountain grades, narrow shoulders, heavy trucks, or rain all lower what counts as reasonable speed.
sec05-card-sec05-F14.must_match_memory_hook: Match speed to road, weather, traffic

visual_sync.text_span: Match speed to road, weather, traffic

sec05-card-sec05-F15.question_text: How can your legally safe speed compare with the posted speed limit when conditions deteriorate?
sec05-card-sec05-F15.teaching_text: Driving the full posted number through dust storms or black ice still draws a Basic Rule citation.

sec05-card-sec05-R04.question_text: How does a posted speed limit sign interact with Nevada's Basic Rule?
sec05-card-sec05-R04.teaching_text: Think of the sign as a fair-weather ceiling while the Basic Rule pulls your legal speed down in hazards.

sec05-card-sec05-F16.question_text: What example Nevada speed limits apply in school zones and in business or residential areas?
sec05-card-sec05-F16.teaching_text: Nevada school zones use both fifteen and twenty-five depending on signage, while business and residential streets run twenty-five.

sec05-card-sec05-F17.question_text: What example Nevada speed limits apply approaching towns, on urban freeways or rural highways, and on rural interstates?
sec05-card-sec05-F17.teaching_text: Step down cleanly from seventy-plus on open interstates to sixty-five and then forty-five entering town transitions.

sec05-card-sec05-F18.question_text: Why must you drop below posted speed limits when bad weather cuts visibility or slicks pavement?
sec05-card-sec05-F18.teaching_text: Engineers calculate sign numbers for dry tires and clear sightlines, leaving zero margin on slick pavement.

sec05-card-sec05-F19.question_text: Where must slower traffic travel when two or more lanes run in the same direction?
sec05-card-sec05-F19.teaching_text: Camping slowly in left lanes triggers sudden braking and risky right-side passes behind you.

sec05-card-sec05-F20.question_text: Over a five-mile stretch, how few seconds do you save driving seventy miles per hour instead of sixty?
sec05-card-sec05-F20.teaching_text: Risking a crash or citation over five miles buys less than one single red-light cycle.

sec05-card-sec05-R03.question_text: How much time does driving seventy instead of sixty save over fifteen miles, and what wipes out that gain?
sec05-card-sec05-R03.teaching_text: One fifteen-minute roadside speeding ticket erases weeks of two-minute commute shortcuts plus hundreds of dollars.

sec05-card-sec05-F21.question_text: Which design features make freeways generally the safest roads per mile?
sec05-card-sec05-F21.teaching_text: Eliminating cross-traffic signals, train tracks, and tight curves removes the deadliest conflict angles.

sec05-card-sec05-F22.question_text: Which four preparation checks should you handle before starting a freeway trip?
sec05-card-sec05-F22.teaching_text: Running dry on long Nevada stretches or hunting exit numbers at seventy invites avoidable emergencies.

sec05-card-sec05-F23.question_text: How must you enter a freeway, and which two signs warn that you picked an exit ramp by mistake?
sec05-card-sec05-F23.teaching_text: Red Do Not Enter and Wrong Way signs flank off-ramp throats to stop head-on freeway entries.

sec05-card-sec05-F24.question_text: How should you use the freeway acceleration lane, and why should you avoid stopping before merging?
sec05-card-sec05-F24.teaching_text: Stopping dead at the ramp tip forces you to launch from zero into seventy-mile-per-hour traffic.

sec05-card-sec05-R05.question_text: How do responsibilities differ between a driver merging onto a freeway and drivers already on it?
sec05-card-sec05-R05.teaching_text: Entering cars carry the legal yield duty, while courteous mainline drivers ease gas or move left to help.

sec05-card-sec05-F25.question_text: Why does freeway traffic often move briskly compared with surface highways of the same limit, and how should you pace yourself?
sec05-card-sec05-F25.teaching_text: Uninterrupted flow without signals keeps speeds brisk and uniform, so pace smoothly within legal limits.

sec05-card-sec05-F26.question_text: Who belongs in the far-left lane on a multi-lane freeway, and why should you skip weaving between lanes?
sec05-card-sec05-F26.teaching_text: Constant lane hopping spikes blind-spot sideswipes while saving virtually zero arrival time.

sec05-card-sec05-F27.question_text: At least how many seconds ahead should you scan on a freeway, and what movements should you watch for?
sec05-card-sec05-F27.teaching_text: High freeway speeds cover a quarter mile quickly, demanding early sight of brake waves and lane shifts.

sec05-card-sec05-R06.question_text: Which four checks and signals belong before every freeway lane change?
sec05-card-sec05-R06.teaching_text: Two cars two lanes apart can merge into the same middle lane unless you watch other blinkers too.

sec05-card-sec05-F28.question_text: How do you use an on-ramp meter when its signal lights are operating?
sec05-card-sec05-F28.teaching_text: Ramp meters cycle much quicker than street intersections to space entering cars one-by-one into mainline gaps.

sec05-card-sec05-R07.question_text: How should drivers use a multi-lane freeway on-ramp equipped with separate ramp meters?
sec05-card-sec05-R07.teaching_text: Spreading across both ramp lanes prevents backups onto city streets while staggered greens alternate merges.

sec05-card-sec05-F29.question_text: How is an HOV bypass lane marked on a metered ramp, and who may roll past the meter without stopping?
sec05-card-sec05-F29.teaching_text: Unmetered diamond bypass lanes reward vehicles carrying two or more occupants with nonstop ramp entry.

sec05-card-sec05-F30.question_text: What does an overhead freeway lane signal showing a downward green arrow with OPEN mean?
sec05-card-sec05-F30.teaching_text: A downward green arrow confirms the lane directly underneath is clear for normal posted-speed travel.

sec05-card-sec05-F31.question_text: How does an overhead yellow X with CAUTION differ from a yellow X with MERGE?
sec05-card-sec05-F31.teaching_text: Both yellow signals warn ahead—CAUTION flags slowdowns or debris while MERGE tells you the lane is closing.

sec05-card-sec05-F32.question_text: What must you do when an overhead lane-use signal displays a red X with CLOSED?
sec05-card-sec05-F32.teaching_text: Red X lanes often shield crash responders or stalled cars directly ahead—stay out and merge open.

sec05-card-sec05-R08.question_text: What is the core usability difference between a yellow X lane signal and a red X lane signal?
sec05-card-sec05-R08.teaching_text: You can still travel carefully or prepare to merge under yellow, whereas red forbids driving there at all.

sec05-card-sec05-R09.question_text: How do overhead freeway gantry signs guide you before, near, and past a crash or work zone?
sec05-card-sec05-R09.teaching_text: Active overhead boards step speeds down approaching trouble and restore green open arrows once you pass it.

sec05-card-sec05-F33.question_text: How many occupants do Nevada HOV lanes require, where are active hours listed, and which two vehicle types are exempt?
sec05-card-sec05-F33.teaching_text: Motorcycles and active emergency rigs qualify solo, while hours change by corridor on regulatory signs.

sec05-card-sec05-F34.question_text: Which two categories of multi-axle or towing vehicles are barred from Nevada HOV lanes?
sec05-card-sec05-F34.teaching_text: Even with four passengers aboard, towing a boat or driving three axles bans you from carpool lanes.

sec05-card-sec05-F35.question_text: Where may you legally cross into or out of a Nevada carpool lane, and what white line forbids crossing?
sec05-card-sec05-F35.teaching_text: Weaving across double solid white buffer lines draws hefty carpool-lane citations and sideswipe risk.

sec05-card-sec05-R10.question_text: Which three transportation goals are HOV lanes built to achieve?
sec05-card-sec05-R10.teaching_text: Packing more commuters into shared cars and buses frees space across every adjacent general lane too.

sec05-card-sec05-F36.question_text: Where should you begin slowing down when exiting a freeway, and to what target speed?
sec05-card-sec05-F36.teaching_text: Braking early on mainline freeway lanes invites seventy-mile-per-hour rear-end collisions before the ramp.

sec05-card-sec05-F37.question_text: How far ahead of your freeway exit should you signal and move into the proper exit lane?
sec05-card-sec05-F37.teaching_text: Lining up a full mile ahead prevents desperate three-lane dives across solid gore stripes.

sec05-card-sec05-R11.question_text: How does Nevada's freeway exit numbering system help you prepare to leave?
sec05-card-sec05-R11.teaching_text: Matching your route's exit number to advance overhead boards gives plenty of warning before ramps appear.

sec05-card-sec05-F38.question_text: What must you do—and never do—if you accidentally pass your freeway exit?
sec05-card-sec05-F38.teaching_text: Backing up on a freeway shoulder or cutting across medians causes catastrophic high-speed collisions.

sec05-card-sec05-F39.question_text: How do you make an emergency stop with four-wheel anti-lock brakes, and why?
sec05-card-sec05-F39.teaching_text: Computerized valves pulse wheel grip far faster than human feet while keeping front tires rolling to steer.

sec05-card-sec05-F40.question_text: What does it mean if the dashboard ABS warning light stays illuminated long after starting the engine?
sec05-card-sec05-F40.teaching_text: You still have normal hydraulic stopping power, though wheels can lock up under panic braking until serviced.

sec05-card-sec05-F41.question_text: What pedal habit switches off anti-lock braking right in the middle of an emergency stop?
sec05-card-sec05-F41.teaching_text: Old-school brake pumping or lifting off steady pressure cancels rapid computer pulsing when you need it most.

sec05-card-sec05-R12.question_text: Which three ways can tell you whether an unfamiliar vehicle is equipped with anti-lock brakes?
sec05-card-sec05-R12.teaching_text: Knowing before an emergency whether you have ABS tells your foot whether to hold firm or modulate.

sec05-card-sec05-R13.question_text: Why must you steer smoothly rather than jerking the wheel during an anti-lock brake stop?
sec05-card-sec05-R13.teaching_text: Because ABS keeps front tires gripping, yanking the wheel hard flings the car onto shoulders or other lanes.

sec05-card-sec05-R14.question_text: How does rear-wheel ABS on some light trucks differ from four-wheel ABS if the front tires lock?
sec05-card-sec05-R14.teaching_text: Rear-only ABS stops spinouts yet leaves front wheels able to skid straight unless you ease pedal pressure.

sec05-card-sec05-F42.question_text: Which type of collision happens more often than any other on Nevada streets and highways?
sec05-card-sec05-F42.teaching_text: Tailgating and misjudged stopping distance combine to make rear-end impacts Nevada's most common crash.

sec05-card-sec05-R15.question_text: Which vehicle, driver, and environmental factors determine total stopping distance?
sec05-card-sec05-R15.teaching_text: Heavy cargo, worn tread, wet asphalt, or drowsy reactions each stretch out how many feet you roll.

sec05-card-sec05-R16.question_text: How do perception and reaction work together before physical braking even starts?
sec05-card-sec05-R16.teaching_text: Your car rolls dozens of unbraked feet while eyes recognize trouble and your right foot swings over.

sec05-card-sec05-F44.question_text: What do highway safety studies give as normal reaction time, and what makes it longer?
sec05-card-sec05-F44.teaching_text: Complex traffic puzzles or surprise obstacles stretch reaction past two and a half seconds in live driving.

sec05-card-sec05-R17.question_text: What is the exact difference between braking time and braking distance?
sec05-card-sec05-R17.teaching_text: Braking time counts the clock while brakes and tires grip, whereas braking distance measures pavement covered.

sec05-card-sec05-F43.question_text: When you double your driving speed—say from thirty to sixty—how much longer does braking distance become?
sec05-card-sec05-F43.teaching_text: Kinetic energy squares with speed, turning a double-speed jump into four times the braking distance.

sec05-card-sec05-R18.question_text: How much can wet pavement increase stopping distance, and why is a season's first rain extra slick?
sec05-card-sec05-R18.teaching_text: Months of dripped engine oil rise onto fresh rainwater, creating a greasy film before heavy downpours wash it off.

sec05-card-sec05-F45.question_text: Between what speeds do most cars begin losing traction and hydroplaning in heavy rain?
sec05-card-sec05-F45.teaching_text: Tires ride up on a wedge of water well below highway limits, disconnecting steering and brakes.

sec05-card-sec05-R19.question_text: At just thirty miles per hour on ice, how many feet does stopping take?
sec05-card-sec05-R19.teaching_text: Sliding longer than an entire football field from neighborhood speed shows why ice demands crawling pace.

sec05-card-sec05-R20.question_text: On dry level pavement at twenty-five miles per hour, what is total stopping distance and its perception-reaction versus braking split?
sec05-card-sec05-R20.teaching_text: Notice over two-thirds of that one-hundred-twenty-seven-foot stop happens before brake pads even clamp down.

sec05-card-sec05-R21.question_text: In the dry-pavement table at forty-five miles per hour, what is total stopping distance and its two parts?
sec05-card-sec05-R21.teaching_text: Adding twenty miles per hour more than doubles total stopping distance to two hundred seventy-eight feet.
sec05-card-sec05-R21.must_match_memory_hook: Two seventy-eight total, one sixty-five reaction

visual_sync.text_span: Two seventy-eight total, one sixty-five reaction

sec07-card-sec07-F01.question_text: Which driving tasks do advanced driver assistance systems help with, and what can they NOT do?
sec07-card-sec07-F01.teaching_text: Sensors help with lanes, blind spots, crashes, and spacing, yet none turn your car into a self-driving chauffeur.

sec07-card-sec07-F02.question_text: Which three sensory alerts do vehicle warning systems use, and what two problems do they warn about?
sec07-card-sec07-F02.teaching_text: Chimes, dash icons, and seat or wheel buzzes grab your attention for impending crashes or equipment faults.

sec07-card-sec07-F03.question_text: What does it mean that most vehicle warning systems are passive?
sec07-card-sec07-F03.teaching_text: Passive alerts ring the alarm bell while leaving every ounce of braking and steering up to your hands and feet.

sec07-card-sec07-R01.question_text: What is the primary job of vehicle warning technologies?
sec07-card-sec07-R01.teaching_text: Whether a bumper closes fast ahead or a sensor faults out, warning tech exists first to wake driver attention.

sec07-card-sec07-F04.question_text: When does a back-up warning activate, how does it alert you, and what checks must you still perform?
sec07-card-sec07-F04.teaching_text: Bumper ultrasonic sensors can miss low curbs or fast-running toddlers unless you check mirrors, cameras, and over your shoulder.

sec07-card-sec07-F05.question_text: How does a blind-spot monitor alert you—especially when signaling—and what must you still do before changing lanes?
sec07-card-sec07-F05.teaching_text: Mirror icons and chimes escalate if you signal toward a hidden car, yet motorcycles still require mirror and shoulder glances.

sec07-card-sec07-F06.question_text: When does a rear camera switch on, and does its video view replace mirror and shoulder checks?
sec07-card-sec07-F06.teaching_text: Wide-angle tailgate lenses still miss cross-lane traffic approaching outside the frame until you turn your head.

sec07-card-sec07-R02.question_text: Where inside different vehicles might the rear-camera video feed appear?
sec07-card-sec07-R02.teaching_text: Check an unfamiliar rental car's mirror, visor, and dash screen before backing out of a tight lot.

sec07-card-sec07-F07.question_text: When does a sideview camera show an enlarged lane view, and how should you pair it?
sec07-card-sec07-F07.teaching_text: Video feeds shrink depth perception at speed, so treat sideview cameras like blind-spot helpers alongside mirrors and head turns.

sec07-card-sec07-R03.question_text: What exterior hardware do some newer vehicles replace with sideview cameras?
sec07-card-sec07-R03.teaching_text: Compact exterior camera pods feed interior displays where glass side mirrors used to sit.

sec07-card-sec07-F08.question_text: How does a surround-view monitor help during parking, and what habits remain required?
sec07-card-sec07-F08.teaching_text: Stitched top-down views line up curbs and stripes cleanly while direct mirror and shoulder scans catch moving people.

sec07-card-sec07-R04.question_text: Where are the cameras mounted in most surround-view systems, and what extra alert do some include?
sec07-card-sec07-R04.teaching_text: Combining a center nose lens with downward mirror cameras builds the perimeter view and triggers close-obstacle beeps.

sec07-card-sec07-F09.question_text: When does a curve speed warning trigger, and who remains responsible for picking a safe speed?
sec07-card-sec07-F09.teaching_text: Navigation-linked curve alerts cannot feel ice or gravel under your tires, leaving speed control squarely on you.

sec07-card-sec07-F10.question_text: Around what speed range does pedestrian, bicycle, and obstacle detection operate, and what do some versions add?
sec07-card-sec07-F10.teaching_text: City-speed sensors around twenty-five miles per hour can spot walkers and even trigger automatic braking on equipped models.

sec07-card-sec07-F11.question_text: What does it mean when obstacle-detection beeps speed up and turn into a continuous tone?
sec07-card-sec07-F11.teaching_text: Faster chirps track shrinking inches until a solid tone warns impact is moments away.

sec07-card-sec07-R05.question_text: What blind angle limits some pedestrian or cyclist detection systems, and where should you verify your car's limits?
sec07-card-sec07-R05.teaching_text: Cross-street runners or oncoming bikes can slip outside forward-only cones, making owner's manual study essential.

sec07-card-sec07-F12.question_text: Why must you never rely on pedestrian, bicycle, or obstacle sensors—especially on city streets?
sec07-card-sec07-F12.teaching_text: Parked vans, rain glare, and crowded corners fool sensors where human eyes anticipate movement.

sec07-card-sec07-F13.question_text: What does a forward collision warning scan for, and does the warning system apply the brakes itself?
sec07-card-sec07-F13.teaching_text: Confusing a passive forward collision warning with automatic emergency braking leaves the brake pedal untouched.

sec07-card-sec07-F14.question_text: How does a lane departure warning alert you when your tires drift toward a lane stripe?
sec07-card-sec07-F14.teaching_text: Camera-read paint stripes fire chimes or wheel buzzes when you drift without a turn signal.

sec07-card-sec07-R11.question_text: Who does the steering when a standard lane departure warning goes off?
sec07-card-sec07-R11.teaching_text: Unlike active lane-keeping assist, a lane departure warning never turns the steering rack for you.

sec07-card-sec07-F15.question_text: What does a constant solid tone from bumper parking sensors tell you?
sec07-card-sec07-F15.teaching_text: Once pulsing beeps fuse into a constant tone, bumper contact is inches away.

sec07-card-sec07-F16.question_text: What specific hazard does a rear cross-traffic alert watch for while you back out?
sec07-card-sec07-F16.teaching_text: Corner radar spots aisle cars approaching behind tall SUVs before your rear window clears them.

sec07-card-sec07-R08.question_text: When does a high-speed alert chime, and how does it help?
sec07-card-sec07-R08.teaching_text: Audible speed reminders catch accidental highway creep before a patrol radar does.

sec07-card-sec07-F17.question_text: How do active driver-assistance technologies go beyond passive warnings in certain situations?
sec07-card-sec07-F17.teaching_text: Active systems step in physically to brake or nudge steering when specific crash triggers fire.

sec07-card-sec07-R10.question_text: What makes a vehicle feature count as a safety-critical technology?
sec07-card-sec07-R10.teaching_text: Features that stop impacts outright or scrub off crash energy sit in the safety-critical tier.

sec07-card-sec07-F18.question_text: When does automatic emergency braking clamp the brakes hard, and what two habits must you keep anyway?
sec07-card-sec07-F18.teaching_text: Slick roads or late sensor locks still crash tailgaters, so scan ahead and hold safe following gaps.

sec07-card-sec07-R06.question_text: What is the exact difference between forward collision warning and automatic emergency braking?
sec07-card-sec07-R06.teaching_text: Test questions pit these twins directly—one only sounds the alarm while the other hits the brakes.

sec07-card-sec07-F19.question_text: What two steps does automatic reverse braking take when an obstacle appears behind you?
sec07-card-sec07-F19.teaching_text: If you miss the reverse beep for a shopping cart or post, the system clamps the brakes immediately.

sec07-card-sec07-R07.question_text: How does a rear cross-traffic alert differ from automatic reverse braking?
sec07-card-sec07-R07.teaching_text: Rear cross-traffic alerts only chime for approaching aisle cars, while automatic reverse braking physically halts the car.

sec07-card-sec07-F20.question_text: How does lane-keeping assist act when you drift, what cancels it, and when does it fail to see lanes?
sec07-card-sec07-F20.teaching_text: A light wheel nudge overrides it, and snow, dirt, or faded paint blinds its lane camera completely.

sec07-card-sec07-F21.question_text: What can left-turn crash avoidance do during a low-speed left turn, and who still judges safe gaps?
sec07-card-sec07-F21.teaching_text: Emergency turn braking is a last-ditch safety net, never a substitute for reading oncoming speed yourself.

sec07-card-sec07-R09.question_text: If active safety tech reacts to a sudden hazard during your Nevada driving test, how is it scored?
sec07-card-sec07-R09.teaching_text: Examiners weigh whether a surprise cut-in or your own inattention triggered the car's emergency intervention.

sec07-card-sec07-F22.question_text: May you use convenience features like adaptive cruise control or automatic parallel parking during a Nevada driving exam?
sec07-card-sec07-F22.teaching_text: Examiners test your own footwork and parallel-parking skill, not what computer buttons your car bought.

sec07-card-sec07-F23.question_text: What does adaptive cruise control manage, and when does the handbook advise switching it off?
sec07-card-sec07-F23.teaching_text: Rain, snow, and slick roads confuse radar spacing and risk wheel spin if cruise accelerates or brakes.

sec07-card-sec07-R12.question_text: What three steps set up adaptive cruise control, and what extra capability do advanced versions add?
sec07-card-sec07-R12.teaching_text: After picking short, medium, or long spacing, stop-and-go versions can even halt and resume in traffic.
sec07-card-sec07-R12.must_match_memory_hook: Reach speed, switch on, pick gap

visual_sync.text_span: Reach speed, switch on, pick gap

sec07-card-sec07-R13.question_text: During automatic parallel parking, what does the car handle and what two duties stay with the driver?
sec07-card-sec07-R13.teaching_text: Letting go of the wheel when prompted never lets go of brake control and scanning all around.

sec07-card-sec07-R14.question_text: What number range does the Society of Automotive Engineers use to classify driving automation from none to self-driving?
sec07-card-sec07-R14.teaching_text: Zero marks zero automation hardware while five marks full self-driving capability everywhere.

sec07-card-sec07-F24.question_text: Which SAE automation tiers qualify a vehicle as autonomous under Nevada law?
sec07-card-sec07-F24.teaching_text: Everyday cars with cruise and lane assist sit at one or two—Nevada reserves autonomous status for three through five.

sec08-card-sec08-F01.question_text: What visibility limits and oncoming hazard make night driving always riskier than daytime driving?
sec08-card-sec08-F01.teaching_text: Darkness shrinks both how far and how early hazards appear while oncoming headlights dazzle your retinas.

sec08-card-sec08-F02.question_text: How fast may you safely travel at night relative to the beam of your headlights?
sec08-card-sec08-F02.teaching_text: If your stopping distance stretches past your beam edge, an unlit deer or stalled car is unavoidable.

sec08-card-sec08-F03.question_text: Where should you aim your eyes when bright oncoming headlights shine toward you at night?
sec08-card-sec08-F03.teaching_text: Tracking the right-side edge stripe keeps your car centered without blinding your night-adapted pupils.

sec08-card-sec08-F04.question_text: What two rules cover sunglasses and windshield cleanliness for night driving?
sec08-card-sec08-F04.teaching_text: Dark lenses starve night vision while interior haze scatters every oncoming headlight into a bright halo.
sec08-card-sec08-F04.must_match_memory_hook: Zero sunglasses, clean glass both sides

visual_sync.text_span: Zero sunglasses, clean glass both sides

sec08-card-sec08-R02.question_text: Why do pedestrians require extra driver vigilance after dark?
sec08-card-sec08-R02.teaching_text: Dark jackets absorb low-beam light until walkers step right across crosswalks or unlit shoulders.

sec08-card-sec08-R03.question_text: What share and count of Nevada fatal crashes occurred between six in the evening and eight fifty-nine at night in the handbook report?
sec08-card-sec08-R03.teaching_text: Dusk glare, rush-hour volume, and fading light packed two hundred seventy-six fatal crashes into three evening hours.

sec08-card-sec08-F05.question_text: During what clock window and visibility distance are headlights legally required in Nevada?
sec08-card-sec08-F05.teaching_text: Switch low beams on from thirty minutes after sunset to thirty before sunrise or whenever sight drops under one thousand feet.

sec08-card-sec08-F06.question_text: Besides dusk-to-dawn and low sightlines, when else are headlights legally required or strongly advisable?
sec08-card-sec08-F06.teaching_text: Daylight headlight corridors mandate beams by sign, while rain, snow, and fog make low beams vital so others spot you.
sec08-card-sec08-F06.must_match_memory_hook: Required by signs, smart in storms

visual_sync.text_span: Required by signs, smart in storms

sec08-card-sec08-F07.question_text: Where do high beams belong at night, and at what distances must you dim for oncoming versus followed vehicles?
sec08-card-sec08-F07.teaching_text: Blinding an oncoming driver or dazzling someone's rearview mirror inside three hundred feet endangers both lanes.
sec08-card-sec08-F07.must_match_memory_hook: Five hundred oncoming, three hundred behind

visual_sync.text_span: Five hundred oncoming, three hundred behind

sec08-card-sec08-R01.question_text: How do Nevada's two high-beam dimming distances compare between meeting and following another vehicle?
sec08-card-sec08-R01.teaching_text: Head-on windshields take full glare at five hundred feet, whereas taillights ahead require dimming at three hundred.

sec08-card-sec08-F08.question_text: Is driving with only parking lights legal, and how may headlights warn a driver ahead before passing?
sec08-card-sec08-F08.teaching_text: Parking lights cast zero road illumination while moving, whereas a brief headlight flash alerts a car you plan to pass.

sec08-card-sec08-F09.question_text: What is the single most important adjustment in bad weather, and how much longer can slippery stops stretch?
sec08-card-sec08-F09.teaching_text: When slick asphalt multiplies stopping distance two to ten times over, only dropping speed buys survival room.

sec08-card-sec08-R04.question_text: Why must you widen following space and track taillights closely in Nevada wind, fog, rain, or snow?
sec08-card-sec08-R04.teaching_text: Desert squalls and mountain snow hit fast, blinding nearby drivers just as badly as they blind you.

sec08-card-sec08-F10.question_text: Which three tire setups help on snowy or icy roads, and do they make sliding impossible?
sec08-card-sec08-F10.teaching_text: Overconfident drivers with chains or snow tires crash first because ice still breaks traction at excessive speed.

sec08-card-sec08-F11.question_text: How should you pull away, check stopping grip, and approach corners on snow or ice?
sec08-card-sec08-F11.teaching_text: A gentle early brake check reveals black ice before you roll fast toward a red light.
sec08-card-sec08-F11.must_match_memory_hook: Start gently, test brakes, slow early

visual_sync.text_span: Start gently, test brakes, slow early

sec08-card-sec08-F12.question_text: Why is no single speed ever completely safe on snowy or icy roads?
sec08-card-sec08-F12.teaching_text: Dry-looking sunlit asphalt turns to glare ice inside canyon shadows or unsanded bridges fifty yards ahead.

sec08-card-sec08-F13.question_text: How does slippery-road braking technique differ between standard brakes and anti-lock brakes?
sec08-card-sec08-F13.teaching_text: Non-ABS brakes need gentle touch-and-release modulation, whereas ABS demands steady pressure to pulse.
sec08-card-sec08-F13.must_match_memory_hook: Light taps without, firm hold ABS

visual_sync.text_span: Light taps without, firm hold ABS

sec08-card-sec08-R05.question_text: Why should you check your owner's manual before winter arrives regarding ice braking?
sec08-card-sec08-R05.teaching_text: Mixing up non-ABS touch-and-release with firm continuous ABS pressure ruins stopping grip on glare ice.

sec08-card-sec08-R06.question_text: Which three preparation and control habits keep snow and ice trips safer?
sec08-card-sec08-R06.teaching_text: Scraping peepholes in frost or rushing late forces jerky steering and braking that break winter traction.
sec08-card-sec08-R06.must_match_memory_hook: Smooth inputs, clear glass, extra time

visual_sync.text_span: Smooth inputs, clear glass, extra time

sec08-card-sec08-F14.question_text: Between which exact calendar dates may studded snow tires—or engaged retractable studs—be driven in Nevada?
sec08-card-sec08-F14.teaching_text: Metal studs chew up dry summer asphalt, making May-through-September stud engagement illegal in Nevada.

sec08-card-sec08-F15.question_text: What does skidding mean physically, and on which four surfaces does it happen?
sec08-card-sec08-F15.teaching_text: Beyond packed snow and ice, wet rain slicks and loose gravel shoulders break tire bite too.
sec08-card-sec08-F15.must_match_memory_hook: Lost tire grip across slick surfaces

visual_sync.text_span: Lost tire grip across slick surfaces

sec08-card-sec08-R07.question_text: Why should you check your owner's manual for skid recovery, and what mindset comes first?
sec08-card-sec08-R07.teaching_text: Front-wheel, four-wheel, and ABS setups respond differently in slides, while panic over-correction spins every car.

sec08-card-sec08-F16.question_text: What sequence should you follow if your service brakes fail, and which gear position is forbidden?
sec08-card-sec08-F16.teaching_text: Pumping may rebuild hydraulic pressure, while engine braking and the parking brake slow you without locking transmission teeth in park.
sec08-card-sec08-F16.must_match_memory_hook: Pump, parking brake, downshift, never park

visual_sync.text_span: Pump, parking brake, downshift, never park

sec08-card-sec08-R09.question_text: Why should you shift into a lower gear before descending a long downhill stretch?
sec08-card-sec08-R09.teaching_text: Riding brake pedals down mountain passes overheats pads until stopping power fades out completely.

sec08-card-sec08-F18.question_text: What steps handle a stuck gas pedal from first quick try to safe roadside stop?
sec08-card-sec08-F18.teaching_text: If a sharp tap does not free it, neutral disconnects runaway engine power immediately while power brakes and steering stay live.

sec08-card-sec08-R08.question_text: How does your gearshift move differ between failed brakes and a stuck gas pedal, and what stays banned in both?
sec08-card-sec08-R08.teaching_text: Failed brakes need engine drag in low gear, stuck gas needs neutral disconnection, and neither ever touches park.

sec08-card-sec08-F17.question_text: How do you test and dry out wet brakes after driving through deep water?
sec08-card-sec08-F17.teaching_text: Soaked pads grab unevenly or slip completely until light friction heat dries them every two hundred feet.
sec08-card-sec08-F17.must_match_memory_hook: Low gear, light brake, test two-hundred

visual_sync.text_span: Low gear, light brake, test two-hundred

sec08-card-sec08-R10.question_text: What should you do if your windshield wipers quit working during heavy rain or snow?
sec08-card-sec08-R10.teaching_text: Rolling down the side window gives just enough sightline to steer safely off the right shoulder.

sec08-card-sec08-R11.question_text: How can you guide yourself off the road if your headlights suddenly fail at night?
sec08-card-sec08-R11.teaching_text: Parking lamps, turn blinkers, and four-way flashers run on separate circuits that shed enough glow to reach the shoulder.

sec08-card-sec08-F19.question_text: What immediate steps belong when smoke rises from under your hood?
sec08-card-sec08-F19.teaching_text: Shutting off the ignition stops fuel pumps, and cracking a hot hood carelessly can feed oxygen to flames.
sec08-card-sec08-F19.must_match_memory_hook: Pull off, cut ignition, hood care

visual_sync.text_span: Pull off, cut ignition, hood care

sec08-card-sec08-F20.question_text: Why must you never throw water on a vehicle fire, what works instead, and how far back do you retreat if unstoppable?
sec08-card-sec08-F20.teaching_text: Burning gasoline floats on water and spreads flames, so use chemical extinguishers or dirt—or retreat one hundred feet.

sec08-card-sec08-F21.question_text: When steering fails, how does your braking choice depend on whether the car tracks straight or drifts toward danger?
sec08-card-sec08-F21.teaching_text: Hard braking on a straight path can yank a broken tie-rod sideways, whereas heading toward people demands maximum stop.

sec08-card-sec08-F22.question_text: What four actions must you take—and which swerve must you avoid—when an oncoming car enters your lane?
sec08-card-sec08-F22.teaching_text: Never swerve left into their original lane because waking drivers instinctively snap back right into you.

sec08-card-sec08-F23.question_text: Which three driver factors fuel Nevada's deadly single-vehicle run-off-road crashes?
sec08-card-sec08-F23.teaching_text: Long open desert highways lull tired, distracted, or speeding drivers into high-speed rollovers off pavement edges.

sec08-card-sec08-F24.question_text: How do you safely recover after drifting onto an unpaved highway shoulder?
sec08-card-sec08-F24.teaching_text: Jerking back across a pavement lip flings the car sideways across oncoming lanes—regain control on the shoulder first.
sec08-card-sec08-F24.must_match_memory_hook: Lift gas, hold straight, ease back

visual_sync.text_span: Lift gas, hold straight, ease back

sec08-card-sec08-F25.question_text: What must you do immediately in a tire blowout before touching the brake pedal?
sec08-card-sec08-F25.teaching_text: Slamming brakes on a shredded tire yanks steering violently and triggers rollovers before speed drops.
sec08-card-sec08-F25.must_match_memory_hook: Grip firm, lift gas, skip brakes

visual_sync.text_span: Grip firm, lift gas, skip brakes

sec08-card-sec08-R12.question_text: How does early braking advice differ between a tire blowout and a shoulder drift?
sec08-card-sec08-R12.teaching_text: Both start by gripping firm and lifting off gas, yet blowouts forbid braking until controlled while drifts allow careful braking.

sec08-card-sec08-R13.question_text: Once a tire blowout is slowed and controlled, what three steps clear you from danger?
sec08-card-sec08-R13.teaching_text: Limping clear of live lanes with hazard flashers lit keeps fast traffic from rear-ending your flat.

sec08-card-sec08-R14.question_text: Where should a disabled vehicle sit, how do you warn approaching traffic, and what comes next?
sec08-card-sec08-R14.teaching_text: Getting every wheel clear with flashers or flares active minimizes highway exposure until a tow arrives.

sec08-card-sec08-R15.question_text: Why is dry Nevada terrain prone to flash floods, and what happens once a vehicle starts floating?
sec08-card-sec08-R15.teaching_text: Baked desert soil cannot soak up monsoon downpours, sweeping buoyant SUVs into fast channels that roll them.

sec08-card-sec08-F26.question_text: What share of flash-flood deaths involve vehicles, and how shallow a film of water can break control?
sec08-card-sec08-F26.teaching_text: Under one single inch of sheet water can hydroplane fast tires, fueling over half of all flood fatalities.

sec08-card-sec08-F27.question_text: How little water pushes a fast-moving car off the road, and what depth floats most vehicles?
sec08-card-sec08-F27.teaching_text: Moving water packs immense lateral force at six inches while sealed underbodies bob up by two feet.
sec08-card-sec08-F27.must_match_memory_hook: Six inches pushes, two feet floats

visual_sync.text_span: Six inches pushes, two feet floats

sec08-card-sec08-F28.question_text: Why must you turn around instead of driving across any flooded roadway?
sec08-card-sec08-F28.teaching_text: Brown floodwater conceals both true depth and whether rushing currents carved away the roadbed underneath.

sec08-card-sec08-F29.question_text: What must you do immediately if your vehicle stalls in rising floodwater and exiting is safe?
sec08-card-sec08-F29.teaching_text: Staying buckled inside a stalled car in rising runoff traps occupants once currents sweep it downstream.

sec08-card-sec08-F30.question_text: What is the only sure flood-safety rule, and how must you treat road-closed barricades?
sec08-card-sec08-F30.teaching_text: Crews place flood barricades over collapsed culverts and deep washes where bypassing cars vanish.

sec08-card-sec08-R16.question_text: Why do nighttime storms and desert washes demand extra flood caution?
sec08-card-sec08-R16.teaching_text: Unlit dips hide rushing creeks until your headlights dip in—move uphill away from channels immediately.

sec08-card-sec08-F31.question_text: What color marks work-zone signs, cones, and barrels, and what roadway conditions should you anticipate inside?
sec08-card-sec08-F31.teaching_text: Rough milled asphalt, pinched shoulders, and dead-stopped traffic queues appear suddenly behind orange barrels.

sec08-card-sec08-F32.question_text: What legal consequence hits a driver who moves barriers or signs to sneak onto a closed road?
sec08-card-sec08-F32.teaching_text: Shoving cones aside risks driving into open trenches or crews and triggers doubled work-zone penalties.

sec08-card-sec08-F33.question_text: What happens to speeding fines in Nevada work zones, and how do black-and-white speed signs differ from orange ones?
sec08-card-sec08-F33.teaching_text: Black-and-white plaques set enforceable legal maximums with doubled fines, while orange signs post advisory safe speeds.
sec08-card-sec08-F33.must_match_memory_hook: Fines double, white binds, orange advises

visual_sync.text_span: Fines double, white binds, orange advises

sec08-card-sec08-R17.question_text: Between a black-and-white speed sign and an orange speed sign in a work zone, which sets the legal limit?
sec08-card-sec08-R17.teaching_text: Exam questions test color authority directly—white carries statutory limit force while orange recommends safer speeds.

sec08-card-sec08-F34.question_text: Which four actions belong whenever orange work-zone signs appear ahead?
sec08-card-sec08-F34.teaching_text: Cooperative early zipper merges and flagger compliance keep crews safe inches from live traffic.
sec08-card-sec08-F34.must_match_memory_hook: Slow, scan crews, obey flaggers, merge

visual_sync.text_span: Slow, scan crews, obey flaggers, merge

sec08-card-sec08-R18.question_text: Why are nighttime work zones extra hazardous, and what often guides single-lane traffic through them?
sec08-card-sec08-R18.teaching_text: Glare from portable floodlights meets late-night fatigue where flaggers and pilot cars pace traffic.
sec08-card-sec08-R18.must_match_memory_hook: Low sight, drowsy drivers, pilot cars

visual_sync.text_span: Low sight, drowsy drivers, pilot cars

sec08-card-sec08-F35.question_text: Which stopped emergency, utility, or service vehicles trigger Nevada's slow-down-and-prepare-to-stop law?
sec08-card-sec08-F35.teaching_text: Nevada protects tow trucks, NDOT rigs, utility crews, and garbage trucks right alongside police and ambulances.

sec08-card-sec08-F36.question_text: Which lane must you choose when passing a protected stopped emergency or service vehicle if conditions allow?
sec08-card-sec08-F36.teaching_text: Putting an empty buffer lane between your mirror and roadside workers prevents fatal shoulder strikes.

sec08-card-sec08-F37.question_text: Which two additional roadside situations trigger Nevada's slow-down protection duty?
sec08-card-sec08-F37.teaching_text: Even an ordinary motorist changing a flat tire earns the same slow-down caution as steady blue patrol lights.

sec08-card-sec08-F38.question_text: May non-emergency drivers stop casually along a highway shoulder marked for emergency use?
sec08-card-sec08-F38.teaching_text: Checking texts or swapping snacks on an emergency shoulder invites high-speed rear-end crashes and tickets.

sec08-card-sec08-R19.question_text: Which seven emergency, incident, or transit vehicles may drive on signed paved highway shoulders in Nevada?
sec08-card-sec08-R19.teaching_text: Where posted signs authorize it, public transit buses, tow cars, coroners, and incident units join police, fire, and EMS.

sec08-card-sec08-R20.question_text: On what date did Nevada's authorized emergency shoulder-driving law take effect?
sec08-card-sec08-R20.teaching_text: Recent handbook updates love testing effective dates on brand-new Nevada traffic statutes.

sec09-card-sec09-R01.question_text: Roughly how many crashes happen each year between passenger cars and commercial vehicles?
sec09-card-sec09-R01.teaching_text: Knowing most of those two hundred thousand collisions are preventable proves smart spacing around big rigs saves lives.

sec09-card-sec09-F01.question_text: How do large commercial vehicles differ from passenger cars in handling, visibility, and stopping?
sec09-card-sec09-F01.teaching_text: Treating an eighty-thousand-pound rig like a nimble sedan sets up sideswipes and rear-end crashes.
sec09-card-sec09-F01.must_match_memory_hook: Less agile, bigger blinds, longer stops

visual_sync.text_span: Less agile, bigger blinds, longer stops

sec09-card-sec09-F02.question_text: Who triggers most car-versus-truck crashes, and who suffers the worst injuries?
sec09-card-sec09-F02.teaching_text: Massive weight differences mean passenger-car mistakes around heavy rigs hurt the people inside the smaller car.

sec09-card-sec09-F03.question_text: What is the no-zone surrounding a large commercial truck or bus?
sec09-card-sec09-F03.teaching_text: Front, rear, and both long side pockets swallow an entire car completely out of the trucker's view.

sec09-card-sec09-F04.question_text: Why is hanging in a truck's or bus's right-side no-zone doubly dangerous?
sec09-card-sec09-F04.teaching_text: The right blind zone stretches longest and puts your car directly inside wide right-turning trailer sweeps.

sec09-card-sec09-F05.question_text: What quick mirror check tells you whether a truck or bus driver can see your car alongside?
sec09-card-sec09-F05.teaching_text: Light travels both ways in flat and convex glass, so missing their face means you sit unseen.

sec09-card-sec09-F06.question_text: How much stopping time and distance do heavy trucks and buses need compared with cars?
sec09-card-sec09-F06.teaching_text: Cutting tightly ahead of a big rig and tapping brakes guarantees forty tons cannot halt in time.

sec09-card-sec09-F07.question_text: When is it safe to pull back into the lane ahead of a truck you just passed, and how must you hold speed?
sec09-card-sec09-F07.teaching_text: Waiting until the entire cab grill fills your center mirror preserves their front braking cushion.
sec09-card-sec09-F07.must_match_memory_hook: Whole cab in mirror; keep pace

visual_sync.text_span: Whole cab in mirror; keep pace

sec09-card-sec09-F08.question_text: Which three dangers make tailgating directly behind a truck or bus reckless?
sec09-card-sec09-F08.teaching_text: Tucked behind trailer doors, neither you nor the trucker can spot trouble until an underride crash hits.

sec09-card-sec09-R02.question_text: How does the front no-zone crash trap differ from the rear no-zone trap?
sec09-card-sec09-R02.teaching_text: Front danger comes from diving in and braking early, whereas rear danger blinds both drivers completely.

sec09-card-sec09-F09.question_text: Why must you never sneak behind a commercial truck while it is backing up?
sec09-card-sec09-F09.teaching_text: Solid fifty-three-foot cargo boxes have zero rear window, leaving anyone crossing behind completely invisible.

sec09-card-sec09-F10.question_text: Why do trucks sometimes swing left before turning right, and what must you never try beside the curb?
sec09-card-sec09-F10.teaching_text: Drivers mistake that opening setup swing for a lane change and get crushed against the corner curb.

sec09-card-sec09-F11.question_text: What legal rights and lane privileges do motorcyclists hold on Nevada roads?
sec09-card-sec09-F11.teaching_text: Riders shift left and right inside their lane to dodge oil slicks and potholes, needing every foot.

sec09-card-sec09-F12.question_text: When may two motorcycles or mopeds ride side by side in one lane, and how must they ride otherwise?
sec09-card-sec09-F12.teaching_text: Without both riders agreeing, staggered formation preserves maneuvering room if debris pops up ahead.

sec09-card-sec09-F13.question_text: Why do oncoming motorcycles fool car drivers waiting to turn left?
sec09-card-sec09-F13.teaching_text: A narrow single headlight tricks human depth perception into misjudging closing speed right before left turns.

sec09-card-sec09-F14.question_text: Why must you confirm what a motorcyclist is actually doing instead of trusting their turn signal?
sec09-card-sec09-F14.teaching_text: Most motorcycle switches do not self-cancel after turns, so pulling out on a stale blinker causes crashes.

sec09-card-sec09-R03.question_text: Which two rider or bike movements tip you off that a motorcyclist is about to turn or shift lanes?
sec09-card-sec09-R03.teaching_text: Spotting a helmet shoulder glance or slight lean warns you of lane moves before handlebars noticeably turn.

sec09-card-sec09-R04.question_text: Which two outside conditions can shove a motorcycle sideways inside or out of its lane?
sec09-card-sec09-R04.teaching_text: Heavy gusts and grooved asphalt push light two-wheelers laterally, proving why generous passing room matters.

sec09-card-sec09-F15.question_text: How should you adjust when coming up behind a motorcycle in traffic?
sec09-card-sec09-F15.teaching_text: Motorcycles downshift to slow swiftly without touching brake levers, catching close followers without red brake glow.

sec09-card-sec09-F16.question_text: Why is dimming high beams even more critical when approaching a motorcycle than a car?
sec09-card-sec09-F16.teaching_text: Blinding a rider who steers by visual horizon balance can drop the bike before they pass you.

sec09-card-sec09-F17.question_text: How should rain or slick pavement change your following distance behind a motorcycle?
sec09-card-sec09-F17.teaching_text: Painted stripes, wet leaves, and oily rain threaten two-wheel traction far worse than four-tire cars.

sec09-card-sec09-F18.question_text: What credential addition must appear on a Nevada license to ride a motorcycle legally?
sec09-card-sec09-F18.teaching_text: Standard passenger licenses alone do not cover two-wheel street motorcycles without passing endorsement requirements.

sec09-card-sec09-F19.question_text: What motor-power cap and flat-ground top speed define a moped under Nevada law?
sec09-card-sec09-F19.teaching_text: Anything exceeding two brake horsepower or thirty miles per hour steps up into full motorcycle rules.

sec09-card-sec09-F20.question_text: Which lane must moped riders use, and what four exceptions allow leaving it?
sec09-card-sec09-F20.teaching_text: Thirty-mile-per-hour top speed belongs far right unless one lane exists, turning left within quarter-mile, hazards, or police orders.

sec09-card-sec09-F21.question_text: What registration, insurance, and helmet rules govern mopeds in Nevada?
sec09-card-sec09-F21.teaching_text: Test questions love contrasting mopeds needing one-time registration and mandatory helmets while skipping liability insurance.

sec09-card-sec09-R05.question_text: How do Nevada motorcycles and mopeds contrast in licensing and lane placement?
sec09-card-sec09-R05.teaching_text: Full motorcycles carry highway speed with an endorsement, whereas low-power mopeds stick to far-right lanes.

sec09-card-sec09-R08.question_text: What degree of caution do drivers owe mopeds, and what duties apply to moped riders?
sec09-card-sec09-R08.teaching_text: Mopeds face identical visibility risks as motorcycles plus slower acceleration limits that demand extra rider care.
sec09-card-sec09-R08.must_match_memory_hook: Same motorcycle caution; extra rider duties

visual_sync.text_span: Same motorcycle caution; extra rider duties

sec09-card-sec09-F22.question_text: When must you stop for a school bus displaying flashing red lights, and when may you proceed?
sec09-card-sec09-F22.teaching_text: Rolling forward before the bus driver kills those flashing red lamps risks hitting children crossing late.
sec09-card-sec09-F22.must_match_memory_hook: Stop everywhere until lights turn off

visual_sync.text_span: Stop everywhere until lights turn off

sec09-card-sec09-F23.question_text: Who is required to stop for a flashing-red school bus on a divided highway?
sec09-card-sec09-F23.teaching_text: Physical median barriers separate opposing lanes so kids never cross oncoming divided highway traffic.

sec09-card-sec09-R06.question_text: How do school-bus stopping rules differ between an undivided road and a divided highway?
sec09-card-sec09-R06.teaching_text: Exam questions test whether a physical divider exists—without one, oncoming lanes must halt completely too.

sec09-card-sec09-R07.question_text: What happens under Nevada law when a school-bus driver reports a car passing illegally?
sec09-card-sec09-R07.teaching_text: Bus drivers forward illegal passers to the school district and state agency, triggering an official owner warning.

sec09-card-sec09-F29.question_text: Who is barred from riding in a pickup bed or flatbed on paved Nevada highways, and what two exceptions exist?
sec09-card-sec09-F29.teaching_text: Unrestrained open cargo beds eject minors violently in minor swerves outside authorized parades or farm work.

sec09-card-sec09-F24.question_text: What serious criminal traffic charge and license penalty can hit a driver who causes even a minor bicycle collision?
sec09-card-sec09-F24.teaching_text: Nevada treats careless motorist interference or minor bike contact harshly because unprotected riders suffer severe harm.

sec09-card-sec09-R11.question_text: Does Nevada's ban on deliberate interference apply only to car drivers or to bicyclists too?
sec09-card-sec09-R11.teaching_text: Safe road sharing works both ways—neither motorists nor cyclists may intentionally harass or obstruct traffic.

sec09-card-sec09-F25.question_text: Where inside a travel lane do cyclists ride, and when may they move away from that edge?
sec09-card-sec09-F25.teaching_text: Expect cyclists to merge smoothly toward center or left lanes before left turns or overtaking slower obstacles.

sec09-card-sec09-R09.question_text: How must cyclists handle traffic lights and signs, and how should they use a pedestrian crosswalk?
sec09-card-sec09-R09.teaching_text: Stepping off to walk across crosswalks turns fast-rolling bikes into predictable pedestrian speeds for turning cars.

sec09-card-sec09-R10.question_text: How often must a cyclist signal a turn, when may they skip it, and how may right turns be shown?
sec09-card-sec09-R10.teaching_text: Pointing straight right is intuitive, and keeping both hands on handlebars for rough braking overrides continuous waving.

sec09-card-sec09-F26.question_text: How must drivers treat approaching bicyclists when yielding right-of-way at intersections?
sec09-card-sec09-F26.teaching_text: Turning left across an oncoming cyclist's path violates right-of-way identically to cutting off a sedan.

sec09-card-sec09-F27.question_text: May you drive, stop, or park in a marked bike lane—and what four narrow exceptions exist?
sec09-card-sec09-F27.teaching_text: Parked cars in bike lanes force cyclists suddenly out into fast motor traffic unless legal exceptions apply.

sec09-card-sec09-F28.question_text: What passing-and-turning mistake must you never make near a cyclist, and when else must you check?
sec09-card-sec09-F28.teaching_text: Overtaking a rider only to hook right across their front tire—or flinging a parked door—causes classic crashes.

sec09-card-sec09-R12.question_text: Why do kids on bicycles need extra caution, and what scan belongs before turning into driveways or corners?
sec09-card-sec09-R12.teaching_text: Young riders often ride sidewalk contraflow against traffic, appearing from the unexpected right side across driveways.

sec09-card-sec09-R13.question_text: What gear and rules should cyclists follow, and which three risky habits should they avoid?
sec09-card-sec09-R13.teaching_text: Riding with traffic flow, wearing bright gear, keeping ears uncovered, and running night lamps saves rider lives.

sec09-card-sec09-F30.question_text: What legal duty do drivers owe pedestrians, and what charge can follow any pedestrian collision?
sec09-card-sec09-F30.teaching_text: Even a low-speed crosswalk bump exposes an inattentive Nevada driver to a reckless-driving prosecution.

sec09-card-sec09-F31.question_text: When is it illegal to swing around and pass another car that is slowing or stopped ahead?
sec09-card-sec09-F31.teaching_text: Whip-passing a stopped car in the next lane blindsides the pedestrian they politely stopped to let cross.

sec09-card-sec09-F32.question_text: Where do legal crosswalks exist even when zero white stripes are painted on the asphalt?
sec09-card-sec09-F32.teaching_text: Unmarked corners and three-way T intersections carry full legal pedestrian right-of-way without paint.

sec09-card-sec09-F33.question_text: Who holds the right-of-way when your traffic light turns green or when you turn right?
sec09-card-sec09-F33.teaching_text: A green bulb means go only after clearing walkers still finishing their crossing or stepping across your turn.

sec09-card-sec09-F34.question_text: For which pedestrians in a crosswalk must you slow, yield, or stop?
sec09-card-sec09-F34.teaching_text: Nevada protects walkers on your side, on the half you turn into, or striding close from the opposite half.

sec09-card-sec09-R15.question_text: How far across must a pedestrian get before a yielding driver may roll forward?
sec09-card-sec09-R15.teaching_text: Accelerating right behind a walker's heels leaves zero margin if they drop something or step back.

sec09-card-sec09-R14.question_text: Where should pedestrians walk when a road has a sidewalk versus when none exists?
sec09-card-sec09-R14.teaching_text: Walking along the left shoulder facing traffic lets pedestrians spot and step clear of drifting cars.

sec09-card-sec09-R16.question_text: Around which five everyday community spots must drivers stay extra alert for pedestrians and kids?
sec09-card-sec09-R16.teaching_text: Rushing commuters dart for buses and excited schoolchildren bolt across curbs around every one of those hubs.

sec09-card-sec09-R17.question_text: Which crossing, signal, eye-contact, and night-gear habits protect pedestrians?
sec09-card-sec09-R17.teaching_text: Holding back on flashing warnings, scanning left-right-left, locking eyes with drivers, and carrying light prevents hits.

sec09-card-sec09-F35.question_text: Within what distance of a crosswalk should you stop for a blind pedestrian, and why?
sec09-card-sec09-F35.teaching_text: Stopping way back hides your quiet engine idle, whereas halting within five feet locates the crosswalk edge clearly.

sec09-card-sec09-F36.question_text: How long should you wait for a blind pedestrian to decide, and what cane gesture means go?
sec09-card-sec09-F36.teaching_text: Giving three to four calm seconds lets them orient, and stepping back with cane tucked yields clearly.

sec09-card-sec09-R18.question_text: Which four actions must you never take around a blind or visually impaired pedestrian?
sec09-card-sec09-R18.teaching_text: Shouting directions or honking masks traffic orientation cues, while blocking sidewalks or crosswalks traps cane travel.

sec09-card-sec09-R19.question_text: Why do hybrid and electric vehicles require heightened vigilance around blind pedestrians at crosswalks?
sec09-card-sec09-R19.teaching_text: Without engine rumble to announce your car, visually impaired walkers may step out thinking the street is empty.

sec10-card-sec10-F01.question_text: What maximum weight rating and total length may a non-commercial Nevada Class C driver tow?
sec10-card-sec10-F01.teaching_text: Exceeding ten thousand pounds rating or seventy total feet steps beyond a standard Class C license.

sec10-card-sec10-F02.question_text: Which official Nevada handbook covers deeper towing rules and the J endorsement?
sec10-card-sec10-F02.teaching_text: Checking the state licensing agency's dedicated Non-Commercial A, B, and J guide preps heavier recreational haulers.

sec10-card-sec10-F05.question_text: How does gross vehicle weight differ from gross combination weight?
sec10-card-sec10-F05.teaching_text: Vehicle weight totals one loaded unit alone, whereas combination weight adds tow rig, trailers, and cargo.

sec10-card-sec10-F06.question_text: What does gross combination weight rating measure?
sec10-card-sec10-F06.teaching_text: Engineers set that ceiling around frame, cooling, transmission, and brake limits for the entire hooked rig.

sec10-card-sec10-R01.question_text: How does actual gross combination weight differ from gross combination weight rating?
sec10-card-sec10-R01.teaching_text: Your scale ticket shows actual combined weight today, which must never top the manufacturer's rated ceiling.

sec10-card-sec10-R02.question_text: What does axle weight measure on a vehicle or trailer?
sec10-card-sec10-R02.teaching_text: Even if total rig weight stays legal, overloading one single axle can snap springs or blow tires.

sec10-card-sec10-F07.question_text: Where do you read a tire's safe weight cap, and which two towing parts also carry ratings?
sec10-card-sec10-F07.teaching_text: Your weakest rated link—whether tire sidewall, leaf springs, or hitch coupler—sets your real safe ceiling.

sec10-card-sec10-F03.question_text: How does improperly loaded or loose trailer cargo endanger both traffic and your trailer?
sec10-card-sec10-F03.teaching_text: Unstrapped items launch into windshields behind you or slam forward through trailer walls under hard braking.

sec10-card-sec10-F04.question_text: What four performance problems hit an overloaded towing rig on hills and stops?
sec10-card-sec10-F04.teaching_text: Excess weight bogs climbs, shoves rigs dangerously fast downhill, stretches stops, and cooks brakes to failure.

sec10-card-sec10-F08.question_text: How does load height affect rollover risk, and where must heavy items ride?
sec10-card-sec10-F08.teaching_text: Top-heavy cargo acts like a lever on curves, tipping trailers that would corner flat loaded low.

sec10-card-sec10-F09.question_text: What goes wrong with too much weight—versus too little weight—on the front steering axle?
sec10-card-sec10-F09.teaching_text: Crushing front weight strains tires and steering effort, while heavy tongue sag lifts front tires off pavement.

sec10-card-sec10-F10.question_text: What traction problem strikes when too little weight sits over the driving axles?
sec10-card-sec10-F10.teaching_text: Without downward load pressing powered wheels into wet pavement or boat ramps, tires spin helplessly.

sec10-card-sec10-F11.question_text: What danger comes from loading one side heavier than the other, and how do you prevent tipping?
sec10-card-sec10-F11.teaching_text: Lopsided weight leans suspension hard toward the heavy side, turning brisk highway ramps into rollovers.

sec10-card-sec10-R05.question_text: What extra cargo risks accompany flatbed trailers and foul-weather towing?
sec10-card-sec10-R05.teaching_text: Without enclosed walls to catch sliding freight, crosswinds and slick roads amplify every slight imbalance.
